We show the rest of the world that climate action and financial recovery go hand in hand. I am very pleased with the deal today and would like to say a big thank you to the parties behind the agreement, ”says Climate Minister Dan Jørgensen (S) in a press release.

In addition, initiatives are prioritized to ensure a transition to a market -driven expansion of solar cells and land winds. Among other things, the technology neutral tenders are continued in 2020 and 2021.

Investments in the catch of CO2 and Power-to-X
The parties agree to allocate what corresponds to DKK 800 million. DKK annually phased in from 2024 to a pool to target catch and storage of CO2. The pool results in reductions of DKK 0.9 million. ton. CO2 per years in 2030 and will support solutions that can capture CO2 from the example from the industry and then use it.

At the same time, a state pool is established to support the establishment of Power-to-X systems in a large scale of a total of 100 MW, which is more than five times as much capacity as the largest plant found in the world today.

Green change of industry
DKK 2.5 billion is allocated. DKK 2020-30 in the form of a grant pool for electrification and energy efficiency in the industry. At the same time, DKK 2.9 billion is allocated. until 2030 for biogas and other green gases needed especially in the industry where green power cannot be used.

Effective use of energy and renovations
Energy savings are required in the state buildings by 2030 and funds will be allocated to a targeted energy efficiency effort, where digital tools must support the energy renovation efforts.

The measures build on the green housing agreement, where DKK 30 billion is allocated. DKK from the Landsbyggefonden for renovations of public housing and the suspension of the construction ceiling for municipalities and regions in 2020 as well as the grant for green investments of DKK 1 billion. DKK in 2021.

Green heat
The agreement contains a relief of the taxes on green power for heating and increased charges on black heat. The tax lapses completely for both electricity -based surplus heat, e.g. Surplus heat from data centers and supermarkets, and when the surplus heat is certified or subject to a similar agreement scheme that ensures energy efficiency of the surplus heat supplier.

It has been agreed to provide support for phasing out oil and gas boilers as well as remove the consumer bonds for natural gas. The requirement that district heating systems must be able to produce both electricity and heat in some places, and at the same time, legal requirements for sustainability are introduced when using wood diomass.

Specifically, DKK 2.3 billion is allocated. DKK to replace oil and natural gas stoves with green heat. The heating package reduces greenhouse gas emissions by DKK 0.7 million. ton of CO2 in 2030.

Green transport
Remaining funds from the 'pool to green transport' are advanced and implemented until 2020 and 2021, and an additional DKK 50 million will be added. DKK for the green transition of transport. The funds are targeted, among other things. charging stations, but also heavy transport and ferries.

After the summer holidays 2020, the government will present a total sector action plan for transport, according to the fact of the fact of the climate agreement.

Green tax reform
The parties have agreed on a green tax reform with CO2 tax, but the details continue to endure. After the summer holidays, look at the green tax reform, which should make it more attractive to choose green solutions rather than blacks.

The entire agreement can be found here.

Title: Baggrund: Klimaaftale for energi og industri tager de første, nødvendige skridt
Full text:
New climate agreement does not deliver the large CO2 reductions, but gets "fixed" a wide range of formal obstacles for, for example, more district heating, and at the same time the long-term technology tracks are laid out

With a CO2 reduction of just 3.4 million. tonnes of CO2 in 2030 out of a recently recalculated MANKO of DKK 20 million. tonnes - the new climate agreement for energy and industry at first glance does not sound very ambitious. Not least because the 3.4 million Tons in reduction include the 0.7 million. tonnes of CO2 reduction that the waste agreement from the past contributed.

But if you look more closely at the content, the agreement will be cleaned up partly in a lot of inconveniences and formal obstacles to the green transition that has been bothered for many years; Partly the traces of the development and rollout of some of the important technologies-CCS, CCU and Power-to-X-must help provide green solutions to the sectors of the community that cannot just be electrified.

Outdated barriers removed
It is first and foremost in the area of ​​'green heat to the Danes' that a large number of outdated barriers are being cleaned up and the district heating has been struggling with.

It is about abolishing the so -called cogeneration requirement (that you have to produce electricity and heat together) that have counteracted heat pumps in the district heating; It is fuel bonding for natural gas and requirements that new district heating projects should be matched against the fossil alternatives in a socio -economic calculation.

The electric heating tax is lowered to promote the utilization of the surplus heat and then the agreement says that one will abolish consumer binding to natural gas.

For private consumers, it is about getting the replacement of oil and natural gas stoves with heat pumps, and this must be done through a combination of lowering the electric heating tax with cash supplements for the replacement- perhaps expanded with a special loan scheme for citizens with a lack of financing options, which The politicians agree to investigate the need for.

Surmølleloft is removed
For the industry, the agreement contains grants for energy efficiency and for the conversion of energy consumption from fossil fuels to electricity- especially in internal transport and in agricultural and manufacturing industries.

Finally, the agreement contains a new support regime for biogas and other green gases from 2024 in the form of pools for tenders that the projects must then compete for. In particular, the industry sees green gases as an alternative and green energy supply to the processes where fossils fuels cannot be replaced with electricity.

And then the future framework for expansion on land with wind and sun will be established in the extension of the energy agreement and after some disagreement, among other things, about a political ceiling for the number of landmills that the new climate agreement has now postponed to 2040.

At the same time, the agreement contains a new settlement model for VE -Strøm - which the industry has long called for - as well as various compensations for neighbors and municipalities that say yes to wind turbines in the neighborhood.

Energy Islands with 5 GW of offshore wind
The long-term technology tracks are first made up of the two much-talked about energy islands; One in the North Sea and one who is Bornholm itself.

The islands must be established by 2030 and have connected a total of 5 GW of offshore wind; Among other things, the third of the total of three agreed offshore wind farms from the Energy Agreement 2018.

The islands only contribute a very small CO2 reduction in 2030, but is considered an important step towards large-scale offshore wind power, which can both be exported and included as a supplier to hydrogen production and the green fuels that can be produced from there.

Prior to the agreement, the government has been criticized for delaying the offshore wind farms from the Energy Agreement 2018 because they had to be part of the Energy Islands. But in the new agreement, it is determined that park number two from the 2018 agreement will be accelerated and put into operation at Hesselø by 2027.

Tendering pool for CCS systems
As for the CCS and CCU technologies, the parties establish a technology-neutral market-based pool of DKK 202 million. DKK in 2024 - growing to DKK 814 million In 2029 and forward. The support must run for 20 years and the parties must decide the specific implementation of the background of the government.

CCS is estimated that CCS can contribute DKK 0.9 million. tonnes of CO2 reduction as early as 2030 and thus have apparently listened a whole part to the Climate Council, which just highlights CCS as the most economical way of reducing CO2 emissions rather than CCU; Where CO2 is utilized for the production of green fuels.

As far as power-to-X technology is concerned, the parties would like to establish a partnership with external actors on a grant scheme through state tender for PTX plants, which include: must help reduce production costs for green hydrogen.

Here, however, no amounts or frameworks have yet been implemented; This must be done in an agreement between the parties on the basis of a proposal from the government, but the parties note that an agreement has already been made with the Netherlands on the statistical transfer of road shares, which gives a proceeds of at least DKK 750 million. DKK, which will go to financing the grant scheme for PTX projects.

Lots of analyzes
In addition to the many specific proposals, the agreement also contains promises for the preparation of strategies and presentations that will form the basis for new initiatives.

For example, a total strategy for CO2 catch, storage and use (CCUS) and for PTX in Denmark must be prepared. The strategy must support the spread of the green solutions of the future.

The government must also present an electrification strategy with scenarios at the beginning of 2021, and then the parties have agreed that an analysis of the possibilities of phasing out oil and natural gas in household heating must be prepared.

In order not to forget the very large elephant in the glass shop, namely a green tax reform that the government has agreed to take in the agreement after great pressure. Here it is stated that a green tax reform, through the general pricing of climatic gas emissions, must be "one of the main engines to reduce CO2E emissions in all parts of Danish society without citizens and companies paying more in taxes as a result of this reform."

The government must prepare the proposal for a green tax reform and convene negotiations on this in the fall of 2020.

The agreement's initiatives will cost $ 22.5 billion. kroner, which is prioritized by the year 2030. The DKK 3.1 billion DKK is financed via reserves and just under DKK 6.0 billion. DKK financed via other pools, re -priorities, etc., while the rest - DKK 13.4 billion. DKK - handled in the overall organization of financial and expenditure policy.

Good pre-exercise
The new agreement has of course been criticized; From the green organizations for not being ambitious enough and from the trade associations to lack this and hint and not to provide certainty and thus enough security for the time and for the investors in the green technologies.

But here it is worth reminiscent that the current climate agreement is only number two in the series of the sector action plans that, according to the Climate Act, must show how we will reach our 70 percent climate target by 2030.

It is also worth remembering that, according to the latest basic projection, collective supply and heating accounts for only 5 percent of our total CO2 emissions by 2030, while business and industry account for 20 per cent.

That is, the politicians still have the benefit of going into the meat of the sectors with the very large emissions in 2030, namely transport and agriculture, forests and other land use, which totaled 69 per cent. of the projected discharge in 2030.

The climate agreement for energy and industry will certainly be seen by some observers as an exercise prior to the very large swords of agriculture, transport and forests.

Title: Banebrydende havbaseret elnet går i prøvedrift tirsdag
Full text:
The project is only expected in commercial operation sometime in December. But the system will form a school for net connection of the energy islands of the future.

When two energy ministers and an EU Commissioner on Tuesday inaugurate a new and groundbreaking sea -based electricity grid, "Kriegers Flak Combined Grid Solution" (CGS), the net is not yet officially put into commercial operation; It only happens in mid -December.

Instead, two months of sample operation of the electricity grid starts, which has a transfer capacity of 400 MW.

Here, Energinet and their German partner, 50 Hertz, must test the feature that is the innovative throughout the project: that the connecting cables between one Danish and two German offshore wind farms can be used to transport electricity between the countries when it is not blowing.

A system that will form a school for net connection of the energy islands that the government and its agreement parties have decided to work for.

"We need to test a system that - on the basis of wind forecasts - must be able to predict what transport capacity between the countries we can offer in the electricity market," says project manager Per Obbekjær from Energinet.

He expects ABB to transfer the converter system today or tomorrow to the project partners, and then the test starts, which you expect will take a few months.

Uses Contek Cable in the test
"Fortunately, we have another cable between Germany and Denmark, namely the contest cable, which is included in the test in the way that if, for example, we want to try to send a certain amount of effect from the inverter to the north, then we can similarly turn down The effect on the context cable, and in this way the market does not notice any difference, ”he explains.

The test must be performed in a collaboration between Energinet's control center in Skærbæk and 50 Hertz 'in Berlin.

Because Eastern Denmark and Germany each belong to its own synchronous councils that it is necessary to establish a double converter plant at an existing transformer station in Bentwisch near Rostock in Northern Germany.

One converter system changes the alternating current from the Nordic electricity system to DC. The second converter system changes the direct current back to AC, which is synchronized with the European electricity system. When exporting from Germany to Denmark, the opposite happens.

Back-to Back gave trouble
It is these so-called back-to-back systems that ABB has delivered and with which there have been technical challenges in the past.

But now, according to Per Obbekjær, these problems have been overcome and the plant is ready to be handed over.

Kriegers Flak offshore wind farm, which gets a total power of 600 MW, is connected to the Danish electricity grid with two pieces. 220 kilovolt cables, while the German park Baltic 2 is connected to the German electricity grid with 150 kilovolt cables.

The differences in voltage level mean that there is also a need to establish a 150/220 kilovolt transformer station at sea, which is built close to one of the two Danish offshore transformer station

Kriegers Flak Combined Grid Solution costs about DKK 2.25 billion. kroner, half of which is paid for by the EU.

Title: Lækkede dokumenter: EU sigter mod 2500 procent vækst i havmøller i 2050
Full text:
The European Commission is aiming for 300 GW offshore wind in 2050, which will require a whole new framework and investment of 789 billion euros, according to a leaked document.

"The Commission estimates that by 2050 an installed capacity of 300 GW of offshore wind (and about 60 GW Havenergi) will be needed in the integrated, greener and climate -neutral energy system by 2050."

This is stated in a leaked document on the EU Commission's strategy for offshore production of renewable energy, which the media Euractiv has published. Euractiv expects the European Commission to present the strategy on Thursday 19 November.

The leaked strategy shows that Europe has "unmatched technological, scientific and industrial experience" with strong capacity throughout the supply chain from manufacture to delivery and installation.

“Nevertheless, it's a very challenging horizon. This means that offshore renewable energy capacity must be 25 times higher by 2050. The necessary investments are estimated to be up to 789 billion euros, 'it says.

Not seen similarly
The total European offshore capacity is today at 23 GW, and about 3 GWs are installed a year. With the current policies and planned installations, it will only result in about 90 GW by 2050.

At that speed, an increase of 2500 percent by 2050 requires a number of 'legislative and practical obstacles' overcome, the document states.

"Going for 300 GW wind and 60 GW garden energy means a massive change of sector scale of less than 30 years at a speed that has not been seen similar to any previous energy technologies," it says.

The European Commission is therefore proposing a new EU strategy to reach 60 GW of offshore wind and 1-3 GW garden energy by 2030, which will pave the way to reach the target by 2050.

More hybrid projects
The European Commission proposes that Member States must cooperate on larger offshore wind turbine projects in the form of 'hybrid projects', but that EU law in this area today makes agreements between countries complicated.

The European Commission mentions the offshore wind farm 'Kriegers Flak' in the Baltic Sea connected to both Denmark and Germany as a hybrid project that is currently under a transitional arrangement due to lack of EU law.

"Innovative projects such as energy islands or 'hybrid projects' are facing special challenges and the current framework was not developed with such projects in mind,' it states.

The Commission therefore proposes a framework for the hybrid projects, which must be an 'intermediate step between national projects on a smaller scale and a fully integrated offshore energy system and network'.

China challenges
Today, a total of 5,047 European offshore wind turbines have a total capacity of 23 GW from across 12 countries included the UK leaving the EU in January.

The UK has Europe's largest offshore wind turbine capacity of 45 percent of the total capacity, followed by Germany with 34 percent and then Denmark by 8 percent.

Belgium and the Netherlands account for 7 and 5 percent of the total European offshore wind turbine capacity.

But even though Europe is the world's leader in offshore wind energy, this leadership is challenged by China and India, and "almost half of the global offshore wind investments in 2018 occurred in China," according to the leaked document from the European Commission.

Correction: Previously, the EU is aiming for an increase of 250 percent by 2050. That's a mistake. This is an increase of 2500 percent compared to today. So 25 times. Thank you to an attentive reader who made attention to the error. Correction: July 2, 2021: Earlier it said: "Today they generate 5,047 European offshore wind turbines a total of 23 GW a year from across 12 countries included the UK that left the EU in January." It is a mistake and is now corrected, Since it is the capacity and not production.

Title: World Economic Forum: Alle fly kan flyve på bæredygtige brændstoffer i 2030
Full text:
Kommunalt affald og restprodukter fra landbruget findes i rigelige mængder til, at der hvert år kan produceres 500 millioner ton bæredygtige flybrændstoffer. Danmark kan blive markedsleder.

I 2019 stod flyindustrien for omkring tre procent af de samlede menneskeskabte CO2-udledning. Men der findes materialer nok til, at der allerede i 2030 kan produceres bæredygtige flybrændstoffer til at opfylde hele den globale flyindustris behov.

Det melder The World Economic Forum (WEF) i forbindelse med rapporten ‘Clean Skies for Tomorrow: Sustainable Aviation Fuels as a Pathway to Net-Zero Aviation’.

Hybridelektriske- og brintfly kan også hjælpe flyindustrien med at nedbringe sin CO2-udledning, men det tager 10-20 år, før de udvikles og implementeres på større skala. Bæredygtige flybrændstoffer udgør derfor den mest lovende løsning på kort sigt, lyder det.

Materialer som kommunalt affald og restprodukter fra landbruget findes i rigelige mængder til, at der hvert år kan produceres 500 millioner ton bæredygtige flybrændstoffer, hvilket skønnes at være den samlede flyindustris behov i 2030.

Der findes dog en række barrierer, der skal overvindes, før produktionen af bæredygtige flybrændstoffer bliver attraktiv og nærmer sig prisen på de fossile brændstoffer.

Én procent af behovet i 2030
I 2019 blev der produceret mindre end 200.000 metriske ton bæredygtige flybrændstoffer. Produktionen udgjorde dermed en meget lille del af de kommercielle flyselskabers samlede forbrug på omkring 300.000 millioner ton brændstof.

Som det ser ud med de nuværende kapacitetsinvesteringer i bæredygtige flybrændstoffer, så kommer produktionen af til at ligge på fire millioner ton årligt i 2030, hvilket svarer til blot omkring én procent af behovet for flybrændstoffer i 2030.

Ifølge World Economic Forum kræver overgangen til bæredygtige flybrændstoffer først og fremmest, at produktionen opskaleres, at der udvikles nye teknologier, og at der indgås »betydelige samarbejder«. Det påpeges, at den største udfordring for dette bliver at udvikle de nødvendige kommercielle og finansieringsmæssige tiltag, incitamenter og reguleringer.

Klassisk catch-22
Lande med lave priser på vedvarende energi og let adgang til råmaterialer kan dog ifølge World Economic Forums afdelingschef for transportindustrien, Christoph Wolff, udnytte den aktuelle coronakrise til at blive førende producenter af de bæredygtige flybrændstoffer.

»De strukturelle ændringer, der sker i branchen, er en mulighed for at genopbygge og overgå til en lav-kulstof fremtid og imødekomme forbrugernes bæredygtighedskrav,« udtaler Christoph Wolff i en pressemeddelelse fra The World Economic Forum.

I dag koster bæredygtige flybrændstoffer omkring det dobbelte af konventionelle flybrændstoffer, men hvis produktionen opskaleres, kommer prisen til at falde, lyder det fra Daniel Riefer, der er luftfartsekspert i McKinsey & Company, der har været med til at udarbejde rapporten.

Han påpeger, at der her gælder det samme catch-22-problem, som man oplever i andre diskussioner om overgangen til vedvarende energiformer, hvor den utilstrækkelige produktion holder prisen pr. enhed oppe, og at de høje priser igen holder efterspørgslen nede.

»Nogle strukturelle løsninger kan føre vej ud ad den blindgyde - B2B-kontrakter, prioriterede luftfarts- og lufthavnsafgiftstrukturer og så videre. Det vil give brændstofproducenter den nødvendige støtte til at investere i produktionskapacitet,« siger Daniel Riefer.

Selvom prisen på bæredygtige flybrændstoffer falder, så vil de i 2030 fortsat være dyrere at producere end i fossile brændstoffer, men denne forskel kan udlignes ved stigende priser på kulstof, fremgår det af rapporten fra The World Economic Forum.

Danmark kan være markedsleder
Ifølge Luftfartens Klimapartnerskabs afrapportering til regeringen fra maj i år har Danmark en »oplagt mulighed for at være markedsleder i omstillingen«, og at »vi kan udvikle os til at blive producenter af bæredygtige brændstoffer, fremfor bare at være konsumenter«.

Klimapartnerskabet foreslår, at der etableres en klimafond til at stimulere udbud og efterspørgsel efter bæredygtige brændstoffer, og som skal finansiere hovedparten af meromkostningerne forbundet med denne grønne omstilling.»Ved at stimulere udbud og efterspørgsel efter bæredygtigt brændstof kan luftfarten således være trækkraft for grønne investeringer i Danmark, hvilket vil skabe flere arbejdspladser samt danne grundlag for balancering af el-systemet og effektive sektorkoblinger med landbruget, affalds- og plastsektoren o.l,« fremgår det af rapporten.

Kæmpeanlæg i Storkøbenhavn
I maj meldte et nyt partnerskab med Ørsted i spidsen ud, at de i i 2023 vil være klar med første del af et anlæg på 10 MW, som kan producere bæredygtige brændsler baseret på strøm fra vindmøller. Anlægget skal placeres i Storkøbenhavn og blandt andet forsynes med energi fra den kommende energiø ud for Bornholm.

Når anlægget er fuldt udbygget i 2030, vil der være brug for 1.300 MW el og produktionen af brændsler vil ligge på cirka 250.000 ton årligt. Dermed vil de kunne erstatte fossile brændsler til vej-, sø- og lufttransport og spare atomosfæren for 850.000 ton CO2 årligt, skrev Ørsted i en pressemeddelelse.


I 2019 stod flyindustrien for omkring tre procent af de samlede menneskeskabte CO2-udledning. Men der findes materialer nok til, at der allerede i 2030 kan produceres bæredygtige flybrændstoffer til at opfylde hele den globale flyindustris behov.

Som det ser ud med de nuværende kapacitetsinvesteringer i bæredygtige flybrændstoffer, så kommer produktionen af til at ligge på fire millioner ton årligt i 2030, hvilket svarer til blot omkring én procent af behovet for flybrændstoffer i 2030.

Læs også: Flystriber skader klimaet mere end flyenes CO2 – og det bliver kun værre

Ifølge World Economic Forum kræver overgangen til bæredygtige flybrændstoffer først og fremmest, at produktionen opskaleres, at der udvikles nye teknologier, og at der indgås »betydelige samarbejder«. Det påpeges, at den største udfordring for dette bliver at udvikle de nødvendige kommercielle og finansieringsmæssige tiltag, incitamenter og reguleringer.

Klassisk catch-22
Lande med lave priser på vedvarende energi og let adgang til råmaterialer kan dog ifølge World Economic Forums afdelingschef for transportindustrien, Christoph Wolff, udnytte den aktuelle coronakrise til at blive førende producenter af de bæredygtige flybrændstoffer.

Hvad skete der ved Crowdstrike-nedbruddet?
Webinar
Hvad skete der ved Crowdstrike-nedbruddet?
It-sikkerhed
»De strukturelle ændringer, der sker i branchen, er en mulighed for at genopbygge og overgå til en lav-kulstof fremtid og imødekomme forbrugernes bæredygtighedskrav,« udtaler Christoph Wolff i en pressemeddelelse fra The World Economic Forum.

I dag koster bæredygtige flybrændstoffer omkring det dobbelte af konventionelle flybrændstoffer, men hvis produktionen opskaleres, kommer prisen til at falde, lyder det fra Daniel Riefer, der er luftfartsekspert i McKinsey & Company, der har været med til at udarbejde rapporten.

Læs også: Kæmpeanlæg i Storkøbenhavn skal producere 250.000 ton flydende bæredygtige brændstoffer

Han påpeger, at der her gælder det samme catch-22-problem, som man oplever i andre diskussioner om overgangen til vedvarende energiformer, hvor den utilstrækkelige produktion holder prisen pr. enhed oppe, og at de høje priser igen holder efterspørgslen nede.

Artiklen fortsætter efter annoncen
»Nogle strukturelle løsninger kan føre vej ud ad den blindgyde - B2B-kontrakter, prioriterede luftfarts- og lufthavnsafgiftstrukturer og så videre. Det vil give brændstofproducenter den nødvendige støtte til at investere i produktionskapacitet,« siger Daniel Riefer.

Selvom prisen på bæredygtige flybrændstoffer falder, så vil de i 2030 fortsat være dyrere at producere end i fossile brændstoffer, men denne forskel kan udlignes ved stigende priser på kulstof, fremgår det af rapporten fra The World Economic Forum.

Danmark kan være markedsleder
Ifølge Luftfartens Klimapartnerskabs afrapportering til regeringen fra maj i år har Danmark en »oplagt mulighed for at være markedsleder i omstillingen«, og at »vi kan udvikle os til at blive producenter af bæredygtige brændstoffer, fremfor bare at være konsumenter«.

Klimapartnerskabet foreslår, at der etableres en klimafond til at stimulere udbud og efterspørgsel efter bæredygtige brændstoffer, og som skal finansiere hovedparten af meromkostningerne forbundet med denne grønne omstilling.

NIS2: Sådan implementerer du art. 21 om håndhævelse
Webinar
NIS2: Sådan implementerer du art. 21 om håndhævelse
NIS2
»Ved at stimulere udbud og efterspørgsel efter bæredygtigt brændstof kan luftfarten således være trækkraft for grønne investeringer i Danmark, hvilket vil skabe flere arbejdspladser samt danne grundlag for balancering af el-systemet og effektive sektorkoblinger med landbruget, affalds- og plastsektoren o.l,« fremgår det af rapporten.

Kæmpeanlæg i Storkøbenhavn
I maj meldte et nyt partnerskab med Ørsted i spidsen ud, at de i i 2023 vil være klar med første del af et anlæg på 10 MW, som kan producere bæredygtige brændsler baseret på strøm fra vindmøller. Anlægget skal placeres i Storkøbenhavn og blandt andet forsynes med energi fra den kommende energiø ud for Bornholm.

Læs også: Kæmpeanlæg i Storkøbenhavn skal producere 250.000 ton flydende bæredygtige brændstoffer

Når anlægget er fuldt udbygget i 2030, vil der være brug for 1.300 MW el og produktionen af brændsler vil ligge på cirka 250.000 ton årligt. Dermed vil de kunne erstatte fossile brændsler til vej-, sø- og lufttransport og spare atomosfæren for 850.000 ton CO2 årligt, skrev Ørsted i en pressemeddelelse.

Sådan optimerer du bygningers elforbrug
Sponseret briefing
Sådan optimerer du bygningers elforbrug
Elforsyning
»Vores vision om at producere bæredygtige brændstoffer i Storkøbenhavn vil give os den nødvendige opskalering til industriel skala, som skal til for at reducere omkostningerne til produktion af vedvarende brændstoffer så meget, at de kan konkurrere med fossile brændstoffer. Med de rette politiske rammer på plads vil dette projekt kunne være et afgørende skridt fremad for produktionen af bæredygtige brændstoffer i Danmark, hvilket vil styrke Danmarks globale førerposition inden for teknologier og forretningsmodeller, der kan sikre en bæredygtig fremtid,« lød det fra Henrik Poulsen, der er administrerende direktør i Ørsted.

Brændstof af gylle og madaffald
Forskere fra Syddansk Universitet konkluderer i rapporten En forundersøgelse af bæredygtigt flybrændstof fra maj 2019, at det allerede om få år er muligt at producere bæredygtige flybrændstoffer fra blandt andet gylle og madaffald.

Undersøgelsen viste, teknologien er på plads til, at metan kan omdannes til bæredygtige flydende brændstoffer til fly og anden tung trafik, og at det første anlæg til fremstilling af 100 procent grønt flybrændstof kan stå færdigt i 2025.

»Prisen på det grønne brændstof ser ud til at blive to til tre gange dyrere end det fossile brændstof. Men da brændstofudgiften kun udgør 25-30 procent af billetprisen, betyder det ikke, at billetprisen stiger lige så meget,« lød det fra førsteforfatter på rapporten om grønt flybrændstof, Anders Winther Mortensen fra SDU Livscykluscenter, i en pressemeddelelse.

Det danske anlæg skulle anvende gassen, der skabes i landets biogasanlæg, fra afgasning af gylle og madaffald. Denne biogas består af metan, der ledes ud i naturgasnettet og varmer huse op, men består også af CO2, der ryger direkte ud af skorstenen.

»Metan fra afgasset gylle og halm er ikke nok til at dække vores brændstofbehov. Men CO2’en fra biogassen kan komme til hjælp. Vi kan omdanne CO2 til metan ved at tilføre brint produceret fra vind- og solenergi,« lød det fra Anders Winther Mortensen.

Metangassen kan omdannes til flydende brændstoffer, som man kan hældes direkte i flytanken gennem en kemisk proces, der kaldes for Fischer-Tropsch. Det er en gammel teknologi, der blev opfundet i 1923 af de to tyske kemikere Franz Fischer og Hans Tropsch.

Teknikken har været anvendt af nationer, som har været ramt af olieembargo. Metoden blev blandt andet brugt under Anden Verdenskrig af tyskerne og under Apartheid-regimet i Sydafrika.

Title: Ordførere: Minister skal afklare skæbne for strandet havvindpark ved Bornholm
Full text:
The politicians have decided that the offshore wind turbines for Energiø Bornholm should stand 20 km from the coast. Thus, there is no danger of a local 100 MW project getting in the way.

On Monday, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply announced a new political agreement on the location of the offshore wind turbines for the two upcoming energy islands in Danish waters.

While the project in the North Sea is only so far outlined with a so-called gross area, the plans for the energy island in the Baltic Sea-which physically become the island of Bornholm itself-now become completely solid.

According to the agreement, the mills at Bornholm will be placed 20 km south of the coast at Rønne. Thus, the mills in the large state project will definitely not come into carambola with another, local coastal coastal offshore wind project, which has set a location between 8 and 10 km from the coast and which is currently stranded because of the plans for the energy island.

“We have been met with the argument in the past that there could be an area conflict between the mills. With this announcement, it is now clearly clear that it is not there. So now it must be right to the right leg for Dan Jørgensen to cancel the coastal reservations, ”says Helle Munk Ravnborg initiative group for the initiative group for Bornholm's offshore wind farm, Helle Munk Ravnborg.

As previously mentioned here at Gridtech, a citizen -anchored project on Bornholm is merging with up to 100 MW coastal offshore wind south of the coast at Rønne.

The project has great local support from, among others, the municipal council in Bornholm Regional Municipality and the local utility company as well as local business. External consultants have calculated that the project will be able to deliver a competitive KWH award, and in addition, the 100 MW extra offshore wind will help the island tremendously closer to becoming completely self-sufficient with electricity.

But the desired location of the project hits an old state area reservation, and therefore the Bornholmers cannot apply to the Danish Energy Agency for permission to conduct preliminary investigations via the so-called open-door scheme.

Requires solution for all of Denmark's sea area
The reservation was made in 2015 in connection with a supply of coastal offshore wind and since then maintained by the then Minister of Energy Lars Christian Lilleholt (V) for the use of future tenders.

But there are no indications that the sitting government wants to print a coastal supply. Thus, a number of obvious offshore wind areas are currently blocked by, among others, Sejerø Bay, the Smålands waters, Sæby and thus at Bornholm.
The Ministry has previously rejected the Citizens' Initiative to raise its land reservation, among other things, on the grounds that no special treatment can be given to the area at Bornholm, and that a solution would have to be found that provides equal conditions for the entire Danish sea area.

Helle Munk Ravnborg therefore hopes that Dan Jørgensen will now, together with the Danish Energy Agency, investigate what conditions it can be possible to abolish all the coastal reservations. The Citizens' Initiative has even pointed out that, for example, it may be a requirement for the withdrawals that the projects have sufficient local support.

Rapporteurs will have answers from minister
Also, the Folketing's energy mayors are prepared to put pressure on the minister to facilitate the blocked areas so that citizen-driven WE extension can gain a foothold at sea.

“We think that when there is a project with a significant local support-which is exactly one of the things we need in the green transition-of course we should not stand in the way-especially when the Energy Island project now does not seem to be caramel with the local project, ”says Carsten Kissmeyer, who is the energy spokesman for the Left.

"We will have a conversation with the minister about the project and emphasize that there is very good logic in supporting local initiatives of this kind," he says.

Also the Unity List's energy mayor Søren Egge Rasmussen goes in to clear stones of the way for the local project:

“Obviously, if the large offshore wind farm had been placed close to Bornholm, then the popular project would have been squeezed. Now you are in a situation where there should be an opportunity for the popular project to move on. If there is still an outstanding with an area reservation, then one must be able to find a solution to it, ”he says and continues:

"I have repeatedly taken it up at meetings with Dan Jørgensen that I consider the answer he has given the Bornholmers as a preliminary answer. It is, after all, now that the question of area overlap is laid behind us. Then at upcoming meetings I will follow up and get the minister to relate to how he will give the Bornholmers properly. "

In relation to the argument that the coastal offshore wind project risks undermining the economy of the energy island by increasing the supply of electricity to Bornholm, he points out that most of the power would, as a starting point, be sent to Zealand.

"If you want to take advantage of the power from wind turbines to something serious compared to Power-to-X, it will be of a size where the excess heat from the processes has to be near a large heating area, such as the capital," he says and continues:

"That's why I don't see the two projects colliding on that front at all."

Carsten Kissmeyer agrees that the economy of the 20 times larger Energy Island project can hardly be threatened by the 100 MW park:

"We don't believe that is right, because the project at Bornholm is not that big," he says.

Title: Så går vi i gang: Forundersøgelser til energi-øer for 1,1 mia kroner
Full text:
Seabed, sea view, Unscrowled bombs. It is the biggest feasibility study that Energinet has ever performed.


At the request of Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen (A), Energinet is now embarking on preliminary investigations for the two energy islands- one in the North Sea and one at Bornholm- which the politicians in this summer's climate agreement agreed to have built by 2030.

Specifically, Energinet must prepare feasibility studies on the sea for an energy island in the North Sea, which will consist of an artificial island construction, to which 3 GW offshore winds are attached.

When it comes to Bornholm, Energinet must not only prepare, but start preliminary studies at sea for the 2 GW offshore winds that will be in the Baltic Sea west of Bornholm, which the offshore wind farms must be connected.

North Sea location comes later
The difference lies in the fact that politicians have recently designated a specific area for the offshore wind turbines west of Bornholm, while in the North Sea has simply designated a gross area and promised before next spring to find the exact location, after which Energinet can start the feasibility studies in the North Sea. .

For Energinet, the preliminary investigation project for the Energy Islands becomes the largest project ever completed:

»This is a huge feasibility study project. Alone on the sea, Energinet must examine areas that together fill as much as approx. Three times Bornholm area. Wind farms, cables and facilities for the energy islands will cross a jumble of sailing routes, fishing areas, already planned offshore wind areas, mining areas from the world wars and much more, ”says Hanne Storm Edlefsen, Vice President and chief responsible for Energinet's work with the energy islands in a press release.

On land, Energinet will plan plants that will connect the energy islands to the energy system on land on Bornholm, Zealand and in the West Jutland municipalities.

Price: 1.1 billion kroner
According to Energinet, the feasibility studies will cost about DKK 230 million. DKK per GW Wind Power and thus the total cost of preliminary surveys of the two energy islands will amount to DKK 1.15 billion. kroner.

"But then everything is also included," says project manager for the preliminary investigations, Jens Larsen from Energinet.

Energinet's feasibility studies will, in general, consist of a strategic environmental assessment based on the plan for the two energy islands delivered by the Danish Energy Agency. A strategic environmental assessment includes assessment of the plan's environmental impact on the sea and on land, impact assessment for Natura 2000 areas and visibility analyzes whose offshore wind farms can be seen from land.

The feasibility study will also consist of geotechnical and geophysical studies of the seabed in connection with the energy islands, the offshore wind farms and cable connections, including foreign connections. For example, they should locate not exploded grenades on the seabed.

Must be finished in 2024
On land, Energinet must designate the point for connecting the electricity on land and the establishment of plants. Energinet will be responsible for the preparation of planning basis for technical facilities and engage in dialogue with relevant municipalities on land to reserve area for any future power-to-x or battery plants.

Energinet must also conduct supplementary studies of the marine environment in addition to the requirements set for the strategic environmental assessment. These studies include, among other things, birds, marine mammals as well as fish, fishing and sailing safety. Archeology on the seabed must also be involved, including not least the area in the North Sea, where the Jutland Battle took place in 1916.

Finally, Energinet must mature and develop foreign connections in collaboration with TSOs in the cooperative countries with which an agreement is made.

The feasibility studies must be completed by the first half of 2024, after which potential bidders can offer their offerings on the actual construction of the plants that the Energy Islands will consist of.

Title: Danmark i samarbejde med Tyskland og Holland om energiøer
Full text:
Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen has just signed declarations to cooperate on energy islands with ministers in Germany and the Netherlands, Energinet writes in a press release.

The declarations are an important step towards a fulfillment of the political desire for the energy islands to be associated with countries other than Denmark. The declarations also mark the beginning of Energinet's work in mature and develop foreign connections in collaboration with TSOs in the cooperative countries that are concluded.


- In Energinet, we are excited that Denmark has now signed statements with Germany and the Netherlands about energy islands, says Hanne Storm Eldlefsen, Vice President of Energinet and adds: 

- The two energy islands in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea can only be realized through strong international cooperation, so the declarations are a very important step towards the establishment of energy islands, which is a vital next step for offshore wind on a large scale and thus for green transition in Europe and world.

With the two statements, the countries are jointly dedicated to conducting a number of complicated studies on how energy islands and offshore winds can be expanded and not least how electrical foreign connections from the islands can connect the countries' energy systems with each other. The use of electricity from offshore wind to hydrogen and green fuels is also mentioned as a central topic.

The Energy and Climate Measurements of the European Union are mentioned in both statements as a background to the cooperation, including the goal of climate neutrality in 2050 and the European strategy for offshore offshore wind.

The statement with Germany also specifically notes the Danish political decision to establish an energy island in the North Sea and one in the Baltic Sea in 2030.

In the statement with the Netherlands, the responsibility for analyzes and studies is given explicitly to the Danish and Dutch TSOs, Tennet, Gasunie and Energinet. The work will be rooted in the International Consortium North Sea Wind Power Hub, where the three TSOs have since 2017 collaborated on the development of a realistic concept for artificial energy islands in the North Sea after the so-called 'hub-and-spoke concept'.

At the end of November, Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen gave energy to conduct preliminary investigations to the two energy islands in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea respectively.

The injunction from the Minister includes, among other things, that Energinet must mature and develop foreign connections in collaboration with TSOs in the cooperative countries with which a statement is made.

Title: Pris for anlæg af energiø i Nordsøen: 38 milliarder kroner
Full text:
The price only includes the construction of the island itself and the electrical engineering plants, but not the wind turbines or direct power cables to the mainland.

The construction of an energy island in the North Sea with 10 GW of offshore wind can only cost up to DKK 38 billion. This is stated in a parliamentary response from Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen (S).

The price includes noticing only the construction of the island itself and the electrical engineering plants (primarily large HVDC converter stations, ed.), Which must stand on it. In addition, all the other investments in the wind turbines themselves come, the electric sea cables from the associated offshore wind farms to the energy island as well as the expensive DC cables that will connect the island with the mainland.

The price estimate has been obtained by the Danish Energy Agency from its adviser COWI, who has also previously made finications and calculated lifetime costs on the gigantic construction project.

However, COWI's estimate depends a lot on what basic layout you choose to construct the energy island from. Currently, two models are being considered: a large artificial and coherent island built up of sand -filled concrete lowering boxes or a collection of independent steel platforms that raise the plants above sea level.

The latter solution is well known in the offshore industry, where welded steel grids that protrude above sea level-so-called 'jackets'-are the most widespread platform construction.

But according to COWI's figures, it is the lesser-tested lower box solution in offshore contexts that will be the cheapest if the island is to support offshore wind capacity totaling 10 GW.

According to Cowi, this solution will cost DKK 29 billion to build, and it even includes a service port, just as the more coherent construction will also make it possible to store equipment at sea while the construction of the associated offshore wind parks - something that actors according to Energinet have demanded as a necessary facility.

But the wind giant Ørsted has apparently also made his own calculations. On Thursday this week, outgoing chief executive Henrik Poulsen wrote a post in the Exchange (in which he pleaded for Denmark to choose the solution with steel platforms rather than the sink boxes, as according to the company's own calculations, it is by far the cheapest solution.

»In Ørsted we have analyzed the two models, and our calculations show that with a caisson island (lower boxes, ed.) It will be about 4 billion. more expensive to establish the first three GWs in the North Sea in relation to the platform solution. Extended to ten GW, the Caisson solution will still be significantly more expensive, ”the CEO wrote on Thursday in the Exchange.

In COWI's price estimate, both types of construction cost every DKK 12 billion if the island has only 3 GW of offshore winds connected, as is the plan in this first phase by 2030.

Thus, there is far from the transformation between the two sets of calculations, and the Danish Energy Agency also points out in the parliamentary response that the estimates are 'subject to considerable uncertainty, and that by using other prerequisites for future prices, other results can be achieved, as well as technology development. also will be able to influence the results in the long term. '

However, clarification of the question is formal right now in the hands of the state's electrical system manager, Energinet, who was recently required to embark on the extensive preliminary investigation around the energy islands in both the Baltic and the North Sea.

Here, the balance of the advantages and disadvantages of the different types of construction will also be included as part of the studies. The work will run until the summer of 2024 and will in itself cost up to DKK 1.15 billion.

Title: Ørsted advarer mod energiø: »Vi frygter, det her bliver havvindens IC4-sag«
Full text:
Ørsted warns politicians against a reclaimed energy island and instead suggests a solution with steel platforms. COWI has previously assessed that an artificial island is the cheapest solution of the two options.

Shortly before the politicians in Christiansborg start to discuss the supply of the world's first energy island, which will become the most expensive construction project in Danish history, the energy company Ørsted is now coming to a warning, Børsen writes.

Ørsted warns politicians against focusing on an untested solution in the form of a reclaimed artificial energy island in the North Sea and suggests instead to erect steel platforms where the energy from the planned offshore wind farms can be handled.

»An artificial island in this context is Risky Business. We simply fear that this will be the ocean wind's IC4 case. That would be the worst case, ”says Ulrik Stridbæk, head of energy economy in Ørsted, to the Exchange.

Ulrik Stridbæk points out that it is "a gigantic investment decision" and denies that the warning comes from a narrow self -interest, as the energy company can bid on offshore wind, whether politicians choose one or the other. He adds that the technology of Power-to-X today is so uncertain that the state risks investing billions in a solution that may later prove not to be profitable.

Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, which is part of a consortium that will bid on the energy island, wonder about the comparison with the IC4 scandal and believes that a solution with the steel platforms does not offer the same opportunities as an actual island.

Cowi: In -Drumed Energy Island cheaper than steel platforms
The solution with steel platforms is well known in the offshore industry, where weighed steel grids that protrude above the sea surface-so-called 'jackets'-is the most widely used platform construction.

Despite this, the engineering counseling company COWI shows that a large artificial island built up of sand -filled concrete lowering boxes will be cheaper than a collection of independent steel platforms that raise the plants above sea level if the island is to support offshore wind capacity of a total of 10 GW.

»A platform solution of 10 GW is estimated at $ 38 billion. This is based on known technology, including that the platforms are established as 1 GW platforms [...] A reclaimed island for 10 GW with associated port is estimated at DKK 29 billion. It is assumed here that the island is constructed by a periphery of sunken concrete elements with sand filling, and that the island at 3 GW will be 18 ha, while the island at 10 GW will be 46 ha, ”according to a parliamentary response from climate, energy - and Supply Minister Dan Jørgensen (S) from December 16.

In COWI's price estimate, both types of construction cost every DKK 12 billion if the island has only 3 GW of offshore winds connected, as is the plan in this first phase by 2030.

The price includes noticing only the construction of the island itself and the electrical engineering plants (primarily large HVDC converter stations, ed.), Which must stand on it.

In addition, all the other investments in the wind turbines themselves come, the electric sea cables from the associated offshore wind farms to the energy island as well as the expensive DC cables that will connect the island with the mainland.

Title: Ørsted uddyber kritik: Vores platformsløsning er 4 mia. billigere end en energi-ø
Full text:
The company fears that experiments with an energy island can provide too expensive and late wind power to Denmark's green transition.

The energy company Ørsted has now on several occasions been out warning against building a decided energy island for the first 3 GW wind power out in the North Sea, which the politicians have adopted in the climate agreement from last summer. The first time was through a debate in the Exchange just before Christmas, and now again Tuesday in the same newspaper.

According to Head of Energy Economics at Ørsted, Ulrik Stridbæk, it is not about Brødnid nor about rejecting fixed energy islands for all eternity, but about fearing a solution that becomes too expensive and uncertain about the short course:

»We are interested in the cheapest possible offshore wind that will be completed on time - ie 3 GW in 2030 - and with all the experience we ourselves and our partners have with wind power and platforms, we believe it is a much more expensive solution To centralize this on a solid energy island, ”he says.

So far, the debate on a fixed island versus steel platforms as a connection for large quantities of wind power in the North Sea has been pretty poor on figures.

58.6 billion For an energy island
A report in May from COWI mentioned a price of $ 58.6 billion. kroner for an offshore wind farm of 3 GW, connected to an energy island, while three individual offshore wind farms of 1 GW would cost a total of DKK 47.8 billion. kroner. So a cheaper solution with without the energy island.

But in a ministerial response from December that compares the cost of connecting to the two concepts in the North Sea, the connection itself costs - ie minus wind turbines - of 3 GW wind power 12 billion. kroner for a platform solution and DKK 12 billion. When connecting via an energy island.

If it is about being able to connect a total of 10 GW wind power, it costs $ 29 billion. DKK at an energy island and 38 billion crowns with platforms, the minister informed COWI as source.

2 GW platforms instead
The calculations are based on transformer platforms in 1 GW-size, and here Ørsted points out that there are transformer platforms along the way with an effect of 2 GW that will be realistic to use until 2030 and which gives a completely different fact in the calculations:

»The Dutch TSO company Tennne has ordered six of these 2 GW transformers and base their extension with offshore wind on them. With 2 GW Transformer platforms, the price of connecting 3 GW wind power will thus be DKK 4 billion. kroner cheaper than the ministry's calculations. If it is about the connection of 10 GW, the price can be reduced by DKK 3 billion. kroner, ”points out Ulrik Stridbæk.

Stridbæk emphasizes that Ørsted is not an opponent of fixed energy islands, which can do some extra things compared to a platform, namely that they can accommodate a PTX plant or other kind of energy storage and facilities for the crew that can live on the island for an extended period of time.

"The decisive factor is whether these main differences can bear the extra costs and risks of a fixed energy island, and according to our assessments it is not-yet," he says.

Special -built ships house the installers
Around facilities for the crew, he explains - with reference to the company's experience with service and maintenance of offshore wind turbines - that today there are large, custom -built ships where installers and service technicians can live at the mill parks and for many days at a time. At the same time, these ships can be added directly at the individual wind turbines.

As for the other difference, space for power-to-x or energy storage system on the island, Ørsted does not think that we still know whether it will be profitable to produce hydrogen offshore at all, as electrolysis requires clean water and thus desalination systems and more Out at the facility:

“We do not believe that a platform solution for the first 3 GW will mean that we can never build a fixed energy island later. We just mean that with all the uncertainties mentioned, it is overlooked to venture out to build a solid energy island now and that we risk that we will not reach the 3 GW in 2030, ”says Ulrik Stridbæk and adds that the first platforms can easily be placed so that they can later be connected to an energy island.

Offering Performance - Not Designed
Stridbæk will advise the politicians - instead of attaching to an energy island or a platform solution - to offer the desired performance, namely the connection of 3 GW wind power in the North Sea and 2 GW at Bornholm - and then let the bids decide if it will be an island or a platform solution.

“We say that we would like to be a leader in offshore wind and at PTX in Denmark, but it does not help an energy island to stay. Instead, let's use the energy to expand with offshore wind and get control of the PTX processes, so the island can come afterwards, ”says Ulrik Stivbæk.

Facing Ørsted is a consortium of the pension companies PFA, PensionDanmark, Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and share (formerly SEAS-NVE), which would like to build a fixed energy island, which they refer to the stock exchange as a new break because you are aiming to be aimed at Make large-scale energy storage and power-to-x out on the island itself.

Professor praises the debate
The consortium estimates that there will be great advantages in producing hydrogen offshore, but should it turn out not to be realized, the island can instead be used for energy storage and transmission, explains Michael Ertmann from CIP:

“The whole point is that it is known technology that has to make the island. But the innovative is what should be on top of the island, ”he tells the Exchange, pointing out that technical problems can also arise with the steel platforms Ørsted proposes to use.

Professor at DTU, Erik Damgaard Christensen, who is an expert in marine and coastal technology, calls it positive and healthy that various technical solutions associated with such a large investment are illuminated from several sides:

“With the Fehmarn connection, for example, we saw that it was only very late in the process that you got stuck on a tunnel rather than a bridge, and in this way you became far more confident that you chose the best solution. It may also apply to the choice of technology around the energy islands, ”he says.

According to the Exchange, the energy politicians will in the coming time discuss how and in what way of establishing energy islands in the North Sea and Bornholm respectively.

Title: Cowi fastholder: Tæt løb på prisen mellem to typer energiøer
Full text:
Updated report from the government's adviser shows that an energy island that can receive 3 GW costs just under DKK 60 billion. DKK, whether designed as a platform or an artificial island. At 10 GW the difference grows.

The two politically adopted energy islands are to be designed as platforms or as a 'real' artificial island of lower boxes - this has not yet been decided, and therefore various actors, politicians and professionals have eagerly discussed this for a while.

In the Baltic Sea the case is ready, because it is Bornholm that must be Energiø, but this is not the case for the island in the North Sea, where you should be able to connect 3 GW offshore wind turbines in 2030 and be prepared for connecting at least 10 GW of offshore wind in a later Time.

Now the Danish Energy Agency's advisor in the field, COWI, has been published with a new report with updated figures for costs, climate impact and schedule for the two concepts. In the report, COWI finds that the price of connecting 3 GW of offshore winds to a lower box island and a platform island is just about 59 billion. DKK for both solutions - including offshore wind farms and electricity transmission.

When they look at the connection of 10 GW offshore wind farms, a lower box solution costs DKK 210 billion. DKK, while a platform solution is DKK 9.5 billion. more expensive - and thus costs almost DKK 220 billion. Kr.

The island is 5 per cent. of the price
To elucidate the difference between the two concepts, COWI has cleaned the figures for offshore wind turbines, HVDC stations and lake land cables, which go back for both solutions, and then the percentage difference between the lower box island and platform island becomes larger, especially on 10 GW The model.

For the 3 GW solution, the Lower Box Island costs between 15.1-16.4 billion. DKK, while a platform island costs DKK 15.8 billion. Kr.

If we go to the 10 GW Ø solution, COWI indicates that the Lower Box Island will be $ 9.5 billion. Cheaper than the central platform island.

According to COWI, the calculation shows that the offshore wind turbines make up about 50 per cent. of the price and the electrical systems about 45 per cent, which gives 5 per cent. of the CAPEX budget to the Lower Box Island. This makes Cowi conclude that the size of the island is less important.

Cowi's calculations have not directed the criticism from Ørsted, who would like to see calculations on transformer platforms of up to 2 GW, which can make the platform solution far cheaper.

Benefits of both concepts
In the report's conclusion, COWI summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of the various island alternatives as follows:

A fixed island with lower boxes has the following advantages:

• Indicative cheapest solution for 10 GW, however, the uncertainty should be reduced in additional studies.

• Possibility of protected port, service and maintenance facility

• Benefits of upscaling from 3 to 10 GW

• Possibility of extended functionality by PTX

• Connecting electrical systems on land -fixed connection

• More flexible interface between foundation and top page

Platform Lake demonstrates benefits when it comes to:

• Relatively mature technology in the desired dimensions

• Possibility of central/decentralized solution without significant impact on CAPEX.

• Better option for gradual implementation

• Less construction work for at sea for the platform odor itself

The electricity connection challenges
According to the report, several configurations of platform islands have been examined-both central and decentralized-and here a general challenge has been defined by the platforms, namely the electrical connection between the different platforms that are located close to each other with 200-300 meters away.

In this study, overhead lines have been proposed, which will, however, be challenged by salt coatings as well as general extreme conditions in the North Sea. An alternative is submarine cables, which will also present additional challenges in relation to cable crossings. Connection of the platforms in the platform lake should therefore be studied more closely, the report recommends.

Power-to-X costs extra
The report also looks at the possibility of establishing Power-to-X on the energy island to achieve savings at the transmission system. Here, the two most nearby PTX products will be ammonia or hydrogen.

Here, it concludes that the savings at the transmission system cannot cover the extra cost of DKK 10 billion. DKK, as the establishment of the area for the PTX system costs, but the report recommends supplementing with decided feasibility studies of offshore electrolysis. Among other things, water must be provided for the electrolysis, and you cannot utilize the excess heat from the electrolysis process out in the middle of the North Sea.

The report also goes into depth with a variety of ways to connect the islands and offshore wind turbines by the islands. Typically with 66 kV connection cables between the mills and the energy island (lower box island or platform island), where the power is transformed up to high voltage and converted from AC to HVCD, transmitted the long way into the respective countries' transmission systems, where they are again transformed into AC.

It is the idea that wind turbine power from the future energy islands should be able to be sent to Germany, the Netherlands and the UK - and then of course to Denmark.

Title: Tysk transmissonsselskab interesseret i energiø Bornholm
Full text:
German 50Hertz and Danske Energinet will already investigate this year whether it is possible and advantageous to build a cable between the two countries via Bornholm as upcoming Energiø.

The establishment of two energy islands in the Danish waters is closely related to the political agreement that cable connections are established from the islands to abroad.

And around the energy island in the Baltic Sea, ie Bornholm, Energinet and their German pendant, 50Hertz have now agreed that they will investigate during the current year whether it is possible and advantageous to build such a connection between Denmark and Germany via Bornholm.

Energinet even calls the agreement "the first breakthrough to connect the two Danish energy islands to other countries":

“If we are to succeed in the massive expansion of offshore wind, which is needed in the coming years to fulfill the climate agreement from Paris, it is crucial that a significant gear change is now being made from national expansion with a few wind farms to energy islands, which in its core are transnational projects, ”says Thomas Egebo CEO Thomas Egebo in a press release.

Overtakes Poland
In the reports made around the energy islands of COWI, it has been assumed that Bornholm should be connected to a cable to Poland, but now it seems that the German system-responsible companies are also interested in cooperation. But the two parties, 50Hertz and Energinet, have agreed that the cooperation can be expanded to other actors.

In the press release, Energinet calls the Energy Islands the largest infrastructure project in Danish history, because the political agreement says that the islands must be operational by 2030, and that there are less than ten years to the deadline for construction projects with large and complicated electricity transmission plants, island constructions or platforms on The sea, foreign connections and offshore wind farms in GW sizes.

According to the political agreement, 2 GW of offshore winds must be established in connection with the energy island, Bornholm, where the electricity from the parks must be picked up.

Considering a hybrid connection
Minister of Climate, Energy and Supply, Dan Jørgensen, in November 2020, informed Energinet to embark on preliminary investigations and preparation of foreign connections for the two energy islands, and in December 2020 Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands took up political statements on cooperation on energy islands and Development of offshore wind in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea.

Specifically, 50Hertz and Energinet have agreed to investigate a so -called hybrid foreign connection via Bornholm, which can both collect wind energy from offshore wind farms and send electricity both ways between the two countries' electricity grid.

They also agree to keep the cooperation open to potential other partners and that they will work to meet Danish, German and European climate and renewable energy goals.

Finally, they will build on the good experiences that the two partners already have with the development and realization of the innovative project Kriegers Flak Combined Grid Solution, which was taken into operation in 2020.

Title: Nu kommer energiøerne - men ikke til tiden: Pris 210 mia. kroner
Full text:
With a broad agreement, the Folketing has decided to establish an energy island in the North Sea. Up to 10GW on the way. Dansk Energi dissatisfied with new deadline.

No less than the largest construction project of Danish history has now been decided by the Folketing. An artificial island 80 km out in the North Sea must be a hub for up to 10 GW of offshore wind turbines, and as it gets the character of critical infrastructure, the state gets the majority ownership.

However, the island in the North Sea will not be ready for 2030 as it was otherwise announced in June in the Climate Agreement on Green Conversion of the Energy Sector and Industry:

"For Energiø Nordsøen, the agreement notes that it is considered difficult to realize the island before 2033 by virtue of the choice of ownership and construction of ownership and the type of construction and on the present basis.

In the first part of the construction phase, where 3 GW of offshore wind turbines will be erected in parallel, the island will have an area of ​​120,000 m2. Later, when the wind turbine capacity is expanded to 10 GW, there will be a need to expand the island's area to about 425,000 m2 or the equivalent of about 64 football fields.

Otherwise, there has been discussion, also here at ing.dk, about the advantages and disadvantages of a reclaimed island that has now been decided, compared to a solution consisting of steel platforms.

Ørsted has warned against the high price for a reclaimed island and instead recommended the solution with steel platforms. Conversely, COWI, the state's adviser in the field, has argued that a large artificial island built up of sand -filled concrete lowering boxes will cost the same as a solution with steel platforms when it comes to the first 3 GW offshore wind turbines.

But if up to 10 GW is to be expanded, the solution with an energy island will be about 10 billion. Cheaper.

Dansk Energi dissatisfied with new deadline
At the industry organization Dansk Energi, it is pleased that the political decisions have now been progressed around the energy island.

But CEO Lars Aagaard, is not entirely pleased that a deadline has now been set, which extends beyond 2030:

“It is not good enough and therefore both political and administrative forces should be constantly gathered to re -look the schedule. I appeal to the ministry reinventing the tendering process and engaging in dialogue with investors. After all, we need to use the green electricity from offshore wind to reach our climate target in 2030, ”says Lars Aagaard

Production of liquid fuels
In addition to acting as a hub for the production of wind turbine power from the surrounding offshore wind farms, the new energy island must be electrically connected to neighboring countries.

It is also expected that technology should be installed on the island to transform the green power into fuels for ships, aircraft and trucks.

In the first phase, 200 mills are expected to be set up, pointing to a mill size of 15 MW. In total, 650 wind turbines must be set up. The total investment is estimated at DKK 210 billion. kroner.

A political decision has been made to build an energy island of 2 gigawatts in the Baltic Sea. Here Bornholm will act as the energy island itself with offshore wind farms connected. The offshore wind farms will be located south and southwest of Bornholm.

The agreement on an energy island has been decided with votes from the government, the Left, the Danish People's Party, the Radical Left, the Socialist People's Party, the Unity List, the Conservative People's Party, the Liberal Alliance and the Alternative.

Title: Kameraer og kunstig intelligens redder sjældne fugle fra møllevinger
Full text:
Kunstig intelligens, der stopper vindmøller, hvis store rovfugle kommer for tæt på, har reduceret antallet af døde fugle med 82 procent. Men det løser ikke problemet, mener Dansk Ornitologisk Forening.

At vindmøller kan være farlige for fugle, især for de store ørne, er dokumenteret talrige gange. I Danmark er syv hav­ørne kommet af dage efter et møde med en vindmølle. I Norge har en enkelt vindmøllepark på 68 møller været skyld i 49 døde havørne over en syvårig periode.

Endnu værre står det til i Tyskland, hvor et studie i den nordøstlige del af landet har vist, at 137 havørne i perioden 2002-2017 er blevet dræbt i sammenstød med vindmøller.

Det lyder måske mærkeligt, at en stor og relativt intelligent rovfugl ikke kan undvige en vindmøllevinge. Men ørne er ikke naturligt bange for vindmøller, og man skal huske på, at tippen på en sådan vinge nemt kan bevæge sig med op til 200 km/t.

Derfor kan et system fra den amerikanske virksomhed Identi­Flight måske vise sig nyttigt, for systemet har gjort det muligt at reducere antallet af døde rovfugle med 82 procent i en vindmøllepark i den amerikanske stat Wyoming bestående af 66 General Electric 1,5 MW-vindmøller med en rotordiameter på 82,5 meter.

Undersøgelsen er gennemført af eksperter fra The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology og Forest and Rangeland Ecosystem Science Center. Resultaterne er offentliggjort i Journal of Applied Ecology.

AI genkender fugl
IdentiFlight-systemet består af en speciel type kameraer kaldet ‘Wide Field of View’ installeret på standere rundt om i parken. På hver stander sidder 8 kameraer og når et af dem får øje på noget, der bevæger sig hen mod vindmølleparken – for eksempel en fugl af en vis størrelse – rettes et stereokamera med høj opløsning mod den, og en analyseproces går i gang: Hvor stor er den? Hvilken farve samt vinge-, krops- og haleprofil har den?

Ved hjælp af et neuralt netværk er systemet herefter i stand til at identificere arten, flyveretningen, og hvor lang tid der går, før den eventuelt kommer i karambolage med vindmøllevingerne.

På nuværende tidspunkt er systemet i stand til at genkende rød og sort glente, kongeørn, hvidhovedet ørn, kilehaleørn, lille skrigeørn og kondor på en afstand af 1.000 meter.

Hvis en ørn er på vej i den forkerte retning, går der et signal videre, enten direkte til vindmøllernes eget kontrolsystem (Scada) eller til operatøren af vindmøllerne. Her kan der så træffes beslutninger om at sænke hastigheden på de vindmøller, som er tættest på fuglen, eller ligefrem stoppe dem helt.

For at finde ud af, hvor godt kamerasystemet fungerer, blev der gennemført et såkaldt BACI-studie (Before-After-Control-Impact), og sammenlignet med en vindmøllepark af cirka samme størrelse, som ligger godt 15 kilometer væk.

En gruppe af personer blev trænet i at gennemgå områder omkring vindmøller for døde rovfulge. For at sikre, at de gennemsøgte hele området systematisk og fandt så mange så muligt, blev der også lagt dummy-fugle ud som kontrol.

Derfor konkluderer folkene bag undersøgelsen, at teknologien har »potentialet til at mindske konflikten mellem vindenergi og beskyttelse af rovfugle«, også selvom en automatiseret kontrol af vindmøllerne ikke fuldstændigt eliminerede problemet.

Men de understreger også, at det er vigtigt at forholde sig til højrisiko­områder og eventuelle trækruter for fugle, før en vindmøllepark bliver sat op, og at et system som IdentiFlight helst kun skal bruges som et alternativ.

Fugle skræmmes væk
Biolog i Dansk Ornitologisk Forening Knud Flensted synes, at systemet fra IdentiFlight lyder som en interessant teknologisk udvikling, og han tror, at det vil kunne bruges i særlige tilfælde.


ai Stop vingerne – der kommer fugl

At vindmøller kan være farlige for fugle, især for de store ørne, er dokumenteret talrige gange. I Danmark er syv hav­ørne kommet af dage efter et møde med en vindmølle. I Norge har en enkelt vindmøllepark på 68 møller været skyld i 49 døde havørne over en syvårig periode.

Artiklen fortsætter efter annoncen

Endnu værre står det til i Tyskland, hvor et studie i den nordøstlige del af landet har vist, at 137 havørne i perioden 2002-2017 er blevet dræbt i sammenstød med vindmøller.

Det lyder måske mærkeligt, at en stor og relativt intelligent rovfugl ikke kan undvige en vindmøllevinge. Men ørne er ikke naturligt bange for vindmøller, og man skal huske på, at tippen på en sådan vinge nemt kan bevæge sig med op til 200 km/t.

Derfor kan et system fra den amerikanske virksomhed Identi­Flight måske vise sig nyttigt, for systemet har gjort det muligt at reducere antallet af døde rovfugle med 82 procent i en vindmøllepark i den amerikanske stat Wyoming bestående af 66 General Electric 1,5 MW-vindmøller med en rotordiameter på 82,5 meter.

Undersøgelsen er gennemført af eksperter fra The Peregrine Fund, Western EcoSystems Technology og Forest and Rangeland Ecosystem Science Center. Resultaterne er offentliggjort i Journal of Applied Ecology.
