The construction sum of 210 billion kroner at full expansion of the two islands equals five big belt bridges

It is in every way epoch -making when Denmark has established the world's first energy islands in Bornholm in 2030 in Balnholm in the Baltic Sea and 80 kilometers off Thorsminde in the North Sea.

The green power plants at the sea are empowering a new era of energy production and becomes a significant part of the green transition in Denmark and Europe.

Everything about the islands is already large: the construction sum of DKK 210 billion at full expansion of the two islands corresponds to five Great Belt Bridges; And for that amount you get 12 GW of green power, equivalent to DKK 12 million. Household power consumption.

It is not only the amount and energy production that blasts the scale of the energy islands. So does the innovation. The decision to establish the world's first energy islands is brave and visionary. If we succeed, it will ensure Denmark the absolute driver's jersey on the use and development of renewable energy for many years to come, and it can potentially become a new Danish green energy adventure of historical dimensions.

But it takes innovation to redeem the potential. Developing and designing an energy island is no trivial task. It has never happened before and requires us to think carefully to ensure the right solutions.

Right now there is a need for research, development and innovation in at least three essential areas:

First, we must ensure that the construction of the energy islands becomes robust. The islands must supply stable and reliable electricity to the electricity grid, but that is not enough. We need to develop solutions and advanced software models so that the systems are able to withstand extreme or rare events, including cyber attacks, which are increasingly belonging to today's disorder.

It requires new approaches so that the complexity of the energy islands does not lead to errors in the design or result in such large security margins that the cost of development and operation becomes far greater than necessary.

Exactly the financial attractive is the second area we need to keep in mind. We must already consider how we can, for example, develop new electrical components for the offshore wind turbines that must be included in the Energy Islands. The mills are not like the current coupled directly to our electricity grid and therefore do not have to live up to the same strict requirements. That exercise alone could save several billion kroner.

Similarly, we have to review the other elements of the energy islands such as. Transformers, HVDC connections and the possibility of any power-to-X system in order to be able to assess in each case how the solutions are screwed together most sensibly and economically attractive.

Finally, we must ensure that the developed solutions not only live up to the standards and technological opportunities we know today. We need to make sure that they are future -proofed so that they can act as the right basis when we get new knowledge and new opportunities in a few years and so that they can be expanded and linked to more future islands.

Effect electronics, intelligent digital control and the interior of the electricity market are undergoing a huge development in these years, and there is no doubt that we will soon have new advanced solutions that are much better living up to the demands that the energy islands make.

There are not many years for the energy islands to be finished. So it's just about getting started. In our eyes, it is right to the right leg to use the first of the Energi Islands, Bornholm, as a live testing laboratory for the new solutions to be developed.

Bornholm is interesting because the island is already there and we can get started quickly. In addition, Bornholm has the very big advantage that it is an island that we can easily get around and get around, just as it has all the social structures that make it easy to work there. Different, it must be expected to be with the upcoming energy island in the North Sea, which requires helicopter transport, clearing access permits and harsh working conditions on days of severe weather.

At Bornholm we have every opportunity to test different constellations and management methods in an environment that is flexible and used to act as living energy laboratory. Once the solutions are developed on Bornholm, it will be possible to subsequently copy them both to the energy island in the North Sea and to other future energy islands in Denmark and abroad.

Everything is clear, so let's get started. The first tests and arrangements can be done already now and ensure the pace and level of innovation needed to get the energy islands in place so that they can contribute to the urgent green transition.

"It is true that we see a growth in electricity consumption, and of course it is a challenge if consumption is inflexible or if actors in Europe choose to close power plants that can contribute to flexibility. But we must also accept that we are entering a new electricity system where we do not necessarily have to be able to hit our maximum electricity consumption with thermal power plants, ”she says, pointing out that Energinet has carried out several sensitivity analyzes - for example, on, for example, What the Energy Islands will mean for the effect situation depending on when they are built.

"In the future, we will also have to enter into closer cooperation with our neighboring countries and look at what it is for some technologies that can help reduce the peak load and which can deliver energy when the sun is not shining and the wind is not blowing," she says.

Remember the decentralized CHP plants
Researchers at Aalborg University have, in connection with the calculations behind IDA's climate response 2045, just looked at the security of supply and the impact deficiency, and while it is possible to build an electricity system based on huge amounts of solar cells and wind turbines and exchange between the countries, there will be situations where Traditional power plants are needed. Here Henrik Lund, a professor of energy planning at Aalborg University, points to two crucial factors:

“First, we need to have a number of biogas -fired power plants standing ready for those situations. They have to be cheap to install and the efficiency does not have to be fantastic, because they only have to run for a short time, ”he says, mentioning that the Danish proportion may as well stand on Danish soil.

The second point he highlights is the existing decentralized cogeneration plants where production today is linked to the associated district heating networks:

"Instead of closing them before their lifetime is reached, we believe that one should consider preserving them precisely in order to have effect available in these critical situations," he says.

By February 15, 2022, Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Dan Jørgens will finally determine the level of electricity supply security in 2031 and he expects to further present an analysis of “Climate Agreement for Energy and Industry 2020” effect on electricity supply security at the beginning of 2022.

Title: Nye tekniske løsninger kan gøre en energiø 20 milliarder kroner billigere
Full text:
Researchers have calculated that changing the technical requirements for wind turbines and grid connections can reduce the price of an energy island with the connection of 10 GW wind power by about 10 percent.

Energy settlement with established standards

There is no need to buy standard sea wind turbines when we start building wind farms in connection with the upcoming energy islands in a few years. Other and simpler types can do it, and the islands themselves can also become a melting digel of new energy solutions.

This is what energy researchers from DTU and AAU have calculated that the new solutions can make an energy island with 10 GW connected to wind power at least DKK 20 billion cheaper than if you simply use well -known solutions and standard components.

The new solutions are all about challenging some of the standards that Danish wind turbine manufacturers and grid companies have been working on for decades, explains Spyros Chatzivasileiadis, associate professor of DTU Electro and contributed to the calculations:

"Because the Energy Islands are likely to be connected to land with an HVDC connection (High-Voltage Direct Current, ed.), Then we can choose on the island itself which electrical standards we want to work with," he says, adding, That there have also been some more exotic technical ideas up and turning - we come back to them.

Not need grid codes
But if we start in the mills themselves, then in round numbers there is a saving of 3-5 percent and waiting. This is because grid -connected wind turbines are subject to strict requirements for fitting into the electricity grid - also called Grid Codes. Overall, this means that the mill must supply electrical energy, but must not be a load for the grid in terms of voltage, frequency and other unodes.

In practice, this means that the mill must be able to help the network, for example, to stabilize the voltage by being able to absorb or deliver reactive effect. It is possible with the converter technology that all new mills today have installed, which is used to convert the 'uneven' energy from the mill's generator to a pure 50 Hz AC:

"The energy islands thus make up their own network, and we can settle for smaller components, as they should not also be able to compensate for reactive effect," says Spyros Chatzivasileiadis, adding that an HVDC connection to country can also compensate for reactive effect.

All of this can also affect the transport of energy from the individual mills to the energy island itself. Today, a larger number of offshore wind turbines are connected with a transformer station, which then leads the energy ashore. The mills in the parks are expected to be 10-15 MW each, and it would therefore be appropriate to assemble them in groups of five mills with their own transformers, which are connected to the transformer that leads the energy all the way to the energy island:

“But when we still want to change how the wind turbines are connected to Enerigøen, we could at the same time increase the internal tension in the wind farm and send the energy directly to the large transformer. That way we would be able to save many less transformers, ”says Spyros Chatzivasileiadis.

This solution alone could save around DKK 12 billion. DKK on the bill for equipment for 10 GW offshore wind turbines.

But there are also more advanced electrical engineering options; For what if the developers completely drop the idea of ​​an alternating current network and instead goes directly to DC? In that case, each mill could settle for a much simpler converter and a direct current cable for a clutch station. From here, direct current could be sent to the energy island. The researchers have not counted on the savings here, but Spyros Chatzivasileiadis is convinced that it will be technically and financially possible.

Hydrogen in the mill
Once the energy has landed on the energy island, another opportunity arises that could potentially save money. It is about the production of hydrogen and possibly also ammonia. It is far cheaper to put a tube for transporting hydrogen into the seabed than to place an electric cable - in fact, the hydrogen can be brought ashore at half the price:

"Our calculations show that it will be 12 percent cheaper to produce hydrogen on the energy island than if it is to be done on the mainland," says Spyros Chatzivasileiadis, which also points to the nearby idea that the hydrogen can be produced directly in the mill and sent to the energy island In a tube parallel to the electric cable.

The type of mill is still at the experimental stage, but on a wind turbine from Siemens-Gamesa in Flø a little outside of Brande, a 0.4 MW hydrogen-producing system has been installed this year, which shows that the idea is already a reality .

It is also the advantage of hydrogen production directly in the mill that energy production can be controlled more efficiently as one unit rather than two independent. It will also make them cheaper in production and operation, as the mill and electrolysis production can share selected components and infrastructure.

Overall, the researchers estimate that for an energy island with 10 GW connected wind turbine capacity, DKK 7.5 billion will be connected. ke. To save on the wind turbines themselves, DKK 12 billion. DKK on transformers and on top of the possibility of more advanced solutions.

However, Spyros Chatzivasileiadis also emphasizes that the researchers' ideas and dreams can face competitive challenges in the mill producers:

“The market for wind turbines that are adapted to our new ideas does not exist today and we must therefore have some wind turbine manufacturers to make an offer. Therefore, there is a risk that there will be only a few providers and that competition will thus be severely limited, ”he says.

The energy islands are still in the planning phase, but the researchers at the Danish universities emphasize that it is now that the lines must be turned into the new technological solutions if they are to become clear and the savings become a reality.

Title: Overset bombe under regeringens grønne håb: Power-to-x kan fordoble erhvervslivets vandforbrug
Full text:
The demand for water for commercial use can be doubled by rolling out Denmark's large PTX ambitions. Professionals warn against using drinking water.

There is a water bomb under the government's large-scale plans for rolling out power-to-x technology that converts green electricity into fuels. It points out several professionals in the water sector, including Director of Lemvig Water and Climate, Lars Holmegaard.

"Based on preliminary inquiries from local PTX producers to Lemvig Vand, we estimate that the demand for water for business will increase more than 100 percent," says Lars Holmegaard.

In 2020, business spent a total of 728 million m3 of water, according to Statistics Denmark - that year consumption was even slightly less than usual due to much Corona home work. Business accounts for such large quantities and so large a proportion of water consumption that a doubling in areas with PTX plants can become a problem for supply.

"In light of the ambition scale that is in the PTX area, this is something that needs to be taken care of," states Lars Holmegaard.

Beat two flies with one bang with senior groundwater
Last week, the government launched its long-awaited PTX strategy, where the ambition is to build a national electrolysis capacity of between 4 and 6 GW by 2030.

Lars Holmegaard also points to something that can be an obvious solution, namely to 'make problem water into resource water', e.g. by applying senior groundwater.

"It is obvious to avoid picking up drinking water from deep magazines to PTX use and instead applying the senior groundwater, which becomes a bigger and bigger challenge," points out Lars Holmegaard.

Climate and Water Valley Denmark, which is set to become a commercial fire tower in Central Jutland in water technology, has just submitted a joint application to the Danish Business Authority, among other things. with a project proposal to utilize problem water rather than drinking water for PTX production.

Lars Holmegaard believes that technology and knowledge that make problem water into resource water can make a significant contribution to the government's vision of doubling the export of water technology.

The water should be cleaned to PTX quality
In the industry organization DANVA, Director Carl-Emil Larsen emphasizes that DANVA also stands with more questions than answers to the water aspect of PTX-and that Lemvig Water is not the only member who has reported that you have inquiries on delivery of about double so a lot of water like today.

“Much indicates that we are talking about exorbitant quantities, at least in the area where the plants should be located. And we do not yet know if e.g. Groundwater or wastewater can be cleaned to the quality required by PTX, ”points out Carl-Emil Larsen.

It is very clean water to be used for electrolysis - probably cleaner than drinking water. But exactly how clean and how it plays with the other cleaning technologies of the water sector is not yet known.

Even bigger problem on energy islands
DANVA also points out that, as one of the first things, one should think about putting the PTX plants where there can be water in excess-as it is not smart climate, environmental and traffic to transport water over great distances.

It becomes even more hassle and problematic if you hold on to the plans to place a slightly longer term to place PTX plants on energy islands in the North Sea. If salt water is to be cleaned to the required water quality, it will be very expensive and require very large amounts of energy - which can undermine the gain.

"It's ... exciting ... not to say a little strange that you seem to make such a great political decision without really investigating the essential water part," points out Carl-Emil Larsen.

Water challenge has been under -lit
Senior researcher Hans Sanderson from the Department of Environmental Sciences at Aarhus University agrees that this challenge at PTX has so far been underlined.

"There is no doubt that PTX we demand large volumes of water," he emphasizes:


“Where and how the water should be provided and then handled are certainly relevant technical questions. I do not immediately have any technically scientific analysis/solution of water the challenge - but can only find that it should be considered in the perspectives you are considering about PTX - along with the many other challenges that are upscaling PTX. Therefore, there is also a need for more research on a large scale of PTX in Denmark so we can develop the techniques. "

After the publication of the article, a clarifying sentence has been added in the 3rd paragraph to indicate that the supply problems can primarily come in the areas where the PTX plants are placed.

Title: Ekspert om Nordre Flint-pause: Bliver svært at skaffe og få økonomi i dværg-havvindmøller
Full text:
HOFOR has gone into thinking box after it has been found that the planned 220 meters high offshore wind turbine park in the Sound is too risky for the flight safety.

It will be difficult for the utility company HOFOR to get finances in the offshore wind turbine park Nordre Flint, even if it succeeds in obtaining as low mills as the project will need.

This is what Peter Hjuler Jensen, Deputy Institute Director at DTU Vindenergi, tells the Engineer, after TV2 Lorry yesterday could tell that the project, which should have culminated in 16-40 offshore wind turbines with an installed power of 160 MW, is paused.

The park should have supplied WE-Energi, corresponding to more than 160,000 household consumption in time for Copenhagen to achieve its goal of being the world's first CO2-neutral capital in 2025.

But the location east of Saltholm close to Copenhagen Airport has caused problems from the start, and now means that the project must either be canceled or delayed.

The cause is flight safety. If an aircraft loses engine power right after starting over the Sound, it must be able to return safely despite low altitude.

But according to a security assessment of the offshore wind farm from Naviair, to which TV2 Lorry has gained access to the file, it will reduce the aircraft's horizontal maneuver room by 40 percent compared to today with the 220 -meter -high wind turbines that are planned at Nordre Flint.

"We have to say that it will reduce flying safety, beyond what is reasonable," Copenhagen Airport's technical director, Christian Poulsen, told TV 2 Lorry.

Special -built wind turbines with poor economy
It is the Danish Energy Agency that will give the final permission for the construction of Nordre Flint. And it is, according to the media, that the Danish Transport Authority discourages a mill height of more than 155 meters.

It will make it very difficult to implement the project - both because Dwarf Sea Wind Mills are not exactly a shelf and because they will be very difficult to get finances in, says DTU's Peter Hjuler Jensen.

"I think it will be difficult to find some offshore wind turbines that are competitive in that size," he says.

He points out that offshore wind turbines have grown larger and larger over the years because the cost of setup does not increase proportionally to the size of the mill.

“If you double the mill size, the foundation may cost only 10-20 percent more. So the mills become more prize efficient, the bigger they become. You lie on the outskirts of the area where the offshore wind turbines are today, and therefore everything else will be more expensive, ”says the Deputy Institute Director at DTU Wind Energy.

One would have to set up more to reach the effect of 160 MW?

“You had to set up more and you had to make some special wind turbines for that site. For they are probably not in a commercial version that can be used immediately, ”says Peter Hjuler Jensen.

Many projects are affected by problems
According to HOFOR, the project cannot be moved because the location close to consumers is important. But if the mills are to be smaller, more may be set up in the same place so that the effect will be the same, says a written response to the engineer from Jesper Pedersen, head of Wind and Energy Trade.

“The economic aspect is difficult to predict at this time when we are still in dialogue about the final design of the project. But the less the wind turbines become, the poorer economy everything else equal. Our goal is that we, together with various actors, find a way forward, taking into account both air traffic, Denmark's green transition and the supply of green power to the Øresund region, ”he writes.

HOFOR is certainly not the only player who has trouble establishing offshore wind farms.

Intercut to be mentioned Hesselø offshore wind farm, where the bottom turns out to be too soft, Omø Syd, which is threatened by an upcoming Natura 2000 area, Lillebælt Syd, which has met great local resistance and Energiø Bornholm, which also risks being significantly reduced by one by one upcoming bird protection area.

In November, Mejls Flak had to be dropped out for Aarhus for reasons, which are very similar to the problems HOFOR faced with Nordre Flint.

The developer European Energy could not find profitable mills that could comply with the requirements of the permit for a total height of a maximum of 150 meters and a distance to the sea surface of 20 meters.

In addition to Nordre Flindt, HOFOR also has the project bylandshage in the mold - it has no similar problems. The offshore wind farm must be approximately 10 km from Amager's southern tip and is expected to have an effect of up to 250 MW.

Title: Nu sættes der strøm til samfundet: Elnettet skal lære nye tricks
Full text:
Elektrificeringen har fået momentum, og ­dermed er en omfattende forvandlingsproces af elnettet også gået i gang.

Der findes et ord på tysk, som kan få hårene til at rejse sig på alle, der arbejder med grøn elforsyning: Dunkelflaute.

Termen kan lidt groft oversættes til ‘mørk stilstand’ og beskriver således den værst tænkelige vejrsituation for et elsystem, der udelukkende baserer sig på produktion fra vindmøller og solceller – eksempelvis en iskold og vindstille decembernat.

Et sådant scenarie er særligt skræmmende, fordi samfundet – i takt med at flere vindmøller og solceller skubber kraftværkerne ud af drift – netop nu lægger mere og mere af sit energiforbrug om til el. Dét som vi i dag bare kalder elektrificering.

Elektrificeringen synes i 2021 at have haft et gennembrudsår. Aldrig nogensinde før har installatører erstattet gasfyr med varmepumper i et omfang som nu.
Salget af elbiler er stigende, og udrulningen af offent­lige ladestandere går så hurtigt, at elnettet har svært ved at følge med.

Al denne elektrificering er på vej til at skabe store omvæltninger i ‘verdens største maskine’, som nogle ynder at kalde det moderne elsystem.

Men er nettet klart til opgaven?

Hvordan skal et elsystem se ud, når alt fra smart­phones til containerskibe skal have energi fra vindmøller og solceller? Og kan vi forvente at have varme i stuerne, hvis juleaften 2050 bliver ramt af en regulær Dunkelflaute?

Hvor det hele begyndte
Det er svært at fastslå med større præcision, hvornår elektrificering af samfundet slog rod som den grønne omstillings omdrejningspunkt. I ingeniørkredse er ideen dog på ingen måde ny.

I 2009 udgav Energinet – den statsejede virksomhed med ansvar for det danske elsystem – en af sine første rapporter, hvor man for alvor havde regnet på en fremtid med rigtig mange elbiler og varmepumper.

Den var Anders Bavnhøj Hansen, chefingeniør ved Energinet Systemansvar, med til at udarbejde.

Han suppleres af kollegaen Carsten Vittrup, energi­strategisk rådgiver i Energinet Systemansvar, som påpeger, at udbygningen af vedvarende energi (VE) er så tæt forbundet med elektrificeringen, at det i praksis er blevet to sider af samme sag.

»Man kan sige, at energieffektiviteten i eksempelvis varmepumper længe har været så fordelagtig, at der har været et rationale i at elektrificere, selvom strømmen stadig blev produceret på kul. Men nu, hvor det er vind og sol, der troner billigst, og teknologien er blevet mere moden, så er det simpelthen ofte blevet en no-brainer,« siger han.

Begge peger på slut-nullerne som en afgørende periode, hvor tankerne om det fossilfrie – og dermed elektrificerede – samfund fik tag i det allerøverste politiske niveau herhjemme.

Dengang blev der fra flere sider regnet på, hvordan sådan en omstilling kunne se ud, og den såkaldte Klima­kommission blev nedsat for at komme med anbefalinger. I 2010 udgav den sin rapport, og en af hovedkonklusionerne lød, at el skulle være omdrejningspunktet for energisystemet i 2050.
Siden da har en udstrakt grad af elektrificering, primært drevet af vind og sol, stået centralt i det overordnede billede af fremtiden, som Energinet har arbejdet frem imod.

Power-to-x
Siden Klimakommissionens rapport er det gået stærkt med at udfase de fossile brændsler, hvis man ser isoleret på elsektoren. I dag er der blot tre kulfyrede kraftværker tilbage – alle med en endegyldig slutdato, hvor den seneste er sat ultimo 2028. Derefter vil den eneste fossile rest i det danske elsystem være gasdrevne spidslastværker. Dem vender vi lige tilbage til.

I samme periode har vind og sol for alvor holdt deres indtog. I 2010 dækkede de grønne strømkilder omkring 20 procent af Danmarks elforbrug, mens tallet sidste år var vokset til over 50 procent og frem mod 2030 ventes at nå op på 90 procent.

Men det er vel at mærke baseret på de politiske beslutninger om elektrificering, der hidtil er truffet. De høje VE-andele i elsystemet vil alt andet lige falde, i takt med at flere fabrikker og fjernvarmeværker piller kedlerne ned og i stedet sætter strøm til produktionen.

Derudover har den såkaldte indirekte elektrificering nu også meldt sin ankomst. Denne del af elektrificeringen omtales typisk som power-to-x (PtX), som dækker over kunsten at konvertere den grønne strøm til brændstoffer via elektrolyse og derved skubbe ­olien endegyldigt ud af energisystemet.

De seneste par år er PtX gået fra visioner og små demoanlæg til planer om at bygge konkrete, store anlæg. Frem mod 2030 har aktører i Danmark annonceret elektrolyseanlæg med en samlet kapacitet til at forbruge op mod 30 TWh strøm, svarende til mere end 85 procent af landets nuværende elforbrug på 35 TWh.

Det er med andre ord et voldsomt elforbrug, de systemansvarlige planlægger efter. Ifølge Klimakommissionen skal el dække 40-70 procent af Danmarks totale energiforbrug i 2050 for at opnå fossilfrihed. I Energi­styrelsens seneste energistatistik for 2020 var blot 19,3 procent af alt energiforbrug i Danmark elbaseret.

Anders Bavnhøj Hansen pointerer da også, at systemet skal have god tid til at forberede sig.

»2050 er jo langt ude i fremtiden, men det er vigtigt, at man gør sig klart, at der er en meget lang transi­tionsperiode op til så stor en omvæltning. Så hvis man vil nå målet i 2050, er man nødt til at være ret langt med ting som PtX allerede i 2030 eller 2035,« siger Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

Det er den transitionsperiode, han og Carsten Vittrup i disse år arbejder på at forberede elsystemet til. Og billedet er det samme over hele Europa, hvor EU’s nyligt opjusterede klimamål har sat elektrificeringen på hele kontinentets dagsorden.

I den forbindelse står Europas eltransmissionsoperatører meget overordnet over for to forbundne udfordringer, som den grønne omstilling bringer med sig: Styringen af elsystemet ændrer sig fundamentalt, samtidig med at behovet for transport af grøn strøm over store afstande vil eksplodere.

Jævnstrømsnettet kommer
Alle større elnet i verden kører på vekselstrøm og har således en frekvens, der skal vedligeholdes meget nidkært for at undgå, at systemet kollapser. I Europa – verdens største sammenhængende synkronområde for el – er den frekvens 50 Hz.

Stabiliteten af frekvensen har siden elsystemets undfangelse været sikret af de tunge, hurtigtroterende synkrongeneratorer, som ligger i maven på store kraftværker og reagerer øjeblikkeligt på små varia­tioner i frekvensen.

Afkobles et enkelt kraftværk eksempelvis på grund af et havari, mangler elsystemet energi i driftsøje­blikket. Denne energi frigives automatisk, ved at de tunge rotorer i generatorerne på andre kraftværker bremses. Den kinetiske energi frigives i stedet ud i nettet og afbøder effekttabet, hvilket betyder, at frekvensen holder sig tættere på 50 Hz.

Fordi hele Europa er ét stort synkron­område deler alle landenes elsystemer den samme inerti­reserve fra kraftværkerne. Men det vil ændre sig.

For vindmøller og solceller leverer ingen inerti til systemet, hvilket åbner for hurtigere og dybere frekvensfald, end systemoperatørerne hidtil har skullet forholde sig til.

»Når vi ikke har inertien fra den roterende masse i kraftværkernes store synkrone generatorer til at holde hånden under frekvensen i nettet, skal vi til at kigge på, hvordan vi i stedet vil tilvejebringe stabilitet i syste­met,« siger Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

Fremover skal særligt havvindparker agere Danmarks og for så vidt hele Europas bærende kraftværker. Størstedelen af disse parker vil med al sandsynlighed komme til at blive forbundet til Europas elsystem via en energiø, ligesom den kunstige ø, der er planer om at opføre i den danske del af Nordsøen.


Kablerne fra øerne vil være af typen HVDC – højspændingskabler med jævnstrøm. Vindmøllestrømmen vil altså flyde i land som jævnstrøm, hvorfor den skal konverteres til vekselstrøm ved ankomst på kontinentet i såkaldte konverterstationer.

Stationerne har den fordel, at de kan styre effekten digitalt og dermed overtage kraftværkernes opgave med at balancere frekvensen i vekselstrømsnettet. Det sker ved hjælp af lynhurtige algoritmer, som i dag er tæt bevogtede forretningshemmeligheder.

Så længe forbindelsen kun skal løbe mellem to endepunkter, er styringen af konverterstationerne mindre kompliceret. Sådanne kabler forbinder allerede Danmark til landene omkring os i stort omfang.

Men med de kommende energiøer skal jævnstrømmen udveksles mellem flere konverterstationer fra ­flere forskellige udbydere – et regulært ‘jævnstrømsnet’. Det forudsætter, at algoritmerne kan tale sammen, og det er en problematik, som man først nu er i gang med at finde ud af, hvordan man skal adressere.

»Energiøerne bliver en af de første store prøver på øvelsen med multiterminale HVDC-forbindelser. De bliver med stor sandsynlighed blandt de første rent konverterbaserede ‘synkronområder’ i verden, og det skal vi have til at spille gnidningsløst sammen med de eksisterende vekselstrømsystemer,« siger Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

Da Energinet ikke har den luksus at kunne bygge en demonstrationsudgave af energiøernes elnet, må man simulere sig frem. Men det er en ekstremt krævende opgave, man end ikke helt har forudsætningerne på plads for at løse endnu, forklarer Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

»Det er enormt tungt at simulere sådan et system. Du kan køre intensive beregninger på de dynamiske egenskaber over en hel nat, og så har du stadig kun simuleret få sekunder. Derudover skal de modeller, vi har nu, helt sikkert videreudvikles meget, før vi med sikkerhed kan sige, hvordan systemet vil opføre sig,« siger han.

Energiøen i Nordsøen skal i sin fulde udbygning fordele og integrere op mod 10 GW jævnstrøm i det europæiske vekselstrømssystem – en ikke ubetydelig mængde.

»Det skal være fuldstændig sikkert at slutte flere forskellige leverandører af HVDC-konverterstationer til hinanden – ellers vil vi ikke etablere det. For konsekvensen ved, at de ikke taler samme sprog, vil i yderste konsekvens kunne blive, at strømmen går i hele Europa,« siger Carsten Vittrup.

Et løsningsforslag kunne være at udvikle en branchestandard for styringsmekanismen i konverterstationer – sådan en proces tager dog år, og energiøernes premiere i årene omkring 2030 rykker hastigt nærmere.

Højspændingskabler er upopulære
Inde på land handler udfordringen også om at opti­mere udnyttelsen af det net, der allerede er bygget. I modsætning til de gamle kraftværkspladser, der blev anlagt i udkanten af store byer, tæt på mange elforbrugere, vil vindmøller og solceller typisk stå langt fra forbrugerne.

Dermed skal strømmen transporteres længere, hvilket de nævnte HVDC-kabler er rigtigt gode til. I modsætning til højspændingsledninger med vekselstrøm kan de tilmed let graves ned. Men det betyder ikke nødvendigvis, at Europa skal have HVDC-kabler på kryds og tværs.

»Tyskerne har været mere end ti år om at få etableret en HVDC-forbindelse, der løber fra nord til syd. Selvom den forbindelse er superkritisk og vil løse en stor flaske­halsproblematik ned til Centraleuropa, har det projekt været udskudt igen og igen på grund af modstand mod den her type infrastruktur,« siger Carsten Vittrup.

»Så det understreger jo vigtigheden af at øge udnyttelsen af det, der nu engang er etableret.«

Derfor har Energinet nu fokuseret ind på en stor omlægning af priserne for transport af el. Filosofien bag de kommende eltariffer er, at de bedre skal afspejle omkostningerne i et VE-baseret elsystem. Man skal i højere grad takseres efter, hvor meget kapacitet man ønsker at have til fuld rådighed, og præmieres, hvis man kan være en fleksibel eller ligefrem afbrydelig bruger af nettet.

Fleksibilitet kommer nemlig til at have stor værdi for systemoperatørerne, når de skal fragte mere energi i kablerne over længere afstande end tidligere.

»I takt med at vi gør mere elforbrug fleksibelt, bliver det også muligt at gå mere til grænsen i kablerne. Lidt forenklet sagt vil vi kunne fylde ledningerne mere op end tidligere, for skulle der falde noget ud et sted, så ved vi, at vi har store forbrugsklumper, der kan smides af, uden at det giver problemer for forbrugerne,« siger Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

»De nye tariffer vil medvirke en øget belægningsgrad af elnettet, så vi optimerer udnyttelsen af det elnet, vi allerede har, og dermed også gør elektrificeringen så billig som muligt,« supplerer Carsten Vittrup.

Små kraftværker bekæmper Dunkelflaute
Men uanset hvor fleksible elforbrugerne måtte blive, vil fremtidens elsystem stadig have en grundlæggende udfordring med at kompensere for en vejrafhængig elproduktion, når vinden ikke blæser, og solen ikke skinner.

»Tidligere analyser har vist, at man kan komme rigtig langt med at forbinde store geografiske områder med hinanden via HVDC-forbindelser. Men uanset hvor stort et område, du forbinder – om det så var hele Europa, der var forbundet på kryds og tværs – så vil du altid have nogle få timer, hvor elproduktionen er meget tæt på nul,« siger Anders Bavnhøj Hansen.

Man kommer med andre ord ikke uden om backup, hvis en flere dage lang Dunkelflaute sænker sig over Europa, hvilket er noget, man er optaget af i Forskningsgruppen for Energiplanlægning ved Aalborg Universitet.

Tidligere på året udgav forskerne i samarbejde med Ingeniørforeningen, IDA, et bud på, hvordan Danmarks energisystem kan indrettes, så vi bliver et CO2-neutralt samfund allerede i 2045. Én af rapportens væsent­ligste pointer var, at man snart bør adressere backup-problematikken.

»Indtil videre kan vi godt fortsætte med vores nuværende strategi – nemlig at trække kabler til andre lande – og så regne med, at der står nogle kraftværker i den anden ende af dem. Men den strategi er jo dum på den lange bane, hvis også England, Tyskland, Sverige og Norge nedlægger deres kraftværker,« siger Henrik Lund, professor i energiplanlægning ved Aalborg Universitet og én af hovedkræfterne bag IDAs Klimasvar 2045.

»Når vi er oppe på så store mængder VE i systemet, som vi er i 2045, så vil der opstå nogle perioder, hvor der ikke vil være nok strøm fra vind og sol – og det problem vil ikke kun opstå i Danmark, men i hele Europa. Det skal selvfølgelig løses i fællesskab, ved at vi hver især giver vores bidrag til en kapacitet, der kan træde til i de kritiske dage og timer,« siger han.

Derfor foreslår forskerne at bruge 16 milliarder kroner på at opføre ny decentral, gasfyret kraftværkskapacitet på i alt 1.400 MW i Danmark. Samtidig skal de små værker, vi allerede har stående, bevares, lyder det.

I disse år er værkerne hårdt økonomisk presset af de lave elpriser, som netop vind og sol forårsager.

Det kan virke kontraintuitivt, at vi skal udbygge kapa­citeten af gasfyrede kraftværker for at få elektrificeringen og den grønne omstilling til at gå op.

Men i 2045 regner forskerne fra Aalborg med, at CO2-neutral biogas udgør 100 procent af ledningsgassen i Danmark. Dermed vil disse værker – den sidste rest fra elsystemets fossile æra – altså kunne blive den grønne slutsten i det system, der skal gøre elektrificeringen mulig.

»Disse små værker vil få stor værdi for elsystemet i fremtiden. Vores pointe er, at vi på et eller andet tidspunkt bliver nødt til at tage stilling til det her, så vi har en eller anden form for kapacitet i fremtiden, når solen ikke skinner, og vinden ikke blæser,« siger Henrik Lund.

Title: Atlas viser hvordan lysforurening fra energiprojekter kan skade havmiljøet
Full text:
A mapping of light pollution in the world's garden shows the North Sea as exposed due to energy projects - both the persistent and the fossil.

A new atlas over light pollution in the world's garden shows the prevalence of human artificial lighting - it extends far into the water in our waters and strikes a vulnerable wildlife that can be adversely affected by too much light at night.

English researchers have mapped out the coastal areas that are most exposed to artificial light at night, Alan (Artificial Night at Light) from major cities or from industrial areas. And they have then calculated the amount of light pollution at different water depths by combining satellite images, field studies and computer modeling of how far the light penetrates.

Their world map of underwater light pollution shows that 1.9 million. Square kilometers Coastal Sea is exposed to 'biologically significant' alan at a depth of 1 meter - that is, exposed to an artificial amount of light that can affect wildlife. 1.6 million M2 has light pollution down to a depth of 10 meters. 840,000 m2 is light -contaminated down to 20 meters depth.

Artificial light at night disturbing nature
Previous studies have shown harmful effects of lighting association on e.g. Tanglops that during the day dig into the dry sand, but every night moves down to the water's edge to eat algae. Their nocturnal migration is disturbed by artificial lighting (Current Biology, June 2020).

A study last year showed that light pollution can reach into the water and affect wildlife on the seabed (Biologically Important Artificial Light at Night on the Seafloor). Especially at low depths, the marine environment is adapted to a large variation in the amount of light as a result of the seasons and the weather's change and often also of the possibility of high and low levels of sediments that filter more or less light from. But over a certain threshold, artificial light at night could affect the balance of biodiversity by changing the behavior of animals.

The atlas do not map the specific effects on local wildlife, but quantifies the amount of light that penetrates the water. The purpose of the map is to create a common framework for assessing the environmental impact of light pollution, which is increasingly attributed to an harmful effect on biodiversity.

“The spread of light pollution on land has been known for years, and some may assume that the artificial light does not penetrate the seas, but it does and in sufficient quantity to have a biological effect. Our Atlas is the first thing that quantifies the amount of Alan in the world seas. The seriousness of the problem in certain regions, including the Mediterranean, the Persian Gulf and the South China Sea, is quite alarming, ”says the study's lead author, Thomas Davies, associate professor of marine environment at the University of Plymouth, in a press release from the university.

Energy projects at sea provide great light pollution
On the new map of the light pollution, there is a long way out in the North Sea luminous yellow and light green plaque, which indicates the light association down to great depth. It is around the gas and oil fields where work is done 24 hours a day with dangerous machinery, which requires strong light for the safety of the employees.

The article mentions the energy projects in, among others, the North Sea, but also in the Persian Gulf, as a separate problem from the Light Association, because the artificial light often strikes directly into the water. In light pollution from metropolitan cities and industry on land, the light sources will most often be directed inward to land and not into the sea. The drilling platforms are also out in the sea, where the water is often clearer and therefore the light will penetrate further than closer to the coasts.

It helps to make garden energy projects a source of light pollution that the researchers behind the Light Atlas are calling for to keep an eye on. And it is true to feel not only the fossil energy, but also large RIGH projects at sea, where the work cannot be done in the dark or exposed to the bright hours.

The Danish Maritime Authority's environmental report from March 2021 on Denmark's marine plan includes the risk of light pollution as part of the environmental assessment, but it is primarily treated as a matter of the influence of seabirds and other wildlife above sea level. The risk of environmental impact in light pollution down in the water is still an underlined area.

Not subject to international law
The mapped 1.9 million Square kilometers of light -contaminated sea make up 3.1 percent of the 'exclusive economic zones' that can be established from the UN League Commission from 1982. The Oatmeal provides a coastal state to utilize natural resources in the sea, on the seabed and in the underground in the zone that can extend Up to 200 nautical miles into the sea and reach out over the territorial waters.

Other states have the right to sail and fly through the zones and must be allowed to lay underwater cables and pipes, but the coastal state has the right to enforce its own respective environmental legislation within the zone, so if light pollution is to be regulated, it would have to be done by Volunteerism and in the individual countries.

Title: Nødråb fra branchefolk: Ingeniørmangel truer den grønne omstilling
Full text:
Danish companies have nowhere near the engineers needed to reduce Denmark's greenhouse gas emissions by 70 per cent. By 2030, several organizations believe.

The lack of engineers in Denmark is now so pronounced that it threatens the green transition. This is how a number of organizations interpret new figures about the situation in the labor market.

Thus, a new cyclical study from the Association of Consulting Engineers (Free) shows that 98 per cent. of the member companies today lack qualified labor while the association's 10 largest members together demand 700-800 engineers.

At the same time, a new mismatch analysis prepared for Danish colleges and the engineering association, IDA, suggests that the problem will be much worse, so that by 2030 Denmark will be missing 13,000 educated candidates in the engineering fields as well as technology and IT. In addition, a shortage of 7,000 people with a medium technology or IT education.

“The figures show that the engineering shortage is a societal challenge. It's not just a single or a few companies that have problems, ”says Fri's director, Henrik Garver, and continues:

“The initiatives in the Finance Act that are intended to ensure sustainability and green transition make it clear that the need for engineering skills will continue to increase. The general lack of engineers threatens Denmark's leadership position in sustainability and green transition, so that development will go too slowly in relation to the government's visions and goals, ”he says.

Henrik Garver refers to the political objectives of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 70 per cent. by 2030 and the Finance Act's initiatives in sustainability and green transition, such as includes a drinking water effort for DKK 120 million. CO2 capture for just over DKK 2.5 billion. DKK and 2 gw more offshore wind.

All engineering subjects are hard hit
The biggest challenge in the green transition is to change the energy system, so that it is primarily based on electricity. It will require extraordinary many engineers.

“The green transition requires us to re -think the way our energy system works. And it requires many more engineers and energy planners. Because there is a big difference between being able to concentrate on maintaining its power plants and nets and then having to build a whole new energy system and do everything in a fundamentally different way. And that's what gives the massive lack of engineers right now and here, ”says Henrik Garver.

From a climate response that Ida and Aalborg University worked together in 2020, it appears that the green transition alone in the wind field will result in a more employment of 54,400 man -years by 2030 - of which well over a few thousand will be within the long scientific and technical higher education Education, such as embraces the engineering programs.

“A special challenge is the electricity we get through wind power that is only there when the wind blows. It requires a much more flexible system that can connect different elements to and from, and which can lead surplus current into power-to-x with the development of energy islands or for heating water to the district heating system, ”says Henrik Garver.

Dependence on abroad
Jan Hylleberg, CEO of the Wind Denmark industry organization, is experiencing a clear lack of engineers throughout the sector-but especially in the offshore field:

“Our sector is characterized by the fact that we draw on the entire portfolio of competencies. Therefore, it is very worrying that all areas are so severely affected by a lack of engineers. For that can mean that we cannot recruit fast enough and that we become even more dependent on foreign labor, ”says Jan Hylleberg, citing 15-20 per cent. of the sector's employees today have foreign background.

“We are dependent on the fact that in the long term, engineers are being trained. So any change that degrades education or reduces the number of educational places is unacceptable. With us, there is a concern that the policy makers are not sufficiently aware of the pace of change and that it can make the challenge greater than it should be, ”he says.

As an example of how fast the transition takes place, Jan Hylleberg mentions the hydrogen sector, where a few years ago there were modest expectations of what Power-to-X and hydrogen production could deliver by 2030.

»Today, expectations are towering as a result of a significant decrease in the cost of green power and hydrogen as well as requirements for CO2 reductions. The technology and market developments mean that the green transition in certain sectors will proceed faster than expected. It pushes the demand for eg. Engineers, 'says Jan Hylleberg.

Salary rises significantly
Another consequence of the lack of engineers is that organizations and companies steal employees from each other, says Henrik Lindved Bang, director of the Builders' Association. He points to membership surveys that show that there is currently extra focus on activities that require engineers with expertise in sustainability and digitization.

IDA's wage statistics also show that the wages for IDA's privately employed members increased by 4.3 per cent on average. In 2021 - the highest wage increase since the years leading up to the financial crisis.

»The salary pressure is due to the fact that, in particular in construction and construction, there is a full drone of the activities, which for the engineers, among other things. is about finding the solutions that have the least possible climate footprint. This means that companies try to entice other companies' employees with the promise of better conditions and higher wages, ”says Henrik Lindved Bang.

As for digitalisation, Henrik Garver is not so concerned. Because even though the task fills a part in the green transition, he experiences the digital skills of both companies and engineers as strong.

On the other hand, it worries and annoys him that neither in the short or long run seems to be political initiatives that can remedy the engineering shortage.

»Government and Folketing could do much more to strengthen the technical and scientific higher education and strike a battle to increase children and young people's interest in these subjects, for example. by lifting primary school teachers' competencies in these areas, ”says Henrik Garver, who suggests to earmark some of the 125 million. DKK, which is allocated to improve teacher education.

However, he also points out that an upgrade of the education system not only solves the problem: The companies must also have more on the field and make a greater effort to track talents, e.g. by recruiting from abroad and collaborating with national and international companies that have the necessary skills in the field.

“But one must always keep in mind that drawing on foreign labor can be both good and bad for Denmark. I've always been sorry when companies move out because they can't find the necessary labor at home. But basically it is a political responsibility to ensure that Danish companies can find the necessary employees and do not move out of the country, ”says Henrik Garver.

The defect is general
Social Democracy's educational spokesman Ida Auken emphasizes that society is not just missing engineers. Lack of labor is a general problem she says:

»The labor market screams at nurses, skilled workers, doctors, educators, teachers, engineers and many others. Therefore, the task of securing people to the sectors who are most needed is more important than it has been for a long time, ”she says.

“The government has entered into an agreement to create new study places around the country, so that the programs become available to more. And I am pleased that the universities themselves are planning to do the corresponding downscaling in the number of study places in the big cities in education with great unemployment, so that more young people are encouraged to apply for education with higher demand for graduates, ”says Ida Auken.

Title: Sensorer i vinger skal forebygge dyre skader på vindmøller
Full text:
DTU scientists are working to predict damage to wind turbine blades using digital twins and sensors inside the wings.

DTU, in collaboration with Siemens Industry Software, has developed a live demo of a digital wind turbine blade twin. By hand, the wing is put into oscillations, while in real time you can see its digital twin mimic all the movements. Photo: Simon Rubin

Monitoring Operators chasing data to predict expensive damage

Data and digital monitoring are high on the agenda of the operators of the world's large offshore wind farms. Not only do the individual mills grow in height and constitute a larger investment than before - they also move further and further out to sea, making it more expensive to inspect them.

Therefore, at the world's largest operator of offshore wind turbines, Danske Ørsted, they have long worked to make IoT a low -cost tool in connection with the maintenance of the ever -growing portfolio of expensive plants far out to sea.

Klaus Baggesen Hilger, head of Operations Digital & Innovation at Ørsted, says that the market for maintenance in a few years has moved from solely of one solution - a technician in a rope equipped with a digital camera - to today that be more multifaceted. Now drones can look both outside and inside the wings and in some cases even make easy repairs.

But he also recognizes that there are opportunities to make it even smarter, and therefore retrofitting of sensors and measuring campaigns is fixed practice at Ørsted existing offshore wind parks.

“The wind farms we have set up are extremely digital from birth. But as we run them, we also find out that there are some data we wish we had. With more data points, we will be able to improve uptime and generally organize a better and more cost -effective maintenance strategy, ”says Klaus Baggesen Hilger.

Not just a saving exercise
But it's not just a saving exercise for Ørsted, he assures. It is very much about dressing the offshore wind parks better for their role as the future power plants in the electricity system.

“Our parks have become so huge over time that it is extremely important for us to secure the uptime. We need to be reliably able to supply electricity into the electricity market, keep the frequency and tension in the network, and therefore we must also be able to demonstrate that we have full control over our assets, ”says Klaus Baggesen Hilger.

In the summer of 2019, the Wood Mackenzie analysis house released a report that concluded that wear and damage to offshore wind mills annually runs up to 5,000 days downtime and costs operators over DKK 450 million in lost profits and repair costs.

Therefore, a Danish-German project called Reliablade is currently looking more closely at how the industry can in future form a better overview of the state of the nature of the wings in particular with the help of sensors and so-called 'digital twins'.

The main purpose of having a virtual replica, complete with physical models that describe the interior of the wing as close as possible to reality is that it enables the wind turbine operators to get ahead of damage to the mill's most vulnerable component.

»The idea is that you can monitor injury development and thus predict the need for maintenance. Instead of conducting a periodic inspection, which can prove to be in vain, if the mills are fine, operators can use the digital twin to only go out to sea when really needed, ”says Kim Branner, a senior researcher and section manager at DTU Wind energy and is at the forefront of the Danish part of the reliablade project.

Sensors into the wings
Kim Branner explains that there is already a continuous monitoring of the nature of the wind turbine blades, but that there are no sensors inside the wings yet, which is a prerequisite for getting the high degree of insight into potential damage.

“To my knowledge, you have not really started getting sensors into the wings of the wind industry. In this way, you are a little behind, for example, the automotive industry, which puts both sensors, Lidar scanners and cameras around the cars in these years, ”he says.

Klaus Baggesen Hilger from Ørsted can sign this. He says the operators have long tried to explain to the mill producers that they very much like the built -in sensors in the wings.

»There are many other sensors on a wind turbine that provides data that you can use to say something about the condition of the wings. We measure vibration, rotational speeds and acoustic signals today, which can be used in that regard. But it would be delicious if we could get sensors into the wings too, ”he says.

»Today there are commercially mature solutions where the sensors are integrated into the wings, and it is therefore just a question that the industry (wind turbine manufacturers, ed.) Take it, because it is too late to do in our joints of the supply chain, 'he says.

The offshore wind has just begun a decade in which Denmark, with its plans to erect energy islands, must more than double the existing capacity of 2.3 GW. At the same time, the EU's climate target is called an annual expansion of at least 30 GW, both on land and sea, by 2030.

In other words, the wind turbine operators can look forward to a busy decade where the number of plants to be kept in mind and serviced will explode. Therefore, Kim Branner believes that it is urgent to have the right hardware installed in the mills.

“If I was a wind turbine operator, I would now start demanding more sensors in the wings. Because whether the physical models and the artificial intelligence behind the digital twins are ready to be used operatively or not, you can always update the software if it has gotten much better in five to ten years. So I think it's about just getting the sensors into the wings now, 'he says.

Title: Storbritannien forventer 86 GW vindkraft til havs
Full text:
Planning and expansion with offshore wind turbines is gaining momentum in the UK. In Denmark, the projects find it difficult to obtain permission from the authorities.

While Danish politicians find it difficult to agree on where and when to expand with offshore wind turbines, things are going differently in the UK.

In the latest statement from the organization Renewableuk, the overall current and planned expansion with offshore wind turbines has been calculated at 86 GW.

In this, both the existing 10 GW of offshore winds, parks that are under construction and then a large number of more or less previous stages of planning must be recognized.

Equally interesting is that the number of planned offshore wind turbines has increased by 60 percent over the last 12 months. This is mainly due to a tender round from England of 8 GW and from Scotland at 25 GW.

517 gw along the way in the world
Renewableuk has further collected the well -known plans for the whole world and assessed that there is a prospect of an extension of 517 GW with well -known plans. Of these, China accounts for 75 GW, USA for 48 and Sweden for 39 GW.

In the total figure, no date has been set on when the many wind turbines are in place and connected to the network, but it is already a lot more than the Global Wind Energy Council could show in their 2021 report. Here it was estimated that by 2030 there could be 270 GW of offshore wind turbines.

For 2050, GWEC estimates that there can be up to 2,000 GW of offshore wind turbines. In comparison, the World Bank estimates that there is a total technical potential of 71,000 GW worldwide.



Denmark currently has 14 offshore wind farms with a total capacity of 1,699 MW. There are another 14 projects while planning a total of just over 4 GW. In addition, wind turbines in connection with the upcoming energy islands in the North Sea (max 10 GW) and Bornholm (max 2 GW).

But planning has in several cases, especially for the coastal parks, run into local problems. Most recently, a protection area for birds in the Omø South area has blocked the construction of a park of 50 mills in the Småland waters for several years.

Title: DEBAT: PtX er slet ikke nyt - det startede på en højskole i 1891
Outlet:
Ingeniøren
Hans Christian Hansen
dr.scient, lærer ved Askov Højskole 1978-95
Full text:
PTX is hype. But inventor Poul la Cour was already on track when he put wind and hydrogen into Askov University College in the last century.

We cannot keep burning too much in the heating lighthouse and engines, because then we smoke into a climate time no wishes. Fortunately, a possible solution has been found. Pure energy from sun and wind is transformed into a pure fuel that goes by the name "Power-to-X". It sounds like a mathematical equation with the unknown X, but a solution has actually been found namely x = h for hydrogen or hydrogen, as it was called during my schooling. The beautiful thing about hydrogen is that it is easily formed by cleavage/electrolysis of water, and that by combustion with oxygen again becomes water. So there is no pollution.

Furthermore, the hydrogen can be propagated to a number of other fuels that can actually to a large extent and with limited pollution replace the current fuels in engines, and the hydrogen can be directly converted into electricity again in the so -called fuel cell. So it's just getting started with energy islands and hydrogen factories.

Why on earth isn't anyone found it before? It is there too, and it happened:

We screw the time back to the 1890s and to the village of Askov, best known for its college, which among other things. Had natural science teaching at a high level. This teaching was carried out by the meteorologist and inventor Poul la Cour (1846-1908).

Askov 1894
The press was well aware that something happened in Askov in the mid -1890s. Politics "Justus" visited the experimental facility in Askov in 1894:

"After the rumor, he succeeded in producing a new light which, by his affordable, would soon displace both gas and electricity. About all this, we spoke in the railway coupe as we got off at Askov on the way from Esbjerg to lead our readers into the inventor's laboratory. Poul la Cour inhabit one of the neat villas that together make up Askov town. His home is easily recognizable on a high mill, which with his free -ridden legs and parasolvings is somewhat reminiscent of the mills used in the Farmer States Dakota and Montana. It was blowing and the mill went to full force. The inventor, who received us with the greatest occurrence, is a forty -year -old man ... He is embarrassed and searches for the words until the conversation is brought into his special area. Then the person gets life
And the speech almost lyrical escape ”.

Then readers are notified of the technical works. The experimental mill in Askov, established in 1891 on the basis of a financial law grant, converted the wind's energy into electricity, which could then separate water in oxygen and hydrogen. The bars were collected in two containers. The idea now was that these gases should be brought down to the college and some other homes in Askov.

The plant was in the development phase when "Justus" was visiting, but it was convincing enough for him to end his report with:

"When we left the mill and from the field so his shadow inside the white clearing, we came to think that this radiant luminous stream was a saved storm - perhaps the same storm we had had a few days ago during the stranding at Thyborøn Channel. And then you don't even believe in miracles ”.

The test mill start 1891
Poul la Cour is known as a pioneer of wind power. Especially his studies of mill models and wing profiles in wind tunnels that resulted in a well -founded recipe for an "ideal" mill. But right from the start, his work with wind power was deeply associated with the idea of ​​hydrogen as an energy redium and stock.

“I ask you to read the feature. It is no fly idea, but a thought that I have for many years. Now it has finally gained the form, partly by the idea you see I have got about the hydrogen, and partly because I have got an appeal to help ”. The idea of ​​sketch form read:
“Task: Collection of the wind power so that it can be used when it is needed, and both for light, for heat and for movement…
The funds: By a wind motor, the wind power is translated through a dynamoelectric machine for electricity…
P. la Cour: Will apply the electrical power to tighten the water in oxygen and hydrogen, collect the hydrogen in a gas engine. Using its combustion for light, for heat and for movement as needed - 1 cubic meter of hydrogen can provide the same force as 5 horses for one hour.
Petition: DKK 4,000 for attempts to carry the case further so that a positive result can be submitted ”.

Brother J. C. La Cour became president of the Landholdholdningsselskabet the same year. He was a know of the business processes about the Finance Act and took the initiative on his brother's behalf. He immediately went to the Ministry of the Interior with the above note and met with the head of the department, later Prime Minister, Hugo Hørring a vacant place on the Finance Bill, and the grant went through a month later. Then in May 1891, the experimental mill in Askov was ready for experimental activities.

The hydrogen plant in Askov
Water -division is basically easy enough. But the process should be effective. So La Cour had to develop an appliance itself, as the best plant on the market turned out not to be good enough. It succeeded, but to demonstrate the utility of a hydrogen power plant, it assumed customers and a distribution network. La Cour therefore had to make sure that Askov College and the teacher's housing dared to join the idea. In the fall of 1893 he was reassured all parties with regard to price and explosion. In a summary of the negotiations in the Teacher Council stands:
“At the college, the petroleum lights in all the larger premises had to be replaced with the new light. Two large lamps in each of the gym, the lecture hall and the dining room were awarded the majority, a total of 1000 normally lights. In the reading room, the "Writing School", the Kitchen, the Living Room, the "Garden Room" and the Living Room, a smaller lamp was to be created each place and in addition a little walking information ",

When the agreement was in order, the hydrogen and the oxygen was to be led to the college. It required buried lead pipes. I was a teacher at Askov University College in the 1980s and experienced how the gas works from Natural Gas South bumped into lead pipes in many places. It was the old hydrogen system from the 1890s, these rediscovered. The system had been in use in the 1890s and a few years into the 20th century. And although the hydrogen tank was only 12 cubic meters, it rarely seemed that the plant had not stored enough energy for windy days. La Cour had demonstrated that a small community could well get its lighting needs from a wind turbine, an electrolysis apparatus and a hydrogen tank.

Big gas and explosion engine
Where the big hydrogen works and energy islands probably come first and foremost to supply hydrogen, La Cours also had to deliver oxygen, even though it is actually in our atmosphere. Taping both oxygen and hydrogen out of the electrolysis devices and leading the tribes underground to the college and into the premises could be dangerous. It is not without reason that the mixture 2-1 of hydrogen and oxygen is called "knobs" and has tempted "fun", now banned trials, in schools' physics rooms.

La Cour even made controlled blasts to clarify how great the risk of bang gas could be. In the experimental mill, I found an old glazing bill that was "renovating all windows after explosion". The hydrogen supply of the future based on wind power and solar energy hardly gets such a parallel course with oxygen and hydrogen, so bright gas explosions will not occur. But the hydrogen must, like any fuel, be treated with care.

La Cour's original application to the Finance Committee stated that he simply regarded the hydrogen as an energy storage. The goal itself was to be able to get "movement", or as we call it today "Power-to-X". To realize this goal, La Cour had to develop an explosion engine that could go on hydrogen or bang gas. After a series of attempts in 1895 in collaboration with the Maskinfabrikken Tuxen and Hammerich, they concluded that the gaseous explosions were too strong for the engine to go right. So he gave up transforming hydrogen back into electricity.

A technology -historical apropos
I have been wondering why La Cour so easily gave up moving on to electricity from his wind turbine hydrogen. Here I think it is striking that two days before he announced Tuxen and Hammerich he would pull out of the trial, had cut out a dated newspaper article and hid it as one of the few clips I could find much later in LA Cour archive. The article was about the German chemist Wilhelm Ostwald's speech in the Bunsendgesellschaft. The speech is famous - because here Ostwald went a consequence of the second main phrase of thermodynamics, namely that burning techniques can never become energy efficient and would otherwise create unbearable pollution. Therefore, the technique and society had to choose an electrochemical future. The article gave as an example Dr. Wilhelm Borcher's development of what we would today call a fuel cell. La Cour has not, in writing, has an impact on this electrochemical program, but his actions in the months around here can be interpreted in that direction.

Title: Med den rette løsning kan den danske olie- og gasproduktion elektrificeres
Full text:
The CO2 emission from the Danish production of oil and gas in the North Sea can be reduced by up to 900,000 tonnes annually. But the price per ton of CO2 is high and the project uncertain.

When oil and gas are to be raised from the production platforms South Arne, Tyra, Halfdan and Dan In the Danish part of the North Sea, large quantities of CO2 are emitted. Because in the process, gas produced on the platforms is used, and just before the Tyra field closed in 2018 (to be renovated), the emission peaked with about 1.5 million tonnes annually.

The Danish Energy Agency has now, in collaboration with the Danish oil and gas industry, prepared an analysis that looks at how it can be reduced by electrifying some of the processes with energy from VE. Three overall concepts have been looked at:

Supply of electricity via high -voltage lines from country
Supply from offshore wind turbines
A combination of the two previous
The result shows that the CO2 emission can be reduced by up to 900,000 tonnes annually by 2030, and that it can accumulate up to DKK 14 million. tonnes up to the expected production stop in 2050. But the results also show that there is a huge difference between the individual solutions compared to the CO2 shadow award, the social and company economy.

»In the analysis we describe a number of solutions in technical as well as financial terms. Thus, a basis has been created to assess whether there are some of the models that are interesting to work on, ”says Head Consultant at the Danish Energy Agency, Troels Krogh, who has been at the forefront of the work.

Different options on different platforms
Today, electricity on the platforms is produced with generators driven by gas turbines, and about 80 percent of the equipment at the production sites Syd Arne and Tyra are already electric. This applies, for example, to gas compressors and water injection pumps.

But at Halfdan and Dan, some equipment is directly mechanically connected to gas turbines, and it can present some practical challenges if it is to be electrified. This applies, for example, in relation to space restrictions and difficult access conditions. The platforms are also different in their options for quickly switching to the electricity and the degree of electrification are also included in the calculations.

Based on the three overall models, different options have been seen to supply the platforms from, for example, an upcoming energy island or a Norwegian offshore wind farm to be built in Norwegian waters but close to the Danish platforms.

Another alternative is to build a commercial offshore wind farm close to the platforms and then use a gas turbine during the hours when the wind is not blowing enough to supply the extraction.

Need to narrow the field in
The many opportunities and combinations also help to provide a mixed country trade of results. On top of this, the Danish Energy Agency estimates that the uncertainty for all data is -30 per cent /+50 per cent.

In the solution with the lowest CO2 shade price, there will only be electrification of South Arne and Tyra, which will also mean that the accumulated CO2 emission reaches only DKK 7.1 million. ton.

But conversely, the model, where electricity is obtained directly from a few offshore wind turbines in the area and then gas turbines are used for backup, give the lowest cost, but also a less potential for CO2 reductions.

“We do not point to a concrete solution but present the information so that qualified decisions can be made about the further course. From here you can imagine that we narrow the field and look a little deeper into instruments, legislation and the temporal aspects, ”says Troels Krogh.

The study of CO2 reductions on the Danish platforms is based on the agreement on the future of oil and gas recovery in the North Sea from December 3, 2020. Here it is determined that the recovery will stop at the end of 2050.
