Title: Sådan overhalede private havvindparker staten indenom i Østersøen
Full text:
The bottom line of the prestige project Energiø Bornholm has gone from black to blood red due to competition from upcoming private WE projects that can destroy the island's earnings by pushing the electricity price to the bottom.

Energi Open Door turned to charging port

On June 14, the Danish Energy Agency received two applications from the investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) on preliminary studies for two offshore wind farms near Bornholm.

The applications came via the so-called open door scheme, which at that time gave private companies the opportunity to bid with offshore wind projects for their own money and in a self-selected location.

One park, according to the project description, must have an area of ​​503 km2 in the Bornholm Basin South at 60-70 meters deep water 25 km from Dueodde with a capacity 1.5 GW.

The other is set to get a size of 341 km2 in Bornholm Basin East at 85-100 meters deep water 41 km from Svaneke. Since CIP wanted this park to also have a capacity of 1.5 GW, CIP applied a total of permission to establish 3 GW offshore winds near Bornholm.

It is exactly the same size as the offshore park that becomes the main element of the high -profile and DKK 67 billion expensive state project Energiø Bornholm.

Where Ørsted became so excited about CIP's projects that the company recently linked them under very high media attention, the Danish Energy Agency downgraded over the summer of the energy island's business case to red numbers for the most likely scenario.

Aggravated Business Case
The engineer has spoken to sources that point out that it is specifically CIP and Ørsted's projects that are the reason why the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply in a note dated June 23, 2022, downgraded its expectations for the island's business case and diminished its Otherwise, indispensable requirements for the island to become profitable.

The memo summarized the results of an analysis which showed that the establishment of Energiø Bornholm is reportedly up to DKK 67 billion, which in itself triggers a loss of DKK 10 billion. In addition, the construction of socio -economically only runs around if the EU provides a grant of two billion kroner.

Worst Case Scenario is a socio -economic deficit by establishing Energiø Bornholm of DKK 12 billion and a project -economic loss of DKK 24 billion - staggeringly large sums that the state has to cover.

Overtaken inside
The explanation of how the private offshore projects undermine Energiø Bornholm's earnings is simple: the private and state projects are so close that the wind will blow during the same periods and with the same strength in the respective areas. It will trigger a simultaneous electricity production.

As it is planned that the power will be led ashore in the same price zones, it will probably push the electricity price down to a level that is well below what the state originally budgeted with in the island's business case.

But even though the business case is poor and does not live up to the parties' own demand for the energy island to deliver a positive social economy, the state has nevertheless chosen to move on with the project.

Thus, the state must derogate from its original principle of earnings and provide state aid. It cannot collect a billion amounts from the actors who will offer the energy island's wind farm. It has otherwise set the nose after that interested bidders at Thor offshore wind farm were willing to pay 2.8 billion. kroner to be allowed to join the bidding round at all.

'Open Door' for large projects
CIP applied for the Danish Energy Agency for permission for the preliminary investigations, just a few weeks before a change in the Renewable Energy Act came into force. The change put an end to the open door scheme being used to apply to establish projects in deep water in distances greater than 15 km from the coast. Thus, in the future, these areas can only be accessed through state tenders, which, unlike the open door scheme, costs the private actors a billion amounts to be allowed to participate in. Therefore, the state tenders are less attractive.

The law was passed on May 19, 2022 and came into force on July 1. In the weeks up, the Danish Energy Agency received significantly more applications from companies that wanted permits to do preliminary surveys on projects - and this is perhaps very natural, in view of the fact that a possible access ticket to put off offshore wind projects in deep water with the change in the law completely disappeared. But what was behind the Danish Energy Agency was that many of the applications even went on very large projects of more than 1 GW. You hadn't expected that.

On its website, the Danish Energy Agency noted the sudden much "great interest" for the open door scheme and stated that it had "received a number of applications for very large projects," several of which are far from the coast.

As some of the private projects are almost sneaking up on the state - as CIP and Ørsted's projects do at Bornholm - the Danish Energy Agency sought advice from the chamber attorney to find out if the applications could be rejected. But they couldn't.

The Danish Energy Agency was therefore obliged to send the projects under the auspices of the authority in the auspices of the old version of the open door scheme. These hearings are still underway and will extend over the fall and over the New Year.

If CIP and Ørsted end up establishing their two wind parks near the energy island, it will have major consequences for the electricity price, points out Per Nikolaj Bukh, a professor of financial management at Aalborg University.

He refers to a 'technical briefing' that the government sent to the settlement circle in connection with the agreement to establish the Energy Islands in February 2021.

The technical briefing was made to elucidate what it means for the electricity price if the energy island of the North Sea is built too large. This can be compared to the fact that CIP and Ørsted establish two offshore wind projects near the upcoming Energiø Bornholm.

»The calculations show that one too large island - equivalent to one or more extra wind projects close by - means surprisingly much. The electricity price must not fall very much until you can see that it costs for the existing project, ”says Per Nikolaj Bukh, who says that a decrease in electricity price according to the calculations would increase the support requirement by DKK 110 million. crowns for each ear that extra wind projects push the price in the area. According to the memo, this means that a fall of 15 øre will increase support expenses by DKK 1.65 billion.

“I dare not venture out in calculating how big an earnings loss Energiø Bornholm will get because of CIP's and Ørsted's joint projects. But even DKK 110 million annually, in normal contexts, is a large amount. And since DKK 110 million only corresponds to a fall in electricity price of one ear, then there are quite large sums at stake here, ”he says.

Who is to blame for the private projects undermining the state?

"The Danish Energy Agency has had a hard time predicting that private actors would use such a fresh degree the open door scheme to make competing projects on this scale," says Per Nikolaj Bukh and continues:

“At the time when the open door scheme came into being, it was thought it made sense. But it would have been good if the Danish Energy Agency had then considered whether there was a risk that the scheme would turn into some form of self -service in energy planning. For it makes the state planning difficult. "

“If the Danish Energy Agency could have seen it, then of course I could have blamed them. But since I have not read the legislation and not a lawyer, I do not know if it was a visible weakness of the legislation. After all, hindsight is a noble discipline. "

'It's all uncertain'
Marc Skov Jacobsen, senior economist at the think tank Kraka Advisory, can spot another point where the two private offshore projects can hurt the energy island's economy. It is about Ørsted and CIP in their project descriptions planning to connect their wind projects to the same cables to Germany and Denmark respectively, which Energiø Bornholm will draw on.

"During the periods when it blows a lot, you can imagine a situation where the whole capacity in connection with Germany is utilized, which is why there is no room for all the power from the energy island," says Marc Skov Jacobsen and continues:

"Since the electricity price in Germany is usually higher, these situations can mean a lot to the profitability of the energy island project until additional transmission cables are established to Sweden and Germany."

However, he emphasizes that CIP and Ørsted must eyes an earning opportunity since they have offered their projects long after the state has launched Project Energiø Bornholm.

Marc Skov Jacobsen can see good, sensible points in the open door scheme. But he can also see a tendency for private actors to use the scheme as a fast track track to overtake the state's projects.

It increases the risk that it will be those who first establish themselves that flour the cake rather than those who are the best at building and operating such a project.

»Denmark needs lots of green power. Therefore, it is good that the focus is on speed. But there should also be more focus on who can do the best and which projects can best be integrated with the rest of the electricity grid, so that it is not just a question of who can sit in the field fastest, ”says Marc Skov Jacobsen.

Kristine van Het Erve Grunnet, Head of Head of Sea and Analysis, Green Power Denmark, doubts it will be a problem.

“We do not know how many parks to place around Bornholm to be connected to the electricity grid. And I think there is a lot that will affect the energy island's profitability. But there are huge uncertainties around, 'says Kristine van Het Erve Grunnet. "

Title: Analyse: Udbygningen af havvind har udviklet sig til Det Vilde Vesten
Full text:
Private actors are no longer alone in wanting to make money on offshore wind. Now the state will. It has created a root in the regulation of the offshore wind expansion, which can cost both market players and the state large sums.

The expansion of new wind farms on the sea must be done as quickly and efficiently as possible.

It all agrees.

Consensus has been that the expansion in the long run should be run by private actors who are pace by competing with each other.

In this regard, the role of the state is to create the framework for this to happen. But that role is the state well in the process of changing, for example. to introduce subsidy schemes where the state in addition to e.g. To cover the owner of a wind farm if the electricity price dives below a certain level also provides an opportunity for bidders to pay money to the state to get an admission ticket to offshore wind areas.

The change must, in all likelihood, ensure that the most effective developers win.

But when the bidders are willing to submit bids that are below the market price and at the same time give a payment to the state, this indicates that the developers have the prospect of getting a price for their electricity that is above the development costs.

In a purely competitive market, it would be so that sufficient offshore winds were expanded to make prices and costs something near matched each other.

When it is not the case, it must obviously be because the developers do not have a sufficiently great freedom to bring the price down to that level.

The benefit of putting the competition more free could be to achieve more green power and a lower electricity price.

In addition, a better Danish implementation of an EU directive could further trigger development - we will return to that.

Limit the market's opportunities
When competition is no more free, the two key interventions from the state are due to.

One is that the state has reserved more and more areas for tender. The second is that the state has restricted the so-called open door scheme.

So far, this scheme has allowed private actors to apply for permission to establish offshore wind projects of arbitrary size in a self -selected area at their own expense. But on July 1, a change in the law came into force that limited the scheme to now only apply to small WE projects within 15 kilometers of distance from the coast.

The official argument for slamming the open door scheme within 15 kilometers away from the coast was that the state would like to ensure that it is the most effective bidders that have access to the areas, rather than the distribution after the first come, -The principle.

Against this, however, it speaks that the open door scheme has been retained within the 15 km from the coast. And it's hard to see why the same logic should not apply in this area.

It is therefore an obvious thought that the closure of the open door scheme also contains an element of the state seeing an opportunity to earn well on the expansion of offshore wind in deep water.

8.5 GW Out of State Control
The problem is that the Danish Energy Agency has not been aware that the old open door scheme was formulated in a way that allowed private actors to also use it to apply for even very large projects far from the coast.

It therefore came to the back of the board when it received a large number of applications from private actors up to the deadline of the scheme's phase-out.

The Board informally asked the Attorney General if it could refuse to relate to the applications for the large projects, citing that the scheme was not intended for it.

The answer was no.

Several of the applications were signed by the investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, which in the middle of June asked the Danish Energy Agency for permission to do feasibility studies on, among other things. Two offshore wind farms with a total of exactly the same capacity that Energiø Bornholm is planned to have.

The fact that the projects are so close is a major challenge.

The challenge is that these wind turbine projects will be linked to the same price zones and thus push the electricity price further down. This can be positive for the social economy as consumers receive a lower electricity price. But it also has a downside by reducing the earnings that the state had hoped to achieve with Energiø Bornholm.

CIP has been able to take into account this decline in electricity price and now also Ørsted as a partner in their business cases for two common offshore wind projects near the energy island, which the two partners have always been aware of would be established.

The state, on the other hand, has only become aware of CIP's and Ørsted's two joint projects long after they had boxed to get the energy island's economy going up. The island's somewhat dubious business case risks being further deteriorating by the two major private projects that suddenly came dumping from the sky.

The engineer is the first media that brought the problem to Torvs in the article Now the economy behind Energiø Bornholm is crumbling. In response to the story, Michael Hannibal, a partner in CIP, subsequently told EnergiWatch that it has never been the idea of ​​bringing the 3 GWs into the electricity grid.
He pointed out that the projects applied for should be used to produce hydrogen via Power-to-X.

But if that was true, CIP in his applications for the projects in the Bornholm Basin South and East would hardly have spent so much space on discussing the possible connection points of their projects to the electricity grid.

Uncertainty for the energy island's wind farms
One of the prerequisites for the energy island of a sensible business case was that the energy island would be in the area with a resulting high electricity price.

But that prerequisite is not fulfilled if two private projects are established near, which push the electricity price down.

The low electricity price makes it less attractive for private actors to offer Energiø Bornholm's offshore wind projects.

It is likely to get the bidders to make a lower bid than what they had otherwise done. Thus, it is less likely that the state can get an income on Energiø Bornholm, which they received with Thor Wind Farm, where the bidders of themselves offered to pay DKK 2.5 billion. crowns just to join the bidding round.

The probability is further minimized by the fact that the bidders are expected to be paid a tax to join Energiø Bornholm.

Overall, it will mean that Energiø Bornholm's project economy will be impaired. And this can mean that we are again in a situation where the state will have to grant subsidies for offshore wind, namely to the one who specifically has to be connected to the energy island.

The question is whether it is a good solution when the market players otherwise appear to be willing to build on market conditions without support crowns.

The Danish Energy Agency is chasing optimal support model
CIP and Ørsted's projects near Bornholm are not the only ones who will challenge the state's plans to make money on offshore wind.

It can arise in all places where private actors are currently trying to wedge projects between the state via the open door scheme.

The Danish Energy Agency is in the process of assessing a total of six applications for a total of 8.5 GW extra offshore wind, which the state has not expected.

If they live up to the requirements for the open door scheme, the Danish Energy Agency has to approve them. And then these free assigned open door projects can also not only undermine the state's opportunity to make money on offshore winds on future state tenders, but also destroy its planning of the expansion itself.

Although the state's ambitions to make money in that way risk tightening legs for the expansion, the state is still determined to make money from offshore wind. But it remains very much in doubt about how it should do it specifically.

The smell of good earnings on offshore wind has prompted the ministry to ask its board to detect and develop new models for how it can best sell electricity from offshore wind.

The Danish Energy Agency is currently working diligently to track a model.

Many suggestions could be in play: One way to go could perhaps be to sell the areas for billions for going forward to get electricity from there at a desired price.

Another way is that the state gets one ear per produced kWh from the private player who has won a tender in a given area. And then of course there is also the opportunity to completely drop the idea of ​​earning something.

Tighten up
The fact that private actors and the state fall over each other in the battle to obtain as much room as possible to establish offshore wind is not only due to the state having an elaborate earning opportunity.

It is also a sign that the legislation is not regulating the area well enough.

The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply can e.g. Ask yourself if it has now also implemented the delegated act of the EU Commission's WE directive as intended, as it requires an increase in electricity needs to always be done with the help of new, support-free green power.

If that act was really implemented at home, it would hardly be possible for the state to hold its hand under its Energiø Bornholm when the Ministry's calculations show that it is hardly profitable and can only be kept alive with state aid.

If the act was enforced in Denmark, one would not be able to get into a situation where large offshore wind farms are built so close that one park eats the other's merit.

Title: Transformerstation på Sjælland udløser protester: Området er et beskyttet grundvandsreservoir
Full text:
The converter system is a hub for green wind energy, which via cables from Energiø Bornholm must be distributed to the Zealand homes.

When the huge amounts of electricity from Energiø Bornholm are to be transported to Zealand from 2030, the cables must go ashore and end at a transformer station.

The plant must, among other things, include a 25 meter high building, a 400 kV GIS plant and so-called 'Sive Islands'. The plant's construction will fill 18 hectares, and together the area will include about 60 hectares of land.

And then it has to be built at the village of Solhøj in Høje-Taastrup Municipality.

But Energinet could virtually not have chosen a worse location, says HOFOR, the capital's utility company.

The area is a protected drinking water area: More than seven million cubic meters of water are pumped every year by the source sites in the area.

In a letter, HOFOR's constituted supply director Brian Hansen Energinet criticizes not having sufficiently related to the drinking water interests:

"Transformer stations have historically been sources of pollution of soil and groundwater, and a large station of a type that has not previously been tested in Denmark should not be placed in an area of ​​drinking water interests," he justifies the concern.

"A location of Energinet's new plant in the area will conflict with existing and irreplaceable infrastructure," HOFOR writes in the letter, calling on Energinet to investigate alternative locations for the transformer station.

However, Energinet rejects the criticism.

“Our plant does not pollute. There will be measures that cut off the plant from the groundwater, so even if an accident occurs, it will not escape. We already have other transformer stations in areas of drinking water interests, and no pollution has been detected, ”says Marian Kaagh, Deputy Director of Electricity Transmission in Energinet, and emphasizes that they are entering into a dialogue with HOFOR.

Locals feel drummed
Energinet chose the location at Solhøj due to its proximity to the existing high -voltage lines and because the 700 -acre area provides space for future expansion of the plant, without exceeding the noise limits compared to the neighbors.

The alternative locations at Hove and Avedøre were deselected primarily due to lack of space, is shown in a note from Energinet.

But the selection of the area has taken place on the 'wrong terms', believes the mayors of the two municipalities Høje-Taastrup and Ishøj, Merete Amdisen (A) and Michael Ziegler (K), who have since been temporarily replaced by Kurt Scheelsbeck (K) due to disease.

On October 1, they received a letter from Minister of the Interior and Housing Christian Rabjerg Madsen, where he expresses a desire to make a landslide directive for the project that can trump the municipalities' own planning.

It caused the two mayors to shout about the process in a single letter.

"Based on a technocratic-economic analysis, Energinet has asked us to trigger a municipal planning that paves the way for the project without real citizen involvement."

Here they criticize The decision to place the facility in the open country rather than an existing industrial area, and calls the whole process a 'state viewing process'.

Same view lets the neighbors have:

At a civic meeting on November 7, people gathered together in a crowded gymnasium and directed several criticisms and angry calls against Energinet, according to Zealand Media.

City Council member of Ishøj Ole Beckmann (V) calls the project "Galimatias," and is skeptical of how much Energinet has really thought out the project before the location has been chosen.

“I basically think that there is a hurry in the case and that there is a need to be thought of in whole. This is one of Denmark's largest groundwater reservoirs and an area of ​​natural -historical values. And they have not investigated access conditions in the area at all: Right now, there are only a few narrow village roads that limit access conditions. So they will probably have to build new ways, and how will they affect the environment? '

He also fears that the authorities have not thought of the security policy situation into the assessment: whether one could prevent a groundwater contamination in the event of sabotage.

Energinet manners to rest
Ole Beckmann and several other stakeholders have also expressed concern about a possible power-to-x plant, as it appeared from an internal presentation between Ishøj Municipality and Energinet that the transformer station in the future may be linked to one.

But according to Marian Kaagh, there is nothing to be afraid here either, as a power-to-X system does not have to be placed in the same area as the transformer station. Even if it should come up, it will require a new permit from the municipality and a separate environmental assessment, she explains.

Marian Kaagh assures that the process will proceed completely after the book, and should there prove to be a danger to the environment, Energinet will take the process from there.

"The Ministry of the Environment must prepare an environmental assessment of the project, and all these considerations will be elucidated."

Until December 5, everyone can submit consultation responses to be processed in the project's environmental impact report. Based on it, the Danish Environmental Protection Agency must prepare an environmental assessment, thus determining whether the transformer station is compatible with the groundwater interests. It is scheduled to result in a Mijøt permit at the end of 2024.

From 2030, Energiø Bornholm will be completed and deliver 3 gigawatts to the Danish and international electricity grid.

Title: Han er kemiingeniør og står i spidsen for Danmarks største anlægsprojekt
Full text:
Morten Hesselager Pedersen has worked as a specialist in much of his career. Now he controls a construction building for billions.

Morten Hesselager Pedersen has what he himself calls a hardcore technical background: Chemistry engineer with many years of employment in various operational engineering roles in Maersk Oil and Gas and Total Energies.

Therefore, it is noteworthy that last year he agreed to be at the forefront of the Vindø project-Denmark's largest construction project to date for a staggeringly large billion amount-where he will establish cooperation with a view to submitting a competitive and therefore winning bid to the Danish Energy Agency at Energiø North Sea.

As Vice President of the Windø Consortium under the auspices of the investment company Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), he thus holds a far more economic-based leadership role than he has previously had.

He himself can easily spot the red thread:

“For the first ten years of my career, I primarily performed technical functions. But in 2012, as project manager for Maersk Oil and Gas, I was thrown into negotiations with Qatar's national oil company on commercial conditions for a major development project, ”says Morten Hesselager Pedersen.

It paved the way for him to move into a field of work where he could use both his technical skills and his experience with the commercial world.

In 2016 he was hired as head of the reconstruction of Denmark's largest natural gas field, the Tyrafeltet, where he was involved in negotiations with the Danish government among many other tasks.

First of all generalist
What goes back in the managerial jobs Morten Hesselager Pedersen has contested is the role of integrator.

It is about using commercial and technical circumstances to form a unified risk picture of the project and translate it into a balanced commercial assessment.

»To be able to integrate, I need a basic understanding of the individual building blocks that underlie an upcoming energy island. Here, of course, I draw on talented advisers who include specialists in both technical and commercial domains, ”says Morten Hesselager Pedersen.

The integrator role fits him well. At least he thinks that himself, as he has always tended to go as a true generalist to go after understanding the overall principles rather than digging into the most narrow and technical issues.

"Although I worked for a specialist role for the first decade of my career, I knew I would never get to move deeply, deep into a specific topic, but would be to a greater extent Jack of All Trades, Master of none, 'as he says.

»When I left the specialist track in 2012, when I headed into my first leadership role and got an integrated team of 100 people, it became clear to me that it was what I wanted to: add value by establishing an environment , where people thrive and work well together. From there, I have really just contested bigger and bigger leadership roles. "

In addition to strong competencies in finance, engineering and project management, in relation to how to understand the overall risk picture, his current task also calls the ability to set and comply with both schedules and budget - not to forget extremely good communication skills.

Therefore, he has also taken a number of courses in project management and communication at Stanford University. However, that does not change the fact that he himself feels that the experience of real life is what counts the most to be able to lift the task.

Two jobs on hand
The first time he was decidedly uncertain about what he needed was in 1996 when he was finishing his thesis as a chemical engineer.

Therefore, he applied for three very different jobs. He was offered two: one as a chemical engineer in House of Prince, the other as a wellsite engineer at Maersk Oil and Gas. He didn't hesitate for a second: It became Maersk.

“One of the things that appealed to me at the oil and gas industry was its great professional skill on the technical as well as the commercial front. I was always surrounded by very competent people, ”says Morten Hesselager Pedersen and continues:

“In addition, the industry gave me an opportunity to work with really large projects where the key to success has not only been a strong technical foundation, but also the ability to work and communicate across many interfaces and technical disciplines. Here, projects of this nature can just something that smaller projects cannot. "

Toward a common target
The ultimate management task has been seen from Morten Hesselager Pedersen's chair to get all the many people associated with the project to go against a common goal.

"The result I am most proud of are the many hot calls and messages I got when I left the job as manager of the Tyra Generet-calls from employees who expressed genuine pride and joy of having been with," says he:

"People asked me again and again: Morten, now you have spent six years on this, why on earth are you not doing it? And there are good and very personal reasons why I needed to challenge myself in new ways, work in a new environment and be squeezed out of my comfort zone at all, which is an important driving force in my life. "

And the possibility of becoming head of establishing Denmark's largest construction project, which even spoke directly into the green agenda, was too tempting.

He struck.

»The Vindø project is not only geared to deliver a significant part of the huge amount of green electricity that Denmark will need in the coming years. The island's location is also optimal compared to being able to export electricity abroad. But it depends on whether we succeed in reaching the goal of the construction. I have to do it, 'he says.

Title: Energiø Bornholm: Gevinst for milliarder ved at udvide med kabel til Tyskland
Full text:
Energinet has prepared a new business case for the energy island's infrastructure.

The Danish state can raise DKK 25 billion by connecting the upcoming Energiø Bornholm to the Danish electricity network.

In addition, the energy island is connected to the German electricity grid, you will achieve a further gain of about 20 billion kroner - ie almost a doubling.

This is stated in a new business case from Energinet.

The Business Case assesses the socio -economic value of the electricity infrastructure, which makes it possible to connect the power from Energiø Bornholm with electricity markets in one or more countries. It relates to all consequences in society, ie. Not only expenses for the establishment and operation of the electricity infrastructure, but also for gains for e.g. the industry and the climate.

Not surprised by the merge gain
Hanne Storm Edlefsen, director of Energinet's work with energy islands, points out that the business case basically answers two questions:

What does the electricity infrastructure cost in two scenarios, and in which there is the best social economy, provided that 3 GW offshore winds have been established, which must be transmitted via the electrastructure.

In this way, Energinet's Business Case becomes a kind of 'proof of concept' for just energy islands with hybrid electricity connections to more than one country, she points out.

She is pleased that the establishment of the electricity infrastructure gives black numbers on the bottom line even if you just connect the energy island to the Danish network. But she also bites that there is more to be picked up by also connecting the energy island to the German with an independent cable.
"The business case shows clear economic and climate advantages in energy islands, which at once enable large -scale offshore wind and connect several countries' electricity grid with each other," says Hanne Storm Edlefsen.

The whole idea of ​​energy islands is that you can just send power where it is most needed or where the price is highest. So it is not in itself so surprising that a connection to more countries is a better project. But 20 billion is immediately a large number in the merge benefit. Are you surprised by the large amount?

"No, it does not surprise me or energy - but therefore it is now very useful and absolutely necessary to meet governance (rules and guidelines, ed.) Having analyzes and calculations that tell you how good the social economy is," says Hanne Storm Edlefsen.

She emphasizes that there are significant uncertainties in the calculations.

Thus, there is a difference between how much better the Danish-German solution is, depending on which scenario for energy development in Denmark and Europe is used.

However, in all the scenarios that Energinet has assessed, the Danish-German solution is clearly the best.

The Business Case only includes the Facilitator Part
Hanne Storm Edlefsen points out that Energinet's Business Case does not answer questions about Energiø Bornholm's overall profitability. It only includes the construction investment, the costs and revenue that can be linked to the electric infrastructure, which must be used to transport the power. Costs for construction of the offshore wind farms are not included.

This is because Energinet is only responsible for planting and operating the electrrastructure in the form of cables and plants that become the heart of Energiø Bornholm. It does not operate the wind farms.

The business case for the construction investment itself has red numbers on the bottom line, which the Engineer has mentioned several times.

The government no longer expects Energiø Bornholm to become profitable.

The most likely scenario is that it will trigger a project economic deficit of DKK 10 billion. kroner.

The same business case shows that the isolated climate effect of the electricity infrastructure at Energiø Bornholm is greatest at European level with an annual C02 reduction from electricity generation of just over three million tonnes in Europe in 2040.

This causes Energinet to conclude that Energiø Bornholm contributes to making Europe greener.

Title: Elnettet om igen: Den grønne omstillings skjulte udfordring
Full text:
New, replacing old and changing in the way we have expanded our electricity grid for over 100 years.

Old and worn

Few people want to get that predicate stapled.

But this is nevertheless what the Danish electricity network must repeatedly put back.

It might have been to live with if we were still in the old world, where large central power plants sat like spiders in a solidly branched network and delivered electricity to large and small consumers in cities and in the countryside.

Electricity consumption dictated when new capacity was needed in the electricity grid.

For example, it could be a high -voltage connection - or a buried cable - to reinforce the supply of a region or a dedicated cable to a new industrial area in a city.

The point was that the electricity companies should respond only when the need arose.

But the entire electrical infrastructure has changed over the last 5-10 years, and instead we have now turned around the delivery of the year, so that it is no longer central power plants that are responsible for the primary electricity supply, but offshore wind farms, Solar cells and foreign connections.

If the district heating does not require a solid feature on a cold winter day, the role of the major power plants has been decimated in a few decades.

Instead, the focus is on charging electric cars and sending energy to new heat pumps as well as ensuring that all the new producing plants can get rid of the energy when the wind blows and the sun is shining.

But the possibilities in the Danish electricity grid are not equally distributed in relation to geography, and in several cases it has caused energetic solar cell contractors to tear their hair over the prospect of connecting a new solar park is 4-6 years out in the future.

In the spring of 2021, the consulting firm Ramboll issued a report commissioned by the industry organization Wind Denmark (now part of the industry organization Green Power Denmark), which calculated that with the expected increase in electricity consumption by 2040, investments in net connections will be needed and SOL Plus other necessary changes in the electricity grid of DKK 42.2 billion.

On top of that, an almost equal amount comes to the connection of energy islands and new foreign connections, so that the total bill hits DKK 80 billion.

These are large figures that of course have to be distributed beyond far more consumed kWh than today. The figure may even turn out to be at the bottom, as new planning figures have since been from the Danish Energy Agency, which includes, among other things, PTX systems on land with a total effect of up to 4.9 GW, all of which must also have electricity supply connected.

Believe in it!
'If you build it, they will come' - the classic replica derives well enough from a movie that big challenges should not stand in the way of doing something in the real world.

Or to put it another way: If you simply believe it and build it (in the case of the film a baseball stadium in the middle of a corn field), then someone will probably come and use it too.

So why can't we do the same with the aforementioned 'old and worn-out' distribution and transmission network? So reinforce it and expand it so that it is ready when a new owner of a solar park wants to get it connected or when the entire residential road chooses to get electric cars and heat pumps at the same time?

Specifically, Energinet could have built a few 132 kV connections between Zealand and Lolland, so the MW-Store Solar cell parks that have long been on the drawing board had been connected to the central transmission network. Now they have to wait several years, and maybe when the parks are dropped by then.

The answer to the lack of future assurance must be found in the predictability of the old world. For both Energinet and the local electricity companies, for years, they have struggled with the fact that, according to the legislation, they had to invest only when there was a specific need to expand the electricity grid - first and foremost an increased consumption.

That restriction has been slightly relieved with the agreement on extension with future -proofed electrrastructure from June 2021, which means that the grid companies can afford to be a little more at the forefront of investment than before.

But the agreement has not yet been implemented, and from both public and private companies it sounds unanimous that it is urgent to get formalities in place so that the WE projects can get started.

The Climate Council has previously said that "it should be a political top priority that the electricity grid does not constitute a barrier for further extension with renewable energy," and Green Power Denmark and Energinet have jointly proposed that zones be designated around Denmark where it is possible to quickly reinforce the electricity grid so that solar cells and wind turbines can be connected to the net faster.

Because in 2030 we do not have an electricity grid that can handle an electricity consumption that is almost twice as large as now, and the many WE systems that are part of the political plans, we can risk having to shoot a white stick after to reach the climate goals.

Title: Med 300 millioner kroner i ryggen: Pionercenter skal frigøre PtX af sjældne metaller
Full text:
According to the new center leader, the global green transition rests on the fact that new, alternative materials are available for the power-to-X process.

Today's electrochemical electrolysis processes are often based on the rare metals platinum and iridium, which risk creating a bottleneck for a global roll-out of Power-to-X (PTX).

In other words, alternative materials are needed if the technology is to be spread the globe around the Terawatt scale.

The alternatives will be the center of the brand new research center CAPEX, which will be presented at a reception today at DTU.

This is one of the Danish Basic Research Fund's so-called pioneer centers, which with a total grant of DKK 300 million will accelerate the development of new materials for PTX processes such as alternatives to today's use of platinum metals in catalysts.

»Materials such as Iridium, Platinum and Ruthenium are not scalable to the global challenges we face. Therefore, at the center we will look for more sustainable and scalable materials, ”says Tejs Vegge, professor at DTU Energy and newly appointed head of CAPEX.

"It is not possible that we find the world's best solutions in PTX if they can only be scaled to deliver sustainable flight fuel to you and me."

The PTX experts of the future
As two of Tejs Vegge's research colleagues from DTU have pointed out in a comment in Nature Energy three years ago, a scaling for a global electrolysis capacity of a TW will require between 100 and 8,000 tonnes of iridium depending on the choice of electrolysis technology.

In comparison, 10 tonnes are extracted a year.

For the same reason, the Nature Comment was also a clear call for professionals worldwide to put into research into alternative PTX materials.

"These are challenges that cannot be solved by a single researcher, group or university, but require entirely new ways of collaboration," Tejs Vegge says.

With CAPEX, a wide range of these international experts in material research and PTX processes will gather their knowledge.

Therefore, it is also obvious that the center must be physically anchored at DTU on a whole floor of the upcoming and newly established building Climate Challenge Laboratory, which in itself brings together research across computer simulations, test benches and synthesis and analysis facilities for material research.

From here, CAPEX will spread its activities to four other Danish and three foreign cooperation universities and researchers in everything from machine learning and chemical synthesis to robots and general PTX processes.

And then Aalborg University as the center's co-host has special facilities in hydrogen production, reliable power electronics and robot technology, which will be utilized with Professor Frede Blaabjerg from AAU Energi at the forefront.

»We have a very big focus on educating the experts of the future or 'Power-to-Xperts'. For the same reason, we expect to be able to educate 50-60 PhDs and a similar number of postdocs during the center's 13-year lifetime, ”says Tejs Vegge, explaining how, for example, fellowshipping programs should be prepared at the Cooperation Universities Stanford University, University of Toronto and Utrecht University.

Not fight back in ptx-ludo
When gathering experts in very different research fields, it is because, according to Tejs Vegge, the center will emphasize the methods of developing new materials.

He explains how the development of material today has to go through many and long -term process steps, from one group a new material in the laboratory, which another group then tests and documents, to one third group must prove upscaling.

Sometimes with failed steps along the way, so the development has to start over at LAB level.

In CAPEX you will go differently to it, so you can avoid it taking 20 years from understanding to commercialization of a new PTX material or device.

"Among other things, we have to create a material acceleration platform where all parts of a development process must be able to exchange data with each other seamlessly," says Tejs Vegge.

This means that, for example, you can take the results of material simulations and use the models' output to control an autonomous synthesis robot that can stand in a completely different
Laboratory, to produce the material that can be tested and analyzed automatically by means of artificial intelligence.

In this way, you can also change the material composition and on conditions such as temperature and pressure and put new parallel experiments and simulations over.

"We will develop a way to avoid sequential PTX-Ludo, where you follow the same way, but can be beaten back all the time," says Tejs Vegge.

Digital coupling from atom to energy island
To ensure that all parts of the development process are talking together, the platform must include, among other things, an advanced digital twin that can follow materials from laboratory to application scale. Including examining how it is best controlled by, among other things, the effect electronics.

»We get a digital twin connecting the whole process. Right down to the atomic level, but also at the system level. How do we best utilize the energy from sun and wind on the future energy islands with given materials, ”says Tejs Vegge.

Just that part of CAPEX is co-leader of the center AAU professor Frede Blaabjerg expert in.

With the help of digital twins, the center will be able to design, test and analyze new materials, electrolysis cells and whole PTX systems in a computer simulated, virtual universe before being manufactured.

In the end, the center will hopefully be able to invite both optimized and more sustainable, scalable PTX processes that can be used for anything from liquid fuels and advanced chemicals to plastic, medicine or proteins for supplementing foods.

The center is scheduled to open during the spring, but is officially presented to a reception at DTU today.

Title: På vej mod 2023: Enkelte tiltag, men ingen plan for cirkulær økonomi i regeringsgrundlaget
Full text:
Regeringsgrundlaget for den nye SVM-regering fylder mere end 50 sider, og miljøområdet har et særskilt kapitel ”Ambitiøs klimahandling”. Klimapåvirkning er således det miljøaspekt, der fylder relativt mest i grundlaget med fokus på planer for mere vedvarende energi og på energiens anvendelse til transport og i boliger. Desuden er der fokus på reduktion af landbrugets klimabelastning.

Regeringsgrundlaget indeholder ikke en plan for cirkulær økonomi. Ordet ”genanvendelse” er nævnt en enkelt gang i regeringsgrundlaget, mens hverken ordene ”cirkulær økonomi”, ”affald”, ”produktlevetid” eller ”design” er nævnt.

Den manglende plan for cirkulær økonomi er skuffende, når cirkulær økonomi er et område med stor opmærksomhed i EU’s miljøregulering, og der er en klar sammenhæng mellem ressourceforbrug og klimabelastning. Samtidig mangler Danmarks nationale handlingsplan for cirkulær økonomi substans inden for især affaldsforebyggelse og produktlevetid, således at regeringsgrundlaget burde have indeholdt planer for en mere ambitiøs forebyggende dansk indsats inden for cirkulær økonomi.

Mulige koblinger til cirkulær økonomi i regeringsgrundlaget
Selvom regeringsgrundlaget ikke indeholder en plan for cirkulær økonomi, er der tiltag i regeringsgrundlaget, som aktører inden for cirkulær økonomi kan anvende til at rejse diskussioner om hvordan den danske indsats for cirkulær økonomi kan gøres mere ambitiøs. I det følgende diskuteres følgende planer fra regeringsgrundlaget som del af et fremadrettet blik på cirkulær økonomi i 2023:

Undersøgelse af konsekvenserne af at opsætte et klimamål for dansk forbrug

Genanvendelse af byggematerialer som led i at sikre materialer til energiøer og andre former for byggeri

Investering i erhvervsskolernes udstyr, lærerkompetencer og fokus på arbejdsmarkedets behov, herunder i forhold til den grønne omstilling

Etablering af partnerskabet ’Sammen om klimaet’, der skal understøtte klimahandling på tværs af stat, kommuner og regioner, civilsamfund og erhvervsliv med vægt på det borgerrettede

Disse intentioner i regeringsgrundlaget kan anvendes af andre aktører til at diskutere, hvordan de pågældende tiltag bør udformes, og samtidig holde Regeringen op på disse planer i regeringsgrundlaget.

Til sidst i artiklen vurderes om ønskerne til regeringsgrundlaget inden for cirkulær økonomi fra et tidligere blogindlæg er blevet opfyldt,. Endvidere vurderes den mulige betydning af regeringsgrundlagets hensigter om ”et mere levende og åbent demokrati” i relation til cirkulær økonomi.

Planlagt analyse: Undersøge konsekvenser af et mål for forbrugets klimabelastning
Et spændende tiltag i relation til cirkulær økonomi er regeringsgrundlagets plan om at ”…. undersøge konsekvenserne af at opsætte et mål for CO2e-aftrykket for det danske forbrug.” (s. 29).

Den korte formulering uden nærmere analyse er et eksempel på, at regeringsgrundlaget flere steder indeholder overvejelser og planer præsenteret med en sætning eller to. Disse korte formuleringer kan skyldes, at regeringsgrundlaget er blevet til i dialog mellem mange politiske partier, som hver især har haft nsker til regeringsgrundlaget – både regeringspartierne og partier, der kun deltog i en del af regeringsforhandlingerne.

Når der ikke hidtil har været meget fokus på forbrugets størrelse og produkters levetid i den danske strategi for cirkulær økonomi, vil et mål for klimabelastningen fra det danske forbrug være et skridt fremad. Formuleringen om at ”…. undersøge konsekvenserne af at opsætte et mål for CO2e-aftrykket for det danske forbrug.” er ikke et løfte om at udvikle en strategi for at reducere klimabelastningen fra danskernes forbrug, men er dog en anerkendelse af, at det kunne være relevant at måle hvordan danskernes forbrug påvirker klimaet.

Inspiration fra Klimarådet
Hensigtserklæringen om en analyse kan være inspireret af Klimarådets notat ”Kommentering af Global Strategi 2022. Klimarådets kommentarer til den Globale Strategi i Klimaprogram”, hvor Klimarådet efterlyser, ”at Danmarks forbrugsbaserede klimaaftryk prioriteres højere som en del af den globale strategi, og at der bliver gennemført en mere målrettet indsats for at reducere det.”
Samtidig Klimarådet foreslår, at ”….det undersøges, om der kan udarbejdes et pejlemærke for udviklingen i klimaaftrykket fra forbruget samt eventuelt et pejlemærke for eksporten” til supplering af Danmarks territoriale klimamål.

Nødvendigt med indikatorer for både forbrug og for territoriale udledninger
Det er ikke nævnt i regeringsgrundlaget, at man for at kunne opstille et mål for forbrugets klimabelastning skal udvikle en indikator for forbrugets klimabelastning, men en sådan vil være nødvendig for at kunne følge udviklingen i forbrugets klimaaftryk.

En indikator for forbrugets klimabelastning vil sammen med en national indikator for klimabelastningen inden for landets grænser (dvs. opgjort efter Paris-aftalens regler) give større viden om forskellige aspekter af Danmarks klimabelastning. Det er således ikke et spørgsmål om enten at måle forbrugets klimabelastning eller måle den nationale klimabelastning ud fra reglerne i Paris-aftalen – begge opgørelser er relevante og kan supplere hinanden.

Opgørelsen af forbrugets klimabelastning vil for forbrugerprodukter, der produceres i udlandet, pege på klimabelastning i udlandet, som danske virksomheder og udenlandske virksomheder i Danmark kunne medvirke til at reducere ved at stille krav til deres leverandører. Dermed kan en sådan indikator blandt andet blive et vigtigt værktøj i virksomheders klimastrategi – ikke mindst strategier, der sigter på at forlænge produkters levetider og dermed nedbringe ressourceforbruget og dets klimabelastning ved at forbedre produktkvalitet og forbedre reparationsmuligheder.

Miljøøkonomisk vismand Lars Gårn Hansen i Økonomisk Råd har efter offentliggørelsen af regeringsgrundlaget peget på risikoen for dobbelttælling, hvis både Danmark som forbrugsland og et produktionsland tæller en reduktion af klimabelastningen fra produktionen af et produkt med i opgørelsen af deres klimabelastning .

Dobbelttælling synes dog ikke at være en relevant risiko, da Danmark ikke kan medregne en reduktion i udlandet som følge af reduktion af dansk import eller reduktion af klimabelastningen fra produktionen af importerede produkter i opgørelsen af sin territoriale opgørelse som vedtaget i Paris-aftalen.

Det vil være vigtigt at offentlige myndigheder, virksomheder, forskere, civilsamfundsorganisationer m.fl. analyserer effekten af strategier for at nedbringe klimabelastningen fra danskeres forbrug i retning af et nationalt mål – både fra indenlandsk producerede produkter som fødevarer og fra importerede produkter som eksempelvis elektronik.

Hvis en CO2e-indikator for forbrug suppleres med analyser af sociale, økonomiske og teknologiske ændringer, der er årsag til positive eller negative ændringer i indikatoren, kan sådanne analyser og tilhørende indikatorer skabe et vidensgrundlag for både den danske klimastrategi og den danske strategi for cirkulær økonomi, og for hvordan et mål for forbrugets klimabelastning skal nås.

Udviklingen af strategierne for at reducere klimabelastningen fra forbruget vil kræve demokratiske processer med deltagelse af civilsamfundet og dets organisationer for blandt andet at sikre en socialt retfærdig grøn omstilling, som Fagbevægelsens Hovedorganisation har formuleret som et krav til grøn omstilling på baggrund af en medlemsundersøgelse . Det vil således være vigtigt blandt andet at måle på forskelle i forbruget inden for og mellem forskellige indkomstgrupper som led i at udvikle virkemidler for at opnå et reduceret ressourceforbrug.

Strategier for forskellige forbrugsområder
Regeringsgrundlagets hensigt om at ”nedbringe klimaaftrykket på de offentlige indkøb, herunder også indkøb af transport og opførelse af offentlige bygninger.” (s. 29) kan anvendes til at fremme fokus på det offentlige forbrug og fremme offentlige grønne indkøb, om end cirkulære offentlige indkøb ikke er nævnt i regeringsgrundlaget.

Regeringsgrundlaget nævner desuden, at ”….landbruget og fødevaresektoren [står] over for en ambitiøs omstilling på mange områder” (s. 29) og nævner at blandt andet den plantebaserede produktion skal øges. Jeg ser selv plantebaserede fødevarer som del af en cirkulær økonomi strategi for landbrug og fødevarer, da plantebaserede fødevarer kan ses som del af en ”narrowing”-strategi for produktion af fødevarer, fordi ressourceforbruget ved produktion af plantebaserede fødevarer er væsentligt lavere end for animalske fødevarer. Regeringsgrundlaget relaterer dog ikke plantebaserede fødevarer til cirkulær økonomi.

Planlagt initiativ: Genanvendelse af byggematerialer som del af råstofplanlægning
Som nævnt er ”genanvendelse” nævnt en enkelt gang i regeringsgrundlaget. Genanvendelse nævnes i forbindelse med beskrivelsen af planen for udvikling af en dansk råstofplan for sand og grus for at sikre ”råstoffer til energiøer og byggeriet” (s. 34):

"Regeringen vil tage initiativ til en råstofplan, som understøtter en bæredygtig udvinding af sand og grus samt mere genanvendelse af byggematerialer. Det skal sikres, at vi har tilstrækkelige råstoffer til energiøerne og byggeriet – uden at vi sætter naturen og havnaturen over styr."

Fokus er her på at indtænke genanvendelse af byggematerialer som led i at reducere forbruget af jomfruelige ressourcer til byggematerialer.

Også forlænget produktlevetid for bygninger er indirekte del af regeringsgrundlaget, idet der i afsnit ”4.6 Øge udbygningen af vedvarende energi og omstilling væk fra fossil opvarmning” kort nævnes renovering af eksisterende bygninger: ”Sikre et stærkt fokus på energieffektivisering af både private hjem, virksomheder og offentlige bygninger” (s.31). Selvom denne målsætning om energieffektivisering af bygninger ikke beskrives som en målsætning, der skal sikre bygninger længere levetid, må det blive en effekt heraf – og dermed kan målsætningen – hvis der sikres flere midler hertil – betyde renovering og dermed levetidsforlængelse af flere bygninger.

Planlagt investering: Erhvervsskolers udstyr, lærerkompetencer og fokus på arbejdsmarkedets behov, herunder grøn omstilling
Regeringen skriver i regeringsgrundlaget, at man ”…vil investere i, at erhvervsskolerne har det rette udstyr, de rette lærerkompetencer og fokus på arbejdsmarkedets behov, herunder i forhold til den grønne omstilling.” (s. 20).
Den foregående regering havde også som målsætning at styrke erhvervsuddannelserne bidrag til grøn omstilling. Det skulle ske ved at etablere tre klimaerhvervsskoler som præsenteret i planen ”Danmark kan mere I”

Forslaget om særskilte klimaerhvervsskoler blev kritiseret fra flere sider og i stedet foreslog blandt andet foreningen Danske Erhvervsskoler og Gymnasier (DEG) , at alle erhvervsskoler og alle erhvervsuddannelser kan og bør bidrage til klimaomstilling.

Regeringsgrundlagets formulering synes at have lyttet til kritikken og ønsket om, at alle erhvervsskoler og alle faglærte uddannelser skal bidrage til klimaomstilling. Regeringsgrundlagets formuleringer om investeringer i erhvervsskolerne blev blandt andet fulgt op af udtalelser fra DEG i pressen, om at planen store investeringer i erhvervsskolerne for at kompensere for de foregående års nedskæringer.

AMU-systemets rolle i klimaomstilling blev også fremhævet af DEG: “Regeringen ønsker et øget fokus på implementeringen af mange af de klimainitiativer, som allerede er vedtaget. Her har vi brug for ikke mindst arbejdsmarkedsuddannelserne (amu), hvor man på 6 uger, kan lave et helt nyt uddannelsestilbud, som kan målrettes præcis der, hvor behovet er.”

Affaldsforebyggende cirkulær økonomi indebærer blandt andet, at kompetencer inden for fejlfinding og reparation af produkter bør spille en central rolle i erhvervsuddannelser. Eksempelvis kan den stigende anvendelse af software til at styre hårde hvidevarer være en udfordring ved reparationer og kan betyde behov for løbende fornyelse af uddannelser og udvikling af nye efteruddannelsesmuligheder.

Planlagt aktivitet: Etablere tværgående partnerskab for accelereret klimahandling
Regeringsgrundlaget lægger vægt på, at der skal ske en hurtigere grøn omstilling i form af omstilling væk fra fossile energiressourcer: ”Det går for langsomt med at gøre Danmark uafhængig af russisk gas og med at udfase andre fossile brændsler. Der skal fart på omstillingen af vores varmeforbrug til grønne varmekilder.” (s. 6).

For at accelerere denne omstilling vil Regeringen blandt andet ”Etablere partnerskabet ’Sammen om klimaet’, der skal understøtte en accelereret klimahandling på tværs af stat, kommuner og regioner, civilsamfund og erhvervsliv med vægt på det borgerrettede.” (s. 32). Partnerskabet indgår som del af regeringsgrundlagets afsnit 4.6 ”Øge udbygningen af vedvarende energi og omstilling væk fra fossil opvarmning”. Regeringsgrundlaget lægger vægt på at finde ud af, hvordan der kan sikres et ”højt tempo i udbygningen af vedvarende energi på land”.

I afsnit 6.1 om et sammenhængende Danmark beskrives endvidere, at Regeringen vil ”Undersøge, hvordan naboer og kommuner bedst får del i økonomiske gevinster ved at lægge jord til vedvarende energi på land. Eksempelvis ved etablering af energifællesskaber eller ved at udvide den nuværende VE-bonusordning.” (s. 42). Det fremgår dog ikke om partnerskabet ”Sammen om klimaet” skal spille en rolle i udviklingen af sådanne omfordelings- og fællesskabsstrategier.

Der er brug for en bredere forståelse af ”klimahandling” end i regeringsgrundlaget. Regeringsgrundlaget kobler således ikke partnerskabet om klimahandling til cirkulær økonomi – dvs. til ressourceforbrugets størrelse og dets klimabelastning. Der kunne være brug for netop et sådant partnerskab til at udvikle koncepter og rammer for etablering af nationale og lokale initiativer inden for cirkulær økonomi – f.eks. deleøkonomiske fællesskaber og reparationsinitiativer baseret på frivillige eller som socialøkonomiske virksomheder.

Blev ønskerne til regeringsgrundlaget opfyldt?
I det følgende gøres status for i hvilket omfang regeringsgrundlaget opfylder de otte ønsker til Regeringens strategi for cirkulær økonomi, der blev beskrevet i blogindlægget ”Hvad du ønsker skal du (måske) få: Ønskeliste til den nye regerings strategi for cirkulær økonomi” . Endvidere vurderes fire andre ønsker, der kom i kommentarerne til indlægget på LinkedIn. Disse tolv ønsker til Regeringens strategi for cirkulær økonomi og en vurdering af hvorvidt de bliver opfyldt med regeringsgrundlaget ses i nedenstående tabel.

De to ønsker ”Bedre økonomiske vilkår for tekniske skoler og FGU” og ”Lovgivningsmæssige og økonomiske rammer for lokale tiltag inden for cirkulær økonomi” er således dem, der i størst omfang opfyldes med regeringsgrundlaget. For de tre ønsker om offentlige cirkulære indkøb, cirkulær økonomi i byggeriet, bevillinger til Det Grønne Nationalregnskab og databaser om cirkulær økonomi er der formuleringer i regeringsgrundlaget, som måske kan medvirke til at få ønskerne opfyldt. For de syv resterende ønsker er der ingen koblinger i regeringsgrundlaget.

Hensigt: Et mere levende og åbent demokrati
Til sidst en vurdering af regeringsgrundlagets formuleringer om demokrati. Jeg har tidligere på denne blog kritiseret den foregående regerings udvikling af strategien for cirkulær økonomi i affaldssektoren, som ledte til en plan for liberalisering af affaldssektoren, som et eksempel på det Hartmut Rosa kalder brug af ”det øjeblikkeliges magt” i et accelerationssamfund. Dvs. en proces hvor der med korte tidsfrister - og uden en bredere debat om andre mulige løsninger presses en løsning igennem under henvisning til, at en løsning haster.

Det er derfor spændende, at regeringsgrundlaget har et mål om en forbedring på dette område, idet Regeringen vil skabe ”Et mere levende og åbent demokrati” og vil sikre ”God regeringsførelse”. Regeringen vil således sikre, ”….at politiske beslutninger ikke fremstår som resultat af en faglig nødvendighed”. Det betyder, at ”….embedsværket ikke må ….. fremstille en politisk besluttet løsning som den eneste fagligt velbegrundede, hvis der reelt er flere fagligt velbegrundede løsningsmuligheder.” (s. 48).

Hvis den foregående regering havde haft sådanne målsætninger, kunne forløbet om udvikling af en strategi for cirkulær økonomi i affaldssektoren være forløbet på en mere demokratisk måde og måske ført til andre og bedre løsninger.

Regeringsgrundlagets partnerskab ”Sammen om klimaet” kan også ses som et ønske om mere demokratiske beslutninger om grøn omstilling med deltagelse af flere aktører i samfundet. Som tidligere nævnt er det vigtigt, at ønsket om acceleration af den grønne omstilling ikke sker på bekostning af en socialt retfærdig grøn omstilling!

Ligeledes kan regeringsgrundlagets formulering om at ”… følge op på anbefalingerne fra ekspertarbejdsgruppen om demokratiske virksomheder” (s. 26) ses som et ønske om at styrke demokratiske virksomheder. Inden for cirkulær økonomi kan sådanne virksomheder spille en vigtig rolle – f.eks. inden for reparationer og deleøkonomi.

Hvis man skal være optimistisk her ved årsskiftet: Der er enkelte gode målsætninger og planer i regeringsgrundlaget, der kan anvendes til at fremme cirkulær økonomi og gøre det på en mere demokratisk og mere ambitiøs måde. Men det kræver, at forskere, civilsamfundsorganisationer, tænketanke m.m. følger op på regeringsgrundlagets målsætninger og holder Regeringen fast på dens intentioner og planer!

Title: Energinet har usædvanlig mange kabelfejl: Risikerer skift af over 100 endemuffer
Full text:
In recent years, there have been so many errors in end muffler that risk causing power breaks that Energinet may have to replace over 100 of them.

All 80 offshore wind turbines at Horns Rev 1 had to be stopped at the beginning of December despite good wind conditions, as an error occurred on the several meters high end muffler connecting the cable from the offshore wind farm 20 kilometers out in the North Sea to the high -voltage station at Varde.

There were 11 days from a large energy discharge destroyed the end muffler until the last wind turbine was switched on again. The error cost the owners of the offshore wind farm several million dollars in revenue, while green power was lost in the middle of energy crisis and record high electricity prices.

End muffs errors have been too many of the lately. It recognizes Energinet, which is responsible for operating the Danish Energy Infrastructure, after the Engineer has gained access to a note of the number of cable errors.

“We've had too many mistakes. We expect something to break, but by 2022 we were significantly higher than expected on cable errors based on history and experience from other countries. The errors are often on end muffler, so that is why we look at them especially, ”says Anders Pallesen Jensen, department head of Asset Emergency Jutland at Energinet.

Specifically, it is about 150 kV and 400 kV end mufflers, which are used at the end of a cable, such as at a transformer station or as a transition between cable and air line on stretches that are cable due to beautification.

Since 2014, Energinet has had a total of 40 cable crashes. Almost half of them happened after 2020, and all five errors of 400 kV connections in the past two years are due to errors in end muffler, which have been relatively new and only about 10 years old.

Anders Pallesen Jensen calls the number of end muffler errors "startling" if there are coincidences, and estimates that there may be systematic errors. According to him, the high error rate is not due to the sleeves that the sleeves have been neglected.

"We have tried to maintain them and look at them as best as we can, so they should be able to last for longer than they have done," says Anders Pallesen Jensen.

Power cuts and lost earnings
End muffs errors and thus high voltage cables limit the transport of electricity that Energinet and thus the Danish Treasury earns through trade with our neighboring countries when electricity from areas with cheap electricity generation is moved to areas with more expensive electricity generation.

In addition to lost earnings, the errors can also have serious consequences for electricity supply security.

"It can in the extreme consequence lead to power cuts for consumers," says Anders Pallesen Jensen.

This was just about to happen last April. Here, an error on a 400-kV end muffler on the important cable stretch Ferslev-Lady, which connects the high-voltage network between Central and North Jutland, put out of play for eight hours.

The error cost a non -calculated million amount in repairs and lost revenue, and for a shorter period a "greatly increased risk of extensive power breaks in East Jutland" because other parts of the electricity grid were at the same time revision, explains Anders Pallesen Jensen.

“It caused some major socio -economic losses, especially because the electricity price has been very high in 2022 - also at the time of the error. In addition, it provided a reduced electricity supply security in the way that it would not fail so much more until it could result in power breaks for some electricity consumers in Jutland, ”he says.

Cause still not found
The reason for the many errors on the end mufflers has not yet been clarified. However, Energinet has identified 400 kV end mufflers with SF6 insulation from Italian supplier Prysmian as the most faulty.
Five out of nine faulty end sleeve since 2014 have been delivered from here.

Energinet's specialists estimate that the errors may be due to insufficient grounding due to wear or be due to small unwanted movements in the cable semiconductor by changes in the temperature that over a long time stresses the end muffler.

If there are systematic problems with the end muffler from Prysmian, it risks causing many errors.

In Jutland alone, 113 of them have been installed, which will cost over DKK 100 million to replace besides being very time -consuming and resulting in some outdoor time.

However, errors on end muffler cost on the same parameters.

Energinet is currently awaiting a final assessment from the Norwegian Research Institute Sintef, who has been assigned the task of clarifying the error more precisely and offers suggestions for actions that can prevent future errors.

“We need to make a final decision about what to do. It depends on what the final assessment of the cause of the error shows. If it shows that with some minor repairs you can expect to have an extended life, then of course we will do it. But if it turns out to be a systematic error, then we may be forced to replace - if not all - at least a large part of them, ”says Anders Pallesen Jensen.

In the coming years, the number of cable errors will, all else being equal, rise as more cables enter the Danish electricity system. In the last five years, the length of Energinet's cables has increased by about 40 percent and is expected to rise by about 50 percent in the next five years - this without including cables for the Viking Link and the Energy Islands.

Title: Verdens største konverterstation og monsterkabler mellem Nordsø-møller og Tyskland
Full text:
The Germans are investing in HVDC cables and converter station at sea to secure the green power from the wind farms in landing.

Like Denmark, so must be massively expanded with wind power in the German part of the North Sea.

In order to get the green energy ashore, DC cables are needed, and therefore the German authorities have started two projects called Lanwin1 and Lanwin3.

The cables from the North Sea and to the connection points in Lower Saxony and North Rhine-Westphalia will both be 390 kilometers long and will, on most of the way, run parallel to each other from the wind farms.

In order to be able to transport the energy as a direct current, two converter stations must be built on platforms about 170 km out in the North Sea.

Each connection has a transport capacity 2,000 MW DC at 525 kv.

Thus, there will be the opportunity to erect up to 4,000 MW wind turbines in the designated German areas of the North Sea.

At the converter stations, 66 kV alternating current from the wind farms is converted to 525 kV DC, which is led ashore.

Same technique on Denmark's Energiø
Contrary to the previous practice, where the energy from each wind farm is carried ashore in its own cable, the construction of large converter stations offers the sea to build a multit terminal HVDC system (High-Voltage Direct Current).

It can subsequently be expanded with several wind farms. The price of the two converter stations will be about DKK 30 billion.

The platforms themselves will be built on a shipyard in Cadiz, Spain, while Siemens will be responsible for the converter stations themselves.

The converter stations must be placed on platforms, each of which will weigh 34,000 tonnes and stand ready respectively. 2029 and 2030.

Then the cables must be connected to land where converter stations and new high -voltage connections must also be built.

In respectively. 2031 and 2033 the first green power is expected to be sent from wind farms to German consumers.

The German venture is part of the Esbjerg Declaration from last year, when Denmark, Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands agreed to expand with 65 GW of offshore wind in 2030 and increase capacity to at least 150 GW in 2050.

It can supply up to 230 million European households with green power.

Title: Energistyrelsen: Danmark frådser muligvis med pladsen til offshore-vind
Full text:
The distance between offshore wind turbines and parks is much larger in Denmark than in, for example, Germany and the Netherlands.

The distance between the wind turbines in the Danish offshore parks is very large compared to other countries. The same goes for the distance of the parks.

At least it assesses the Danish Energy Agency, which in a presentation whose Slide's Engineer has gained access to the Danish conditions as possible 'fråts with the space'.

For a reason, the board has begun to investigate whether there will be gains by packing both wind turbines and parks at sea closer.

This will increase the benefits of the areas available to Denmark and make it easier to meet the political targets of 4 GW extra offshore wind by 2030.

Jonas Axelgaard, who is the office manager of the Danish Energy Agency, confirms in an email that the low energy density of the Danish parks is currently concerning the board.

However, he emphasizes that the board has not yet decided on - and if so how - to work with another energy density for upcoming offshore wind farms.

»It is true that, compared to several other countries, Denmark uses low energy density in connection with the supply of offshore wind farms. Increased energy density may entail better utilization of the sea area - but conversely can push the costs per produced amount of energy up, ”Jonas Axelgaard writes in the email.

Vattenfall: Thor should be twice as big
The presentation at the Danish Energy Agency was held a few months after Vattenfall's director of the development of offshore wind projects Ane Mette Lysbech-Kleis criticized the Danish state for having only set the energy outcome for the offshore park Thor to 1 GW.

After Vattenfall's then calculations, there should in fact have been room to set up to 2.2 GW of offshore wind on the area - that is, more than a doubling of the effect that the state had set as the top limit.

“It became clear to us in the process and subsequently that there could be room for something more in the area set aside for Thor. When we look at similar areas that we have elsewhere around Europe, it clearly shows that Thor can be optimized, ”Ane Mette Lysbech-Kleis told the Exchange.

Researcher: Take care to fall for the temptation
Xiaoli Guo Larsén, a senior researcher at DTU Vindenergi, has been submitted to the relevant slides from the board's presentation.

She warns against distinguishing too much on how to do abroad and headlike packing offshore mills and parks more closely.

"It is tempting to stop more turbines in the limited area, so that you turn up the density of turbines and also achieve a smaller distance between the wind farms," ​​she says.

“The problem is that by increasing turbine density, you also automatically increase costs. At the same time, the efficiency of the wind farms is reduced because the mills create more turbulence, and at the same time steal winds apart - together called wake effects, ”Xiaoli Guo Larsén points out.

Before the Danish Energy Agency embarks on increasing the density, it should consider from her chair how big the wake effect is and how much extra energy production is achieved from the higher density.

»The goal is to harvest more potential wind energy and at the same time minimize the establishment and operating costs measured by the parameter 'Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE)'. And it depends a lot on the specific situation, how close the wind turbines and parks should be placed on each other, ”she says.

Xiaoli Guo Larsén points out that in an offshore supply there are many things to take into account at sea such as national borders, sailing routes, environmental protection, water depth and distance to the coast.

For this reason, there is, as a starting point, very little space to do well to establish offshore winds.

"Therefore, it is understandable that we are looking to place more turbines and wind farms in the limited space we have available," she says.

The greater the park the lower efficiency
Senior researcher Xiaoli Guo Larsén urges the Danish Energy Agency to take care of putting the parks too close up and down.

She refers to a review brought in the scientific journal Boundary-Layer Meteorology in December 2022, which shows that the efficiency of the parks falls as the size of the parks is increased.

Title: Her er Energinets store plan: Sådan ruster nye kabler og ledninger elnettet til fremtiden
Full text:
Both 400 kV high voltage connections and new transformer stations must be expanded to accommodate a much higher electricity consumption, new solar parks and wind turbines.

Today, Energinet publishes a new plan for the expansion of the electricity grid, which prepares and strengthens the pervasive electrification of Denmark's production and energy consumption.

In this, the Danish regions are reviewed separately in relation to the extensions already adopted and which energy expects to be necessary to handle the energy.

All the latest political agreements and the cold data in the Danish Energy Agency's latest calculation assumptions for the energy system called AF22 point only one way - namely, against a massively higher electricity consumption in a few years.

AF22 shows that Denmark's total electricity consumption increases to approximately 80 TWH in 2030 and 156 TWH in 2040.

In addition to many new heat pumps, data centers and electric cars, consumption will especially be powered by a massive expansion with PTX systems.

It will require new electrical connections, both locally, but especially on the overall network.

Are to be used as early as 2030
The report called 'Long -term grid structure for the electricity transmission network 2022' is closer to a benchmark than a final bid, Energinet writes.

It acts as an intermediate station for the long -term development plan (LUP), which will be released in a year and draws a more adequate picture of what will be built until 2040.

Here, there may well be even more new connections on the map, because even though the new plan takes into account the past year's policy, it is made based on the old analysis prerequisites (of21).

AF21 predicted a significantly less electricity consumption: Consumption by 2040 corresponds to the consumption already expected by 2030.

"With the current political ambitions, the network structure must thus be established in more detail around 2030 than 2040," Energinet writes in the report.

Much more electric from ve
In addition to electricity consumption rising sharply over the coming years, the expansion with VE will also press the electricity grid.

In AF21, it was expected that there would be an electricity generation capacity from wind and sun of 30 GW in 2040.

In AF22, it has now doubled to 60 GW. Report's 'Big marks' does not set date on the individual extensions. They can "be initiated as the need arises."

Potential extensions
The possible extensions are divided geographically and especially North Jutland and Lolland-Falster are the focus on an expectation of many new solar parks.

In some places, existing systems will be expanded with new wires, in other places new cables will be dug into the soil, especially 150/132 kv.
