Several new 400 kV connections must also be established, and here Energinet emphasizes that it has not yet been decided whether they should be buried or hung on electric masts. This is because it is not always technically possible to dig down such strong connections.

In North Jutland it has already been decided to establish two new 150 kv transformer stations in Tylstrup and Tue Kær.

In addition, two 400 kV transformer stations must be expanded so that they can pass on energy in the system.

In Djursland, Funen and Central Zealand, 150 and 132-KV connections will also be expanded, while the connection from Central Zealand to South Zealand will be expanded by up to four 220 kV cables.

Three of them continue to Lolland-Falster.

In particular, Central Zealand can prove to be a demanding task, as large quantities of electricity have to be handled from solar cells on Lolland-Falster and electricity from Energiø Bornholm.

Energinet also writes that previous solutions based on the old prerequisites in AF21 will no longer work due to restrictions in the grid between Køge and Roskilde.

Title: Mens Danmark bygger energiøer: Tyskland og Holland vælger dem fra i Nordsøen
Full text:
German network manager prefers platforms when electricity from offshore wind turbines must be sent ashore.

The countries around the North Sea have seen a golden opportunity to harvest energy with giant wind farms.

This was clear when state leaders from Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands last summer signed the 'Esbjerg Declaration' to ensure that 65 GW of offshore winds in 2030 and 150 GW by 2050.

But where Denmark is aiming to build an energy island with space for manpower, spare parts, converter station and possibly also electrolysis, both the Netherlands and Germany have chosen a completely different solution.

Instead, the wind farms should be connected to a converter station located on a platform.

The model is also known from the Kriegers Flak offshore wind farm in the Baltic Sea, where the energy can be sent to both Denmark and Germany according to market price.

Two platforms for 30 billion kroner
The German network responsible company AMPRION has just presented a contract with Spanish Dragados Offshore and German Siemens Energy to establish two large platforms located about 170 kilometers out in the North Sea.

From 2030, the two platforms will houses converter stations to a number of upcoming German offshore wind farms.

On the platforms, 2 GW electricity from the wind turbines can be converted to 525 kV DC, which is then sent ashore and converted back to AC stream in northern Germany.

It is also included in Amprion's considerations that the new converter stations can be linked to other national or international offshore converter systems.

The total price for the two converter stations will be about DKK 30 billion.

It is not immediately possible to compare that price with the Danish plans for an energy island.

It is estimated that it will cost about DKK 10 billion to build the island itself. There are no costs for converter stations and the like.

The total price for the Danish Energiø with all equipment on the island and offshore wind turbines connected, is estimated to cost around DKK 210 billion.

A way other than Denmark
With the choice of platforms, the Germans go a different path than Denmark.

We have asked Amprion why it is focusing on converter stations located on platforms instead of an energy island and we have received a written response.

"AMPRION prefers platform -based connections to offshore wind turbine projects located in the German part of Nordsø as they build up on well -known platform topologies," says Stefan Sennekamp, ​​spokesperson for the project.

One of the arguments for amprion is that with two platforms they get a backup option and can send power ashore, although errors should occur somewhere.

But the platforms, according to Stefan Sennekamp, ​​also offer a unique opportunity to continuously expand the number of connected wind farms.

So it is not necessary to build a whole energy island to get started.

"The first systems are multi-terminal DC with a low number of terminals where potential benefits of the island approach do not count so heavily," he says.

Does this mean that Amprion completely depreciates energy islands?

"No, in general, energy islands are interesting alternatives and should be preserved as an opportunity for future interconnected offshore systems in the German part of the North Sea."

Production of hydrogen and ammonia on an energy island highlights several as an essential argument. But is it no longer possible with a platform?

»Electrical energy can always be most efficiently used in the electricity sector. Thus, from a climate perspective, it would be ineffective to use offshore wind energy for hydrogen production if it could instead be used within the electricity sector. Only excess energy that cannot be integrated into the electricity market should be used for hydrogen production. Therefore, we need both options: to be able to use offshore wind energy in the electricity sector - which requires cables to land - or in the gas sector via electrolysis located on land, ”says Stefan Sennskamp

Whether the German platforms will be connected to the Danish Energiø or other international systems will, according to Stefan Sennskamp, ​​build on an assessment of the benefits of such a link in relation to the cost.

Denmark is holding onto “flexible” solution
During the spring of 2023, the Danish Energy Agency will send the upcoming energy island in the North Sea in tender, and here is a reclaimed island and a number of platforms around the island.

Ing.dk has asked the Danish Energy Agency why Denmark is aiming for a reclaimed island instead of platforms alone.

In an email, Deputy Director Mogens Hagelskær writes that the board has chosen a flexible island solution where both island and platforms will be erected.

»The exact design is prepared together with the winning bidder. By building an island, you secure more options both in terms of installation of technology and the possibility of innovation than if it is only platforms. '

He does not share the Dutch concern about whether it can be done fast enough.

"We see the platform solutions as good, where the need is known and relatively predictable, while the reclaimed island provides greater maneuvering room over the life, which we have set for at least 80 years for the Energiø North Sea."

"The same rationale is done in Belgium, where our colleagues in Elia are also in the process of building a permanent base for their energy island," Mogens Hagelskær writes in an email.

In Belgium, the system -responsible company, Alia, has announced in the autumn that one is aiming for an energy island in the style of the Danish one.

Title: LEDER Omtanke frem for politisk prestige: Ideen om en energiø må ikke stivne i beton
Full text:
It is fully understandable that ministers, in their eagerness to secure a good aftermath of the contemporary, seek the world's admiring look with prestige projects they put in the lake. Thus, it was a significant point in a digital meeting between US President Joe Biden and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen (S) in September 2021 that we "soon [will] make the world's first energy island a reality". And who wouldn't want to reap acknowledging nod from one of the most powerful people in the world?

The problem arises if the gaze, nod and recognition spin us into a lined world. Therefore, the need to ask completely banal questions. When it comes to the Energy Islands, there are several warning lights that glow and call for a re -visit of the project's design. In the agreement on the Energy Islands from June 2020, two energy islands were to be established. Already in February 2021 it was clear that there was really only one, as Energiø Bornholm is no longer an independent island. The fact that the remaining island comes 'soon' and should become the world's first - as the prime minister mentioned - also looks like a bright image of reality. The energy island in the North Sea is delayed at least from 2030 to 2033, and with the current supply crisis - we lack both professionals and components - it is a real question whether it can be reached. This week the engineer could tell about a Belgian energy island that is expected to be completed in 2026 and fully connected to the electricity network in 2030.

Most importantly, the question is whether it is a good idea at all with such an island. The basic idea of ​​an energy hub on Danish seabed is right: to connect more offshore wind farms to a hub rather than individually to land saves expensive cables. And it allows for easier to send electricity in the direction where the need is greatest and the kilowattime price best. When it blows a lot in November in the North Sea, but is poor in Southern Europe, we can send cheap energy there. But as the Dutch and the snuffy Germans have already fooled, this need can easily be solved with old -fashioned and far cheaper platforms of steel - a well -tested construction we know from production platforms to oil and gas.

The Germans also have a more sober look at what the nodes on the sea are actually to be used for. Professionals to the south state that the electricity from the offshore wind must be led ashore to be exploited here in an electricity -based society, secondary to the production of liquid fuels. At home, we stick to an idea of ​​the production of sustainable fuels in the North Sea. Thus, the argument from former Climate and Energy Minister Dan Jørgensen (S) was that the Danish concrete island also 'must' be able to accommodate technology for this production. Of course, you avoid not in my backyard problem far out to sea. But there are several weighty technical arguments for not placing PTX on an energy island. Up to a quarter of the energy born into PTX system turns into heat from the electrolysis process and the plant's compressors. It is by nature impossible to use the massive amounts of surplus heat for district heating if it is produced 80 km from land. Just as it is its case to transport hydrogen or fuels ashore.

Thus, an eco -construction risks becoming climate -ineffective with loss of surplus heat and a self -created unnecessary need for costly transport. In the analysis, it certainly also counts that it is not small money that is at stake. The eco -construction itself is stated to cost DKK 38 billion. In total, the assessment of the total construction sum of a staggering DKK 210 billion, and even before the project has been given a physical expression, the economy is stabbed. In the summer of 2020, it was a clear agreement that the energy islands should be profitable. Now the assessment reads that a significant deficit will occur.

According to the Danish Energy Agency, the expected return on investors has sounded four percent. It is so low a return that Professor Per Nikolaj Bukh, Aalborg University, has questioned why pension funds should put money in a Danish energy island if they can get double on wind turbines in other countries. Most recently, figures from the Danish Energy Agency show that a positive cash flow can be expected after six years. How to attract investors is unknown, but the supply of energy island is postponed this fall.

The good news is that the Danish Energy Agency has gone away from only betting on a larger fixed island with sand -filled concrete lowering boxes to also consider a less reclaimed island with associated steel platforms. But further steps need to be taken through that path: There is indisputable need to recalculate the project and explore alternatives, including whether there is a market for rental of areas for actors in power-to-x at sea. And whether steel platforms are both more profitable and sustainable.

The consultancy EY has designed campaign material for the board, where the painting does not leave anything to want: The island will be a 'Game Changing Concept' and 'Future-Proof'-in addition to the Danish state being highlighted as an 'Experienced business partner'. Experience we have quite right, but unfortunately not the good of the kind when it comes to leading the way with technological 'game-changing'. Just think of the debt recovery system EFI, the property valuation system, the train signals, the travel cards and the IC4 purchase, where we would also be a firstmover and self-develop from scratch. Historical experience indicates that it is no shame to stop, listen to others and scale down in time. Not even if it may not end up with the very same recognizing glances for ministers and idea men when cutting red cords.

The government has pointed out that there can also be room for a small hotel on the energy island. But even a good sea view can be purchased too expensive.

Title: Åben dør-ordning kan være EU-stridig: Styrelsen stopper vurdering af VE-ansøgninger
Full text:
The Danish Energy Agency is in the process of case management of 33 applications for setting up offshore wind turbines and other WE projects.

The open door scheme, which allows developers to establish a WE project in a self-selected area, may be in violation of EU law.

Therefore, the case processing of all 33 projects is put on hold, states a press release from the Danish Energy Agency.

It has promptly triggered furious outbreak from the industry.

"Completely unheard of," says the trade association Green Power Denmark's director Kristian Jensen, who in a press release calls it "a breach of Danish energy policy".

"A pure disaster for the green transition," DI-chief executive Lars Sandahl Sørensen told DI Business, while European Energy's Oatmeal Manager Andreas Karhula Lauridsen to EnergiWatch describes the decision as a completely "incomprehensible surprise."

"The government suddenly slams the door to the green transition in with a bang that sends shock waves throughout the green energy industry," Kristian Jensen said in the press release.

“The companies have done a great deal of preparation and are ready to build more green energy, and then the government is pulling the plug on the 'open door' scheme for 11 hours. It's simply not okay. It is a breach of the way we have historically driven energy policy in Denmark and create tremendous uncertainty about the green investments. "

The intervention occurs after an autumn where the Engineer has, among other things, uncovered how Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) and Ørsted use the scheme to bid on areas very close to the upcoming state Energiø Bornholm - so close that there may be a risk of the risk of The projects are going to cannibalize on the energy island's earnings - all due to an ambiguity in the rules of the scheme.

Would not miss billion earnings
The Engineer finds that officials of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply, the Ministry of Business and Finance have since this summer been looking for a management justification for closing the 'open door' scheme completely- apparently independent of the sitting ministers.

The state simply did not have to miss the large sums that it could potentially earn by sending the areas in question.

Here, in particular, there was a skeleton for the supply of Thor Havvindmøllepark, which triggered DKK 2.5 billion from all five applicants.

Several possible arguments have been turning up, such as That it could be state aid to share the state's seabed without getting any compensation.

As the argument on closer reflection turned out not to hold, the officials chose instead to bet on the argument that it does not hold a scheme based on the first-come, first-served principle, as it means that the area has not been exposed to competition , as it should.

And that is the argument that EU law has now been asked to relate to.

The fact that the Danish Energy Agency puts the case handling in the back of an industry that this summer got the chamber attorney's words that their applications were in accordance with the rules of the open door scheme.

The Danish Energy Agency believed that from July 2022 it would both gain full control over the scheme and at the same time restrict it. Because then a change of law for the scheme came into force that closes the possibility of sending open door applications on offshore wind parks, located more 15 km from the coast.

Open the door scheme suddenly popular
However, in the months of the change in the law, however, the board received a large number of applications via the open door scheme to establish very large WE projects on deep water far from the coast.

The board first tried to reject the applications on the grounds that the scheme was not intended for such large projects.

When the Attorney General shot down the argument, the Danish Energy Agency had to pass on the applications for assessment.

Bent Ole Gram Mortensen, a professor of public law at the University of Southern Denmark, points out that one must see the Board's intervention in the light of receiving a very large number of applications for large RIK projects in deep water last summer.

"The large number of applications must be held up against the fact that until then a few applications have been submitted to the scheme," says Bent Ole Gram Mortensen.

He does not know why the board chooses so drastically a step.

But one possibility is that the board will allow itself to coincide the applications via the open door scheme with the plans for the state energy islands and the national sea plan.

Another explanation could be that it would rather have a tendering procedure than the open door scheme now that it can be seriously possible to make money on offshore wind.

“It provides the opportunity to ensure that the state can harvest concession fees for the projects. After that, that is what is the motive of the board, I can only guess, ”he says.

If you listen to what Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard (M) says, it does not seem that he himself has been informed of or involved in the decision to put the open door scheme on hold.

For he calls the decision a "serious situation for the green transition" that offshore wind turbine projects.

"The specific situation raises a lot of questions about the consequences for the individual applications and the scheme to be clarified," Lars Aagaard said in a press release.

"I can assure that I am going to pursue quick answers to behalf of the applicants who are currently left in uncertainty about the future of their projects."

Title: Med statsstøtte til PtX kommer danskerne til at betale for rige nabolandes grønne omstilling
Full text:
The thoughtful thinking Kraka believes that the politicians' ambition for a massive expansion with PTX by 2030 may very well become a costly solution to the climate challenge.

It is a violent enterprise that takes place in these years when it comes to the production of green hydrogen and similar fuels.

What we are widely called PTX.

Gigantic facilities in Aalborg, Esbjerg, Fredericia and Avedøre are already on the drawing board, and on top of that comes a lot of smaller plants in Danish provincial cities.

Frederik Læsøe Nielsen, senior economist at Kraka Advisory, starts by emphasizing that he basically has no problem with companies that want to manufacture and sell PTX products on commercial terms.

If companies can get the business out of the public money boxes and deliver a product, whether it is hydrogen, methanol, ammonia or one of the more energy-heavy products like e-Jetfuel, then they just have to get started:

"But we are at Kraka skeptical of whether the state should send support crowns to such products," he says.

“First and foremost because PTX products are a very expensive way to solve the climate challenge right now. In other words, it is some of the fruits that sit at the highest in the tree that many focus on. We think the money is better spent elsewhere. "

Energiø is coupled with PTX
Kraka has just published the report 'Power-to-X can become a future climate solution, but contributes little to Danish climate goals' where the problem is reviewed.

The report has been prepared on the basis of a grant from the Novo Nordisk Foundation and with sparring from researchers at DTU.

“You should not dig very far into the argument for offshore wind and an energy island in the North Sea before the entire project is linked with PTX. It's as if the two things can't be separated. It also sounds intriguing that PTX can turn the energy when there is overproduction of power and acts as a kind of battery for the days when it is not blowing. It's almost as if they become each other's prerequisites. "

"But what's up and down in that story?" He asks rhetorically.

They have wondered well and thoroughly at Kraka, and on the basis of technical and financial calculations, there have been some conclusions that probably do not fall into good ground with some politicians, green organizations and commercial players.

Because if the political ambition, as shown in the new calculation changes from the Danish Energy Agency, is that Denmark must have 4-6 GW PTX in 2030, then Frederik Læsøe Nielsen and his colleagues believe that a lot of intermediate accounts will be skipped.

»PTX in that magnitude will in the short term give some very expensive CO2 reductions. It contradicts politicians' desire for us to take the most cost -effective technologies first, ”he states, pointing to a parallel desire to get rid of Russian gas in the European energy system.

Electrification is better than PTX
On top of that comes that all the electricity to be used for PTX could be used far more effectively if we prioritized electrifying all the places where possible first.

Here Kraka points to air traffic as one of the most obvious examples.

The previous government promised green air transport within a short number of years, and the easiest technology to reach that goal will be to use a liquid green fuel in traditional aircraft.

»But using green electricity to produce a synthetic jetfuel is both expensive and ineffective. At the same time, we just want to displace an oil -based fuel and not Russian gas, which we have otherwise also set in the light of the pending energy crisis and Europe's dependence on gas, ”says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

As a third point, Kraka points out that a large part of PTX production will go to export because domestic demand does not match the big PTX ambitions. Therefore, politicians should carefully consider the extent to which they want state aid PTX.

In practice, state aid means that Danish tax dollars are used to reduce the CO2 emissions in the customers - probably Germany and the Netherlands.

“Here we must again emphasize that if commercial players want to produce hydrogen or other products and sell it on market terms, then it is very fine. But when we hear from the hydrogen industry that infrastructure needs to be built so that we can export hydrogen to Germany, we may well be apprehensive, ”says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

However, he can imagine a solution where Energinet stands to build and operate a pipe network, while users pay all costs through taxes.

No benefit in being first
So far, DKK 1.25 billion has been allocated to develop PTX projects in Denmark as well as a number of million kroner through various support schemes.

But Kraka has calculated that if we are to reach a capacity of 6 GW by 2030, it will require investments of up to DKK 20 billion.

Since the products that come from the PTX plants are likely to be more expensive than fossil alternatives, Kraka presupposes that it will require state aid if the plants are to be erected.

Now we have for a number of years provided grants for the production of biogas, which has led to a huge increased production. Shouldn't we also do it with hydrogen?

“There is a big difference between biogas and hydrogen in this context. We have developed biogas to get domestic security of supply as an alternative to our consumption of natural gas. The same can also be said about the electricity supply, where we must ensure that the citizens have electricity in the outlet. But there is not a domestic demand for hydrogen or other PTX products that can defend a capacity of 4-6 GW. "

But cannot the expansion of PTX in Denmark lead to other beneficial effects? For example, the development of a new industry and thus high -tech jobs?

“Here we must probably separate things in commercial interests and social economics. It is clear that there are commercial companies who would like to start and have an interest in being the best so that they can export to the rest of the world. But then we are back at some of the other arguments, namely that it is expensive reductions and that PTX will seize very large quantities of green electricity that we should use elsewhere. "

Wasn't that what we just did with the wind power extension in the 90s, ie gave a production grant so that companies could build a market and grow?

“I don't think you can compare with the wind power extension. For already, there is a great deal of appetite for building PTX. But of course it is a legitimate political argument to believe that we must be a pioneering country and from a political point of pushing for a technology development. But it is difficult to put crowns and ears on how much a Danish state aid will increase the likelihood of Danish technology companies' products becoming financially attractive to the rest of the world. "

Isn't it important that we are first so that others do not come and take over the market?

“One can argue that if our wind resources give us a competitive advantage in the production of PTX products, it is not important whether Denmark is the first to produce it on a large scale. Denmark should probably join the wagon - state aid or not. Thus, Kraka will in no way encourage actively stop the many PTX projects that are currently in the mold around Denmark, but one must carefully consider whether it is the right way to go to actively push the development given that situation. , We are in right now, ”says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

Title: Minister baner vej for 9 GW havvind i år – og møllerne skal måske stå tættere
Full text:
The smoke has barely laid after the misery with the open door scheme, before the minister now announces the initiation of state tendering of 9 GW offshore winds this year.

Minister of Energy Lars Aagaard (M) will this year start the supply of 9 GW offshore winds by 2030, which will help ensure that the ambitions of 12.9 GW of offshore wind in 2030 will be fulfilled.

It will be a five -fold of Denmark's current capacity and corresponds to electricity consumption for about nine million households.

It announces the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply in a press release on Monday, just as the smoke from the open door scheme has barely settled, after the Danish Energy Agency on February 6 paused the scheme on the basis of an assessment that the scheme may be in violation with EU law.

“We need to have a quick clarification on the open door applications, and that is our top priority here and now. But beyond that, we must also look at what we can do to turn up the expansion of offshore winds through state tenders, ”says Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard in the press release.

Mill density must be examined
In January, the Engineer could tell that, internally in the Danish Energy Agency, it is concerned about whether "the space with the space" is being made at the erection of offshore wind turbines, because they are generally located at a greater distance than in other European countries.

The Danish Energy Agency started to investigate whether there can be gains by packing both wind turbines and parks closer.

In the press release, the ministry writes how to give the sets the freedom to set up more offshore winds on the offered areas at sea.

To Ritzau, the minister says a densification could potentially lead to a greater capacity than the nine gigawatts that are being tendered this year.

“Our assessment is that you can. That is, potentially, if we can make a proper model, and the Folketing is involved in it, then it will be my expectation that we can also get more than the nine gigawatts, ”Lars Aagaard told Ritzau.

However, to the engineer, senior researcher at DTU Wind energy Xiaoli Guo Larsén warned that one must be careful about concluding that more wind turbines necessarily lead to greater capacity.

“The problem is that by increasing turbine density, you also automatically increase costs. At the same time, the efficiency of the wind farms is reduced because the mills create more turbulence, and at the same time steal winds apart - together called wake effects, ”Xiaoli Guo Larsén pointed out.

We are missing power to Power-to-X
Green Power Denmark praises the government for starting the tender, but at the same time calls for the open door scheme.

“We lack green power today and tomorrow. The nine gigawatts of offshore winds are important to our climate ambitions, but we need the offshore wind farms under the open door scheme if Denmark is to become a pioneering country within Power-to-X. Here we cannot wait until the state offshore wind farms are in operation by 2030. For at that time, other countries will long ago sit on the market for green fuels for heavy transport, ”says Green Power Denmark CEO Kristian Jensen.

The tones also sound from Dansk Industri.

“I am glad to see that we have a government that is drawn into work clothes and is working to find solutions to the challenges we are facing at the moment. This applies to the open-door scheme and other large green projects. The open-door scheme and the state tenders on offshore wind can together give Denmark a huge boost, ”says Lars Sandahl Sørensen, CEO of Dansk Industri.

The 9 GWs that the government will start tendering this year includes Energiø Bornholm, Hesselø and another 5 GW offshore wind projects, the ministry writes in the press release.

Title: Vindø-konsortiet: En fast energiø er både billigere og bedre end platforme
Full text:
One of the consortia that expects to offer the energy island of the North Sea has no doubt what it prefers.

It is now almost three years since the idea of ​​an energy island 80 kilometers out in the North Sea was announced in connection with the climate agreement from June 22, 2020.

Great visualizations, discussions for and against the island and a number of specific questions have characterized the debate since then:

Should it be a big or small island?
Should there be electrolysis on the island?
Why not put converter stations on platforms?
And how should the energy from the island be part of the electricity market across the connected countries?

Specifically, the Danish Energy Agency says that the energy island in the North Sea must be established as an artificial island with platforms.

By 2033, it must be a hub for 3-4 GW of offshore wind farms. By 2040, the island will have a capacity of 10 GW.

To the attentive reader, two things have changed since the original plan from the climate agreement:

The commissioning time has been pushed from 2030 to 2033, and then 'with platforms' has been added.

At the same time, Denmark is not the only nation that intends to build a large wind turbine capacity in the North Sea.

In the 'Esbjerger Declaration', the government leaders from Denmark, Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands signed an agreement to build 65 GW of offshore wind in 2030 and increase capacity to at least 150 GW by 2050.

Already, it seems that the countries are choosing different strategies.

The German system responsible company AMPRION has chosen a solution with converter stations on platforms for two upcoming offshore wind farms.

The Dutch also immediately seems to focus on platform solutions, while the Belgians hold on to a solid energy island.

CIP is betting on an island
Several consortia have signed up on the course to offer the Danish Energiø, which has now also added 'platform' to the description.

Furthermore, you can now see a visualization on the Danish Energy Agency website with info about the energy island, which shows a solid energy with platforms located around it.

One of the consortia that expects to offer the task is Vindø, which has CIP (Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners) at the forefront. In addition, the pension companies PensionDanmark and PFA and the electricity distribution company share.

To stand for the actual construction of the energy island, the consortium has entered into an agreement with the companies Boskalis, Deme and MT Højgaard International, who together have the expertise to build an artificial island in the North Sea, says Thomas Dalsgaard, a partner in CIP.

Why hold on to an artificial island when, for example, the Germans have decided to build platforms, among other things to get started quickly?

“Now we have spent three years thinking about the energy islands and have come up with some crucial points: First of all, we will have to think differently if we are to have offshore wind farms on a new scale. It will be too expensive if we are to connect the parks 'point-to-point'. Here is a fixed energy island with room for electrolysis the best solution, ”he says in an interview with the Engineer.

In the Danish Energy Agency's latest material, the possibility of platforms has been added around the islands. Wouldn't it be able to give the flexibility that you need and the opportunity to get started quickly?

“It's not because we've been staring blind to regular islands and can't see other solutions. We have actually established platforms in the German part of the North Sea, so we know how cumbersome and expensive it is. We know from our partners in the consortium that once the permit is there, they can build an island of about three years. It's hard to imagine that platforms can be done faster. Therefore, we think it will be unnecessarily expensive and complex to set up platforms around the energy island. At the same time, it's hard to imagine that we will build electrolysis on platforms. "

If hydrogen production is to be done on an island, will we not lose the possibility of utilizing the waste heat for district heating?

»Calculations we have made ourselves, and analyzes from both EA Energy Analysis and COWI show that we can save about 20 percent of the cost of building electrolysis directly on the island - even if we cannot utilize the surplus heat for district heating. This is partly due to the fact that it is far cheaper to put a hydrogen tube to land than an electric cable. At the same time, we get a more flexible production mix and better capacity utilization of the cables to land because we can constantly choose between sending electricity or hydrogen ashore. "

Critics have recently pointed out that production of hydrogen on an energy island may risk draining the treasury for reimbursement crowns because the products are not sent to Denmark, but are instead sold to rich European neighboring countries. Where do you think hydrogen should be brought ashore?

“The hydrogen must first and foremost be sent to where there is a market. It can be Denmark, but it can also be Germany or the Netherlands, for example Rotterdam. So we're going to look at what hydrogen infrastructure is under construction. If the hydrogen is sent directly to Central Europe, then state aid may not be needed for that production. "

In the summer of 2022, the supply was pushed for 12 months, so it is now expected that it will only be ready from the Danish Energy Agency in the earlier autumn 2023. When do you expect an island to be ready?

“Once we have seen a tender, it will probably take about 2.5 years before a final winner is appointed. From there, in addition to environmental permit and detailed design, we expect to spend three years building the island itself. The challenge is that no one has done it before, so it's not a service you just go out and buy. Then wind turbines, converter stations will be built and cables, so if we believe in a conservative timeline, then we are probably around 2031-2032. In fact, we don't think that can be done faster if you choose platforms. "

Title: Belgierne er allerede godt i gang med at bygge verdens første energiø
Full text:
The Belgian state has assigned a consortium the task of building an artificial energy island in the Norse Lake. The construction will start in 2024 and will take 2.5 years.

The Belgian energy authority Elia plans to install 3.5 GW wind turbines in a new area of ​​the Belgian part of the North Sea.

Therefore, in order to collect the energy from the wind turbines and send it ashore via direct current, an energy island must be built.

Now a consortium consisting of the companies DEME and Jan de Zero, both of which are experts in offshore constructions, have been tasked with building the island.

Only when the island is built will Elia installed electrical equipment such as transformers and converter stations.

The island, which has been named Princess Elisabeth Island, will be 45 km off the Belgian coast and will have an area of ​​about 24,000 square meters. In addition to all the electrical equipment, there must be room for a helicopter platform and a small harbor.

Thus, there is no prospect that the island will also house spare parts for the wind farms, PTX plants or housing for staff.

It is planned that the energy island connects the Belgian system with other countries in Northern Europe, for example Denmark via the cable called Tritonlink, which has been planning for a number of years.

Britain can be connected via the cable called Nautilus. In this way, Belgium can be part of the overall plan for the North Sea, where by 2050 there is a prospect of up to 300 GW of wind power.

Concrete lowering box and sand
The construction itself will consist of an outer wreath of concrete lowering boxes filled with sand.

It is expected that the actual construction of the island will start in 2024 and be completed in the summer of 2026. After that, the island will be linked to the upcoming offshore wind farms in the North Sea.

Plans have already been approved to build wind turbines with a total capacity of 2.3 GW in an area in the Belgian part of the North Sea.

The new Energiø will be built in connection with a new area called Princess Elisabeth Zone. The area covers about 285 square kilometers and the capacity here can be expanded to 3.5 GW.

Princess Elisabeth Island is expected to be associated with the wind farms and the Belgian electricity system by 2030.

With the new agreement, Belgium Denmark comes in advance with the world's first energy island.

The Danish plans are that the supply for an energy island in the North Sea will only be published in September this year.

According to the Danish Energy Agency, it is expected that a Danish energy in the North Sea will be ready in 2033.

Title: Storstilede danske PtX-ambitioner kan blive forhalet af mangel på ingeniører
Full text:
Thousands of Stem competencies are needed to realize the many ambitious PTX projects, according to the head of the CAPEX research center.

It does not lack announcements of large power-to-X projects (PTX) in the whole country.

But one is great ambitions on paper, another to make them come true.

This requires, among other things, a nice build-up of STEM competencies at a time when there is already a massive lack of engineers, says the assessment of the CAPEX research center, among others.

"In the long term, several thousand experts will be needed who can help accelerate the green transition in connection with PTX in Denmark," says Tejs Vegge, professor at DTU Energy and center manager at CAPEX.

The estimate is based on a concoction of political and industrial announcements, how the technologies can be scaled and what competencies should be brought into play.

“It may sound like a large number, and that's because we count broadly. From the researchers at the universities to the R&D engineers sitting in the companies and developing and producing the materials, those who build the electrolysis cells and stacks and ultimately those who need to test and implement the technologies, for example, on the energy islands, ”says Tejs Vegge.

'Outdated' engineers are getting hot again
For Preben Birr-Pedersen, specialist in energy technologies and especially PTX and CCUS (catch, storage and use of CO2), there is no doubt that the hydrogen community is right at the door-something he himself has shouted for the last 20 years.

He estimates that technology has happened more in the last three years than in the previous 17.

“We do not have the voice skills in place-and it is really in the whole value chain. It is also with the authorities that have to deal with the projects. There is a great time with all actors, including also the Danish Security Agency, the Danish Environmental Protection Agency and out in the municipalities, because otherwise the permit processes will take too long, ”he says.

Among the 'traditional' engineering subjects, Preben Birr-Pedersen mentions, among other things, strong current engineers, process engineers and oil engineers as important profiles in the upcoming PTX landscape.

He claims that 'the last twenty years' have been missing strong current engineers, nor do the oil engineers hang on the trees.

Title: Rambøll i grøn vækst: »Jeg er stolt af de store transformationsprojekter«
Full text:
In 2022, the consulting engineering company won many large projects pushing the world in a more sustainable direction. Still, resources are also used on all the small steps that the group can help individual companies take.

The largest plastic sorting plant in the Nordic region in Esbjerg, a new urban neighborhood around Stockholm Central Station, electrification of the German railway, a green infrastructure project to storm the coast of New York and climate -neutral office buildings in Manchester.

2022 offered a wide range of new tasks for the consulting engineering company Ramboll, which in February last year launched a new strategy targeted future partnerships on projects that are changing the world in a sustainable direction.

And the financial statements, which were published on Friday, show that that strategy has borne fruit. In any case, the group has made a turnover of 12.6 per cent. greater than last year, and the greatest organic growth in 14 years.

"A very satisfactory result," says CEO Jens-Peter Saul, who is convinced that there is a connection between the result and the sustainable focus.

'Of course, it happens thanks to the classic sustainable services we are leading, e.g. within offshore wind. But also a new area such as our strategic sustainability advice, which is part of our management Consulting unit, has really started the growth, ”says the CEO.

Not just theoretical documents
The Management Consulting business takes the driver's jersey as the area that had the greatest growth by 2022-of 21.4 per cent. The unit has been part of Ramboll for many years, but for the past year and a half, the Group has been aiming for advising both public and private companies in strategic sustainability - e.g. about navigating the EU's taxonomy and developing strategies for sustainable transition with effects such as fewer emissions and a more circular business model - and this has produced results. 

Management Consulting business has been part of Ramboll for many years but the latest
A year and a half, the Group has been charged with advising both public and private companies within
Strategic sustainability - e.g. About to navigate the EU's taxonomy 

So far, the business has primarily been focused in Denmark and Germany, but Jens-Peter Saul says that Ramboll is now expanding to the UK, Sweden, Norway, Finland and the USA.

“Customers appreciate that we show the way and work with them on how their sustainability challenges can be solved. You can easily make a lot of theoretical documents that can eject themselves in a drawer, but more and more people are choosing to involve the full, holistic expertise in the form of our engineers and economists who both help design the strategies and perform them, ' says Jens-Peter Saul.

An example of such a company is the Danish construction group Aarsleff, which is helped to screen whether they comply with the requirements of the EU's new CSRD directive. At the same time, Ramboll's Management Consultants Aarsleff helps to analyze whether the company's financial activities comply with the EU's rules on when economic activities are environmentally and socially sustainable.

All steps count
The sharpened focus on saying yes to projects with sustainable solutions within eg. offshore wind, PTX, climate adaptation and sustainable construction are well suited to Ramboll's core values, believes the CEO, who is satisfied with the big projects Ramboll won last year.

»The big lighthouse projects are good to show up to journalists like you, and of course I am proud of the major transformation projects where you can really see that we are moving society in a positive direction-it can be railway electrification, a PTX system or energy islands . But one should not be mistaken for all projects to influence the world in a more sustainable direction, ”says Jens-Peter Saul, stating that all projects do not have to be about, for example, completely CO2-neutral buildings:

“There are many projects where we can influence the world through our daily commitment, and you can say that every little step on the journey counts. It also matters if we can help someone reduce their CO2 emissions by just 20 per cent. "

Sustainable tools at hand
That approach has not only raised the Management Consulting business, but now characterizes the entire group. Thus, over 4,000 Ramboll staff last year was further trained in sustainability at the company's internal sustainability academy, The Sustainability Training Universe, which is still under development.

Here they learn e.g. To advise customers on how to reduce CO2 emissions with its material selection, how to recycle materials, make LCA calculations and think sustainability already in the design process.

"In this way, we complement the general understanding of what it takes to become more sustainable, with our engineers also having the methods and tools at hand to actually implement it," says the CEO.

But even though the engineers have been given more sustainable methods and tools at hand, it does not mean that there are enough hands to fulfill the coming year's ambitions. After the Management Consulting area, energy was the area that grew most with its 13.8 per cent by 2022, and Jens-Peter Saul's stated target for 2023 is first and foremost to accelerate the growth there.

Do you think it will succeed?

“The question is rather how fast we can succeed. It is very much about how we can retrain engineers so that they can take work in that sector instead of their current. Because as it seems now, the growth is going to be so strong that in some areas we have to say no to customers because we are fully booked. So we will obviously have to look at how we can scale up and equip people to move into energy advice. "

Title: SYNSPUNKT Åben dør-ordning: Afpolitisering er vejen ud af krisen for havvind
Outlet:
Ingeniøren
Otto Brøns-Petersen, analysechef i Cepos
Full text:
It has aroused a significant stir that the state has so far set the use of the so-called open door scheme for offshore wind turbines. The stakeholders have put considerable pressure to clarify the EU legal problem that led the government to pull the plug.

But there is reason to revise the entire policy of renewable energy, which is characterized by harmful and expensive politicization. The basic problem-also behind the EU case-is that the energy sector is steeped in political desire to control the development, often encouraged by strong interest groups and with symbolic policy manifestations.

It is not possible to determine for us from the outside whether the stop for open door is well -founded or expressions of the officials' overlooking. Specifically, the Danish Energy Agency and the State Aid Secretariat in the Ministry of Business Affairs have assessed that there is a risk of violating the EU's state aid rules.

So far, wind energy has received two forms of support. One is not to be loaded by the full costs that wind energy inflicts on the rest of the electricity grid and the energy system. Wind energy requires great backup capacity, net capacity and in the future also storage options when the Norwegian water magazines for hydropower no longer reach as 'battery'.

The other is in the form of production support for electricity. The level of support is determined by tenders, so that the investor, which requires the least in support, is allowed to build the offshore wind farms decided politically. This support includes the parks sent in tender. The open door scheme, on the other hand, means that one can apply for permission to erect wind turbines that are not decided politically, but without getting production support.

So far, it has not been lucrative. But now technological development and competition have led to the sign of tendering. We have got investors who are willing to pay to build the parks. The willingness to pay partly reflects the benefit of the indirect support and partly that the windplaces at sea are scarce. In the same way that the windplaces are also on the land where investors pay the landowners for the right to raise the mills.

This development has also made open door-mill interesting and the applications have flowed in. Authorities' concern is now on whether the free access in the open door constitutes illegal state aid when the winners of tenders have to pay. Of course, it can also play a role that the interest in participating in tenders on the political prestige projects can evaporate if access to open door is free.

Basically, there is a need to create good, neutral framework conditions for renewable energy, so that commercial decisions and socio -economic considerations become coincidental. The extension of renewable energy should be done on market conditions without political governance and without other state aid other than the favor of fossil competitors paying a high price to deduce CO2.

First, it is important to run the indirect support completely and ensure that the tariffs for wind turbine power manufacturers contain all derived costs for backup capacity, net capacity, etc. Secondly, the wind energy should be decided. Ideally, all planned tenders should be canceled, including the energy islands, and at least no new ones should be planned. Third, a consistent pricing of the sea areas, which reflects the scarcity, should be ensured. Exactly as the land is priced.

Far along the way, the handling of the scarce oil and gas deposits in the North Sea can serve as inspiration. There are largely identical issues. In both cases, the right to utilize the scarce spaces at sea generates a so -called basic rate. The most far -reaching step would be simply to abolish the supply and allow the utilization to drive the commercial use of open door. If the tenders are still maintained, it should be like in the North Sea, where the tender rounds are about organizing the expansion, not to control production according to political targets (the same cannot be said of the political agreement to run the North Sea production, including not holding more tender rounds).

In the North Sea, tendering rounds and open die side by side without conflicting with state aid rules, because a uniform payment is charged in the form of hydrocarbon taxation. The hydrocarbon taxation is approximately a tax on the basic rate and thus solves the pricing problem on the underground. It is really a payment to utilize the occurrences of scarce resources. There is nothing in principle in the way of incorporating offshore wind turbines on the state's areas under hydrocarbon taxation.

An alternative to letting the basic rate accrue to the state is to let the companies utilize the land that come first. In that case, the basic rate will accrue to the investors in question, but if the rights can be translated, it will also price the scarcity. However, it will require that the basic rate will not be eaten by the race to come first and that it is credible that no special taxes will be introduced anyway. Otherwise, it may be appropriate to get the tax regime in place from the start and possibly with clauses that protect against subsequent special taxes, as is also known from the North Sea.

In any case, the energy sector is too important for the massive current politicization. The division of labor between politicians and the commercial actors should be that the first sets neutral frameworks and with socio -economically healthy incentives, and that private operators fill them without political retail control or state aid.

Title: Vandkøling vinder frem i datacentre: Global Connect sænker servere direkte ned i væske
Full text:
For the first time, Immersion Cooling is taken, where servers are lowered directly into liquid, in use in a Danish co-location data center.

"You can just lower your camera into the liquid," calls Luke Davies, data center manager at the Nordic Data Center Giant Global Connect.

We are in a large white space in Høje Taastrup, where Global Connect in the neighboring rooms runs a large data center.

The room is hundreds of square meters large and is virtually completely empty, except what looks like four large connected bathtubs in a corner, which together reach 20-25 square meters.

They are not purchased for relaxation or spa experiences for the employees.

They should be used to cool hardworking servers using so -called immersive cooling - also known as submerged cooling or sunken cooling.

The liquid is mixed with a mineral oil that ensures that the liquid conducts the heat away but is not electrically conductive.

So you do not get a shock by sticking your fingers down to a lit server.

“You can actually drink it, but it's not something I would recommend. The texture is reminiscent of baby oil, ”says Luke Davies.


As heavy processors and graphics cards for, for example, artificial intelligence are emerging, the need for more efficient cooling increases, and here the Immersion Cooling is at the forefront.

"Immersive Cooling is aimed at the servers that run the most intense work tasks, such as AI, AutoCAD rendering or major meteorological analyzes," explains Luke Davies.

Increased computing increases the need for cooling
Today, most of the cooling takes place with air, either as a free cooling or compressor cooling.

This is also how the rest of Global Connect's data center in Høje Taastrup is cooled down.

It will also be in the future, because it is a relatively cheap method.

Even with high efficiency on the fluid cooling also comes higher costs. Therefore, so far, only the most work -intensive tasks are suitable for the new type of fluid cooling.

Global Connect today has 17 large data center sites in the Nordic countries and a large number of small servers sites.

The majority is cooled with air, either free cooling or compressor cooling depending on the outdoor temperature.

It is Global Connect's ambition that all 17 large sites offer Immersion Cooling over the next few years.

While the processors themselves in the heart of the servers are regularly upgraded with multiple transistors in less space, the cooling technologies do not follow in the same way with automatic.

However, most people agree that fluid will take over air cooling.

The question is how quick the conversion is going to take.

“Moore's law means that computing power will continue to rise in the coming years, which is why the need for cooling is also rising. Our investment in Immersive Cooling gives a clue as to how we think the next generation cooling will look, ”says Anders Frich Mathiesen, who is responsible for the operation of Global Connect's data centers and has been responsible .

When shaking the bag and putting new technologies into operation, side gains can occur. When removing the moving parts on a server, eg the fan, the electronics are also not worn out in the same way.

"We expect a lifetime that is 20 percent longer than standard systems," says Anders Frich Mathiesen.

»Besides the blower to be removed - and you are sure that the server does not fail because it misses a fan - there is not much other adjustment, besides the extra neighborhood servers need to drip off when lifted out of the water bath. ""

According to Global Connect, power consumption to cool serve directly in liquid up to 90 percent lower compared to conventional air cooling.

When the cooling is more efficient, the electronics can also be pressed maximum without the risk of overheating.

"For example, you can overdue your servers by 25 percent, and it can pay off financially," says Anders Frich Mathiesen.

Each vessel is on larger with a smaller server rack.

»Because you can load your electronics more, the performance gets higher. If you need to run the chat bot Chatgpt, it today requires a large data center of 15,000 square meters if you are running with a standard air cooling. We can do that with 10 vessels, ”says Luke Davies.

Heat pump at the end of the road
Today, the surplus heat from many Danish data centers disappears into the air.

Later in the year, Global Connect's data center in Høje Taastrup will be connected to the district heating network.

However, fluid cooling is better at integrating directly into the district heating network because the temperature can be squeezed higher.

»Liquid just leads heat better than air, which is why we can cool more efficiently. This means that we can deliver the cooling water with a temperature above 40 degrees with Immersion Cooling, while we do not get above 30 degrees by air cooling, ”says Luke Davies.

Does not require special hardware
In Denmark, the North Jutland data center company Asetek has for a number of years supplied water cooling solutions, where the surplus heat is moved into the district heating network.

Here the water is pumped around around encapsulated processors and the electronics do not come directly in contact with the water. It also provides high efficiency but requires special hardware.

“We supply co-location data centers, which means that our customers bring their own servers themselves, and then we take care of the infrastructure. Therefore, we need to be able to handle all types of servers and not just specially designed hardware, ”says Luke Davies.

Although it intuitively seems completely wrong to lower electronics into liquid and turn on the on-button, it is actually a perfectly legitimate way to use its equipment that does not break neither warranty nor insurance policy.

Before the Global Connect, the Immersive Cooling system purchased, they contacted a number of the major server manufacturers, such as Dell, HP and Micrologic, to hear what they are thinking about lowering their hardware into fluid.

“It turned out that they already have insurance policies that include immersive cooling. It gave us a belief in the solution, 'says Luke Davies.

The Immersive Cooling solution is provided by American Green Revolution Cooling. Global Connect was the first to demand redundancy in the system, so it is custom built for the solution in Høje Taastrup.

If a heat exchanger goes down in a tub, another is ready to take over without the servers shutting down due to lack of cooling.

In a more radical version of water cooling, Microsoft has become known for packing a data center in a container that they have dumped on the bottom of the sea off Scotland.

»Most data center customers want to be close to key fiber connections, which is why data centers on the sea's bottom are not so obvious. But it is obvious to explore the possibilities in connection with the upcoming energy island in the North Sea, ”says Luke Davies.

Today, the fluid cooling solution is used largely only by large Enterprise customers with their own data centers, by professional cryptominers or the military.

“It's new that co-location is trying this type of fluid cooling. In this industry, you must constantly be one step ahead with rooms that are completely empty, which can be ready for new solutions, ”says Luke Davies.

Green Revolution Cooling, which is behind the Immersion Cooling solution, announced a great collaboration with Intel on the development of fluid cooling last year.

But in connection with a larger savings round at Intel, a large development center for four billion Danish kroner has been looped, and therefore it is currently uncertain whether Intel will in future bet on fluid cooling.

Title: Energiø Nordsøen udvider til 4 GW: Energinet godkender elinfrastrukturen
Full text:
The blue stamp made by Energinet's Group Board is seriously launching the feasibility studies.

The two business cases for the upcoming electricity infrastructures for Energiø Bornholm and the North Sea have now been approved by the Group Board in Energinet, an access to documents shows. 

It pleases the company's Deputy Director Hanne Storm Edlefsen. 

“For us it's a milestone. It is an important thing with the approvals because at the same time it is a blue stamp of the projects that we can now start. The politicians wanted us to start the projects early before they matured completely so that we can reach the political ambitions, ”says Hanne Storm Eldlefsen. 

She says that the two approvals are now pushing the preliminary investigations for the two projects. 

In addition, it gives Energinet green light to talk to the citizens of the affected local areas and to prepare the market and talk more in depth with Belgium about what is needed to establish an upcoming connection to Energiø North Sea. 

It is in line with the agreement that Energinet landed with the German authorities in the fall. 

Awaiting signature from minister
Lars Aagaard (M) has, as the Minister of Climate and Supply, approved the business case for Energi Bornholm, which thus lives up to the requirements of §4 under the Energinet Act that the Minister is stamping projects over a certain caliber. 

The next step will be to get Energiø North Sea through the same needle eye. 

»The same will happen to Energiø North Sea. We have landed an agreement with the Belgians on the North Sea. So right now the business case is ready for signature inside the minister's desk. The access to documents shows that the Group Board has also approved an application from Energinet to expand the capacity for Energiø North Sea from 3 GW to 4 GW in the first phase, which is scheduled to be completed in 2033. 

Energinet has applied for it in an attempt to achieve a better social economy that has previously been questioned. 

According to the material, such an expansion will require Energinet to increase the capacity of the energy island's connection to Jutland as well as the transformer plant in Revsing from 1.4 GW to 2 GW.
