Many risks and great uncertainties
The permit to expand is granted on the condition that the politicians in Christiansborg approve it. And that has not yet happened, the ministry told the Engineer. 

It will probably only happen in the time up to the ministry initiating the supply of the island itself. 

Whether it is realized depends, among other things. of whether the social economy of the two islands looks reasonable. And here the ministry is currently holding the cards close to the body.

“We have not yet started spending the big money and made agreements on deliveries. We will only do that later. At that time, we also expect to update the decision -making basis if it turns out to come to big changes to business cases, ”says Hanne Storm Eldlefsen.

And such changes will be very likely. In a letter from July last year, Energinet writes to the ministry that "the business case has been prepared with significantly greater uncertainties and risks than for traditional infrastructure projects, which is why Energinet will update the Business Case's decision basis on an ongoing basis if it proves necessary."

A business case is the management tool in the project that documents the business impact of the project's deliveries. In addition, the business case contains information that justifies the project from start to finish.

Title: Atomkraft lurer i kulissen: Stort behov for grøn el udfordrer Sverige
Full text:
Closing electricity generation and great distances present completely different challenges in Sweden than we have in Denmark.

Stable electricity supply is Sweden's pride.

For over 50 years, ample approach of CO2-neutral water and nuclear power has been king.

Unlike Denmark, coal and oil are a special sight when it comes to electricity generation, and primarily used for peak and reserve load works.

Neither is natural gas particularly widespread, and a single natural gas pipeline on the Swedish west coast stood by 2020 for just three percent of energy imports.

Hydroelectric, on the other hand, was expanded throughout the 20th century, especially in the mountain rates of central Sweden, so that the capacity has been on stable 10,000 MW over the past many years.

In the late 1960s, nuclear power comes on the field with stable electricity supply from up to 12 reactors at four power plant sites.

The total capacity fluctuates in the 1980s up to 11,000 MW.

Today, there are six reactors left with a total capacity of 6,885 MW.

Overall, hydropower and nuclear power today supply about 60 percent of Sweden's electricity generation of just over 180 TWh, while the rest comes from wind power, biomass and a bit of solar cells.

Fortunately, the Swedes still have a surplus of electricity on an annual basis, as consumption today is around 140 TWh.

Especially 220 kV high voltage connections from the hydroelectric are moving energy towards the Stockholm area, and a 400 KV system ties nuclear power in southern Sweden with the rest of the country.

North is consumption sparing as the industries are few and the former mining was especially based on fossil solutions.

The industry provides electric boom
But the winds of change are blowing.

Like Denmark and the rest of Northern Europe, Sweden faces violent electrification.

"In total, we think we will come up with a consumption of 290 TWH in 2045," says Tobias Edfast, the unit manager for grid development in the Swedish energy authority Svenska Kraftnät:

“It is first and foremost in the industry that we see a huge need for electricity. A very large part of this consumption will be in Northern Sweden, and it will have a huge impact on how we are expanding the transmission network in the future, ”he says, emphasizing that although Sweden is today a net exporter of electricity seen on an annual basis, it is Expected that there will be a deficit of electricity generation within relatively few years.

Nor has it helped that the nuclear reactors that have been closed, including at the Barsebäck Power Plant, are in southern Sweden.

Specifically for Northern Sweden, the problem is particularly great. There are no opportunities to expand with more hydropower, and therefore large wind farms are especially seen in the mountains. There are already plans for many thousands of MW wind turbines on land, but it is very uncertain whether they turn into something as the protests are already pouring up.

Conversion of EnergiFlow
Sweden is divided into four price areas from north to south: SE1 to SE4. And the difference in production capacity and the need to transfer energy between the price areas is changing rapidly.

“We are facing a major transformation of the energy flow between the different areas of Sweden. Consumption is changing and we can see that more wind power is coming in the north and more solar cells in the south, ”says Tobias Edfast.

In Northern Sweden, there are companies like Northvolt in Skellefteå that will produce batteries for electric cars, H2Greensteel in the booth that will produce 'green' steel, and the mining company LKAB, which breaks iron ore in Kiruna and Malmberget, which will be responsible for increased electricity consumption .

So where the energy was previously secured with stable production in the south (SE4), the closure of Barsebäck has meant that reinforcement must now also be made:

“Conversely, we also see that in the slightly longer term there will be a need to get more energy transported to the north. On top of that, many of the existing 400 kV connections have reached their lifetime and need to be replaced. This is especially true of those on the west coast down to Denmark, ”says Tobias Edfast.

Need for new cables
Precisely towards Denmark, there are also new challenges, because within a number of years, both the cables for Jutland and Zealand must be renewed if the transfer capacity is to be maintained. The connection to Bornholm constitutes a special case as the island is given the status of 'Energiø'.

Meanwhile, Svenska Kraftnät, together with the German system manager, 50Hertz, is in the process of building a 700 MW connection directly to Germany, which will be ready in 2029.

But where in Denmark there is a lot of talk about PTX, it is not really something that the Swedes spend so much time on, says Tobias Edfast:

"Right now it's mostly about getting hydrogen for steel and cement production and perhaps in connection with offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea, so that's not where the focus is today," he says.

On the other hand, a discussion has begun to bubble about new nuclear power on the basis of Sweden's prospect of having a very specific deficit of electricity generation within the next 10 years:

“We can see a movement in both the power plant industry and society against the fact that it has again become ok to discuss new nuclear power in Sweden. It is especially the power plant Vattenfall that has begun to look at the possibilities, but we are still in a very early phase and it is therefore uncertain whether we are talking about lifetime extension of existing nuclear power plants, new traditional works or the smaller SMRs, ”he says .

What is certain, however, is that Sweden - like most other Northern European countries - faces a huge challenge when it comes to labor to implement all the many projects that have already been started:

»This applies to all links in the process, from the first environmental analyzes and technical analyzes to project management and specialists. And of course we must have suppliers who are able to supply components and equipment, ”says Tobias Edfast.

Therefore, Svenska Kraftnät also does not see any prospect that prices for electricity will fall significantly in the coming time.

Title: Fra næsten ingenting til lidt mere: Metode forbedrer atmosfærisk CO2-fangst
Full text:
A study in the Science Advance presents the method of catching the atmosphere's CO2, which among other things makes the sea possible storage space.

According to the Climate Council, it is still quite uncertain whether the catch of the atmosphere's CO2 in the future will be a technical and financial opportunity.

Large-scale system for Direct Air Capture (DAC) is not yet available, and the largest plant only catches about 4,000 tonnes of CO2 annually.

This corresponds to about 533 average dancers' annual emissions.

In other words, there is room for improvement, and that is exactly what researchers from Lehigh University have made a bid for.

In a scientific article in Science Advances, they present a new method of capturing the CO2 of the atmosphere that can absorb 5.0 moles of CO2 per kilogram absorbing material.

The researchers are based on amin-based materials, which are often used for CO2 catch. But by adding copper to the material, they have made the method two to three times as effective for catching as existing DAC technologies, the article's summary says.

Limited comparison basis
Otherwise, the basis of comparison is not large, explains Philip Fosbøl, associate professor of DTU Chemistry Technique and researcher in CO2-catching.

“It's not to compare with other DAC technologies, because there are no classic or common solutions today. There are too few existing examples, 'he says.

For the same reason, he welcomes the new approach.

“It's always inspiring with new and other ways of doing things. And this is definitely having potential, ”says Philip Fosbøl.

"That said, I also have a number of concerns."

We will return to them, but first we must have presented the new method.

The sea as a storage space
The newly developed CO2 filter is, as mentioned, a extension of the amin-based catch materials. This is a polyamine cu (II).

Therefore, the filter can be used in the very same way that technologies known today: CO2 in gaseous form can be captured and released again in gas form with a sight of storage or commissioning.

But it is also a hybrid material where additional reaction steps can be added.

"This is a new way to catch CO2, which is immediately based on ion exchange," says Philip Fosbøl, who knows of a similar electrochemical catch method from a research partner.

By adding salt water in a next reaction step, the CO2 is precipitated in the form of NAHCO3 - or baking soda in everyday speech.

Lehigh researchers even demonstrate how seawater can be used in the reaction while opening up the possibilities of using just the sea as a storage space for the CO2 by directing the alkaline baking soda solution into the oceans.

Circular perspective is lost
With high catch efficiency and the possibility of bypassing often expensive storage in the underground, the researchers believe that the new approach can in the long term remove CO2 at a price of less than DKK 700 per ton.

In comparison, the Climate Council has estimated that DAC with subsequent storage costs DKK 2,600-4,400 per ton.

So what is Philip Fosbøl's concern?

First, the recycling of the absorber requires another reaction step after the formation of baking soda, then polyamine-cu (II) is restored. It requires the supply of caustic soda or sodium hydroxide (NaOH) in the relationship one to one with CO2 catch.

"That is, one ton of NaOH is needed to capture one ton of CO2. That's right, really much. Where should it come from? ”Says Philip Fosbøl.

The caustic soda must then be diluted by a factor of 100. Thus, 100 times as much water per tonne captured CO2, which causes a very large water consumption in Philip Fosbøl's eyes.

"They don't really control the circular portfolio," he says.

And then the DTU lecturer estimates that there are still a number of difficult scaling steps ahead when the method is to be lifted from the laboratory level to a million-ton scale.

At present, according to him, the method is "very far from practice".

Requires a whole energy island to operate
According to the Climate Council, there are two major uncertainties associated with DAC: costs and energy consumption.

With the current known technologies, the International Energy Agency, IEA, estimates that the latter is about 6-10 GJ per year. ton of CO2. For example, if we in Denmark are to catch 5 million tonnes by means of green electricity, energy consumption will approx.

So all of the upcoming Energiø Bornholm production.

Based on Philip Fosbøl's assessment, the new DAC technology will not change that image. Rather the contrary.

“It's going to require two to three times as much energy as existing methods. It will place great demands on the production of energy, ”says the DTU lecturer.

Large amounts of air through the system
Energy consumption is associated with several stages of the catching process. For example, contemporary amin-based catch methods require heating the absorbent material to release the CO2 before catching.

Here, the researchers from Lehigh University promise to be able to keep the desorption process to temperatures below 90 degrees C if thermal release of CO2 is to be made.

Alternatively, the CO2 can be released at ambient temperatures when it is done using the aforementioned reaction with salt water.

Another significant factor in relation to the high energy consumption of the current DAC processes is the relatively low concentration of CO2 of the atmosphere.

Despite the CO2 concentration of 420 ppm, which was measured in May last year, the highest measurement result in history is the climatic insert only a small part of the composition of the atmosphere.

"When caught CO2 from the air of the atmosphere, where the concentration is small, you have to have very large amounts of air through the system," says Philip Fosbøl.

"Here it is about developing a setup that does not require very large and energy -intensive fans."

No one knows the DAC of the future
How that setup will eventually look like, Philip Fosbøl will not guess.

"Immediately, I don't think we know today about the technology that will dominate in the future," he says.

“It is difficult to predict the development of DAC technologies, but it only goes one way. Forward. '

Title: Synspunkt: Energiøer: Pres ikke danmarkshistoriens største investering igennem
Outlet:
Ingeniøren
Claus Leth Bak, Professor , AAU Energi
Filipe Miguel Faria da Silva, Lektor, AAU Energi
Full text:
It is a wildly impressive project and a gigantic step for the green transition: Energiø North Sea will cost over 200 billion kroner and can supply enough power to cover half of the current Danish consumption - and then the island can even be expanded to the triple .

But there is pressure to reach the project to 2033. It requires technology that has not been fully developed yet or that are very expensive and the suppliers can hardly keep up with the existing need. Also, there is not enough qualified labor, and on the whole, the project is something of a Marsmission that researchers from DTU and Aalborg University have previously described it in a whitepaper.

Even the tools needed to plan the energy island by making computer simulations are challenged. Several parts of the planning are based on simulation models, which come from the suppliers of technical solutions. You get them only after the technology is purchased and thus locked. This is also the case today with wind farms and transmission of electricity via high -voltage connections with DC. But there is the extra big challenge with the huge energy island in the North Sea that the complexity is much greater, and it is limited what can be learned from previous installations because it is a new, groundbreaking project.

The message is not to pull the plug. Not at all. But it requires resources and time enough to devise the optimal solutions. If mistakes are made, Danish society risks paying dearly to them. A skew of 5 per cent. is 10 billion kroner! The unknown factors of the gigantic project are equivalent to launching a whole new form of car, with a new type of engine that will run on a different kind of roads than those we know and which have not been developed yet. At the same time, we have to run according to new traffic rules we have not started talking about. All at once.

An example is Power-to-X, where power from wind turbines is translated into green fuels that can be used in the heavy industry and for transport. It is a furious good idea that is being developed a lot. For example, the production of sustainable flight fuel in Aalborg will begin next year with the project Mesaf, in which AAU Energi is a partner in.

But with a project like Energiø North Sea, it is necessary that Power-to-X be developed faster and on such a large scale that sufficient fuel can be produced to utilize the surplus flow from the wind turbines in the North Sea. The fuel must be set aside and the vehicles and machines to be driven by it must be ready by either being built for the purpose or being rebuilt so that the engines can run on sustainable fuels. 

If that development does not happen fast enough, there will be too much power to the electricity grid. It requires the web to be further reinforced and it is already expensive. According to a report from the consulting firm Ramboll from March 7 this year, the expansion costs DKK 110 billion - 30 billion more than it was estimated in 2020. Such a significant expansion also takes a long time, and it is doubtful whether it can be reached in time. At the same time, the large amounts of surplus current from the energy island in periods of much wind will either go to waste or be sold extremely cheaply. For example, one cannot just expect to export to Germany, which is even in the process of a significant expansion with offshore wind turbines. 

Another example is labor. There are lack of qualified hands and heads to everything from the heavy construction work to extensive technology development and planning, which requires, among other things, many engineers. This requires that social responsibility be taken so that more young people are made interested in creating the specific technical solutions that the green transition needs - among other things through energy islands. It should start in primary school and go all the way up to research programs at the universities.

The gigantic amount of electricity that can be produced in the offshore wind farms must go to shore and be connected to the electricity grid. It assumes that we can make solutions that work as well as those used today. The current electricity grid is based on AC (AC), and is based on an old technology that has been tried for decades as the network was expanded and learned from the problems that arose. 

Over time, the energy island must be able to be connected to the electricity grid via multit terminal, high -tension DC (MTHVDC). No one has tried the shift from two terminals to several terminals with HVDC, and there are only a few multit terminals with high -tension DC today. They have restrictions that do not dare to an energy island, and overall it is a new concept that has not been tested in use in this way and to the extent that the electricity grid requires. It necessitates research and a great deal of development work by suppliers of equipment and with those who have to build and operate an offshore electricity grid. It will also be helpful if standardization is introduced in several areas. If the energy island is pressed too quickly, there is a risk of being locked in to one supplier. This makes future tenders difficult and can make it difficult to implement new technology and other solutions that will be developed in the coming years. If the solution with MTHVC does not work properly, the economy throughout the project will be worse and the green energy will not be nearly as accessible. 

So far, the development of the electricity grid has taken place in steps where you could learn along the way. With a large system that is established at once, the risk is that the shelf life is only like the component that has the shortest life because continuous replacement has not been tried before in the new system, and the interaction between the old and the new equipment can give problems. 

It is definitely a good idea to invest massively in sustainable energy and to create significant projects that can drive development forward. We work intensely for this at AAU Energi, where one of the research missions is directly about renewable energy and energy islands. But it is crucial that resources and time are allocated enough to ensure the planning and development of technologies, so that this giant step forward for the green transition is taken properly.

Title: Ni lande vil fordoble strøm fra havvind i Nordsøen
Full text:
120 GW offshore wind in 2030 and at least 300 GW of offshore wind in 2050. The Common Measure signed nine countries yesterday at the North Summit in Oostende in Belgium.

The capacity of the North Sea's offshore winds must be doubled by 2030. It became heads of state and ministers from Denmark and eight other countries to agreed to yesterday's North Sea summit in Belgium. 

By signing five agreements and a statement, participants paved the way for the North Sea's total offshore wind capacity to be 120 GW in 2030 and at least 300 GW of offshore wind in 2050. 

It is more than it takes to cover the consumption of all European households, which will transform the North Sea into a decided power center for wind energy, the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply Ministry notes in a press release. 

However, Belgian Prime Minister Alexander de Croo rushed to say that he and the representatives of the other countries are well aware that it will require something of a power effort from the WE-Brance, which already has difficulty living up to the ambitions in relation to both producing and setting up the required number of mills. 

Therefore, agreements were also signed that allow the pace to be turned up, among other things. By increasing standardization, improving security and strengthening coordination. It takes careful planning to reach the goal - and if you try to do it all at the same time, the industry is forced to the knees, they warned the CRO.

Connections across
It will go too far to review the individual agreements. But several of them (link https://kefm.dk/aktually/News/2023/apr/danmark-indgaar-en-rarakke- Agreements-om-Taetter-energi Connections-til-europa) is about collaborating with other countries on Possible connections between the Danish Energiø in Nørsøen and other foreign energy hubs. 

They help ensure that the Danish -produced green power can also be transported to consumers and industry in the other countries. 

Shortly before the summit also announced the Netherlands, according to Euronews, that they had entered into a historic agreement with the UK to link a Dutch offshore wind farm and the UK's electricity grid. 

The project called Lionlink is scheduled to air in the early 2030s, writes Skynews.

100 companies from the WE industry also used the summit to publish a statement that emphasized the massive need for great new investments in increasing the production of wind turbines and supporting infrastructure in the form of both networks and ports. 

The statement refers to estimates made by the European organization Eurowind. They show that the seven GW of offshore wind turbines a year, which the European industry is currently able to produce and set up each year, suggest as a tailor in hell. 

There is a need to increase the pace up to 20 GW a year until 2030 to be able to follow. 

Last month, the EU countries and members of the European Parliament agreed to double the production of renewable energy by the end of the decade.

According to the agreement, the proportion of renewable energy in the EU's total energy consumption must be 42.5 % by 2030 and preferably 2.5 % higher in an attempt to reach 45 %. The new rules are part of the FIT for the 55-legislation package, which is to reduce the U-emissions by 55 % by 2030.

By 2021, according to Eurostat, renewable energy accounted for 21.8 % of energy consumption in the EU. Wind made up 37.5 % of the total electricity produced from renewable energy sources.

In pipeline waiting so far largest offshore offerings
No one knows yet whether the agreements entered into the desired effect. But they land after a year of very small investments in wind turbines in Europe and where the WE industry at home has criticized the Danish government for breaking the so-called open door scheme that allows developers to bid with VE projects in one Self -selected area for own money. 

In an attempt to raise the pace, the Danish authorities have promised to initiate the largest offshore wind offer before the year is over. The supply will kick -start the expansion of a further nine GW of offshore winds before the end of 2030 - a number that can turn into 14 GW - and maybe even more. 

The government's proposal for a new marine plan also contains a doubling of the laid out area for renewable energy, the ministry writes in the press release.

Title: Storbritannien og Holland skal forbindes med nyt kabel og havvindmøllepark
Full text:
New cable between the UK and the Netherlands will make it possible to send energy in both directions from offshore wind farm in the North Sea. Cable, offshore wind farm and converter station will be completed by 2031.  

It is not only in Denmark that we think in energy islands. Next year, the Belgian grid company Elia is the construction of an energy island. Germany and the Netherlands have also previously shown interest in building energy islands, either as regular islands or as platforms.

Now the British are coming to the field in collaboration with the Dutch. A new project called 'Lionlink' must connect the two countries with an HVDC cable and an offshore wind farm. 

The project was presented in connection with Monday's energy summit in Belgium, where nine Northern European countries met to discuss energy in and around the North Sea. Here, the countries agreed to double the target of wind power in the North Sea, so instead of 150 GW, it will hit 300 GW in 2050.

The UK already has connections abroad with a total transfer capacity of 8.4 GW. Out of those, 1 GW goes directly to the Netherlands via the Britned connection from 2011. The new Lionlink connection will add between 1.4 and 2 GW of new transfer capacity between the two countries.

As mentioned, Lionlink must be connected to a transformer station in the Dutch part of the North Sea, from which there are cables for one or more offshore wind farms. Initially, the transformer station is expected to have a transfer capacity of 2 GW. 

The energy from the wind turbines must be connected to the platform via 66 kV AC cables. Here it will be transformed into 525 kV dc.

In order to send energy to both the UK and the Netherlands, the transformer station must be equipped with a so-called HVDC multite terminal. These are technology that today is known only from relatively few installations in the world.

Partners in the UK and the Netherlands expect a tender for the project to be ready by 2026 and that the connection can be ready around 2031.

Title: Energiø Bornholm kræver over 30 milliarder kroner i statsstøtte
Full text:
New figures from the ministry are showing a huge slide in the Energiø project's economy from an expected profit of DKK 16 billion to a thunderous and growing billion deficit.

The economy of Energiø Bornholm, which from 2030 will be a collection point for 3 GW green electricity from offshore wind turbines, goes from being bad to even worse. 

It shows updated assessments of the project's profitability that the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply has prepared and which the Engineer has come into possession of. 

The most likely scenario, where the design of the energy island is continuously adapted to upcoming climate targets, will deliver a project economic deficit of DKK 12 billion, which must be covered with state aid. 

This scenario will trigger a support requirement of just under DKK 1.6 billion annually for 20 years - a total of DKK 31.5 billion. This corresponds to DKK 10.5 billion per GW.

The deficit has grown by two billion since the last estimate sent out in the fall. Here, the Ministry set the project deficit of DKK 10 billion. In comparison, the ministry expected a profit of DKK 16 billion in the energy island's original business case, which was created under the climate agreement 2020. 

It gives a total of a MANKO of 28 billion kroner from 2020 to today.

Seeing a democratic deficit
However, the prospect of standing with such a large bill for a project that came into being able to deliver plus on the bottom line does not make the government drop its plans. 

The project continues. And that is a great wonder from the consulting firm Kraka Advisory. 

»All energy island agreements hold a prerequisite for the islands to be profitable. Therefore, the government and its agreement parties have a major problem when they reach the opposite conclusion without announcing it to the citizens, ”says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen, senior economist at Kraka Advisory. He continues:

»The project exudes democratic deficit. When the project economy only gets worse, the more the ministry is expecting it, politicians owe it to telling citizens why you still keep going that way. The politicians owe to defending why one does not pull the handbrake. "

That view shares the Alternative Climate Mayor Theresa Scavenius.

“In the Alternative we take good care of the citizens' money. And it seems that the government is not doing in this context. We will try to go for solutions that are about building renewable energy without being unnecessarily expensive, ”says Theresa Scavenius.

The new figures nurture the party's skepticism about the project.

"We have always been skeptical of whether it was a good way to make renewable energy because it is predictably a really expensive solution," she says.

State aid for the benefit of the Germans
The calculations are based on the fact that a two-third of the electricity produced is scheduled to be sold to Germany and transferred directly to the German electricity grid via a cable. And Frederik Læsøe Nielsen has a hard time seeing meaning in that, since the establishment and operation of the island requires such massive state aid from Denmark.

"It is a strange idea to order yourself to establish an energy island with state support, which first and foremost produces electricity for the Germans," says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen.

An obvious path outside of state aid is, in his opinion, moving part of the energy island's planned energy production into land. For land winds are much cheaper to establish and operate - so cheap that there is certainly no need for state aid, he says.

In addition to presenting the economy of the most likely scenario, the ministry also reviews several other scenarios. Common to them is that the project economy looks even worse in all cases.

For the scenario 'Frozen Policy', where the energy island does not change shape regardless of what is happening around it, the ministry expects a project deficit of DKK 26 billion. DKK and a state aid requirement of DKK 58 billion.

In addition, figures are presented for a so -called equilibrium -corrected scenario with a project -economic deficit of -16.6 billion. DKK and a support requirement of DKK 32.1 billion.

Finally, there is the scenario 'Target Filling', where the deficit is expected to be DKK 6.5 billion and the support requirement DKK 12.6 billion.

It is up to the government and the parties to decide whether the Energiø North Sea should be realized.

Title: Politisk aftale i hus om transport af brint: 'Så kan vi få lagt rør i jorden'
Full text:
The government and most of the parliamentary parties have agreed that a network of pipes must be established in Denmark to transport hydrogen from PTX.

If Denmark is to have a hydrogen industry, it is necessary to build a network of pipes for transporting hydrogen between the PTX plants and the industries that will use the hydrogen in Denmark and further down in Europe.

Now a majority in Christiansborg has so appointed the state companies Energinet and Evida to own and operate the pipelines. 

This is evidenced by a new agreement - which comes in continuation of the PTX offering that opened in April - which all parties in the Folketing except the Danish Democrats and the New Citizens have agreed.

»We have great ambitions for the expansion of offshore wind, which can supply large quantities of green power, which we can use, among other things, to make hydrogen and green fuels that can replace fossil fuels in Denmark and export to the German industry. This agreement clears a stone of the road so we can put pipes in the ground and make the adventure come true, ”says Climate, Energy and Supply Minister Lars Aagaard.

Shares the task
Evida and Energinet will distribute the task between themselves.

Evida must, as a starting point, connect domestic hydrogen producers and consumers and can connect them to a linked hydrogen system, while Energinet will basically stand for a so -called "backbone" of pipes. 

That is, connections to abroad, connections from upcoming offshore plants (energy islands) and pipe connections across the country to a hydrogen stock. Energinet can also look forward to becoming a system manager for the hydrogen network.

"With today's agreement, we will be able to take the next big steps so that we can redeem the potential for renewable energy in Denmark and a new Danish position of strength in PTX," says Thomas Egebo, CEO of Energinet.

The agreement also states that no state funding or direct state costs must be made to such a pipe network. A proposal on how financing the extension should take place must be ready as soon as possible in 2023.

CEO of Evida, Kim Søgård Bering Kristensen, "Looking forward to developing the [Hydrogen] infrastructure in a continued close dialogue with the market players to support their business ambitions in the future hydrogen economy".

Brint business praises minister
H2 Energy is one of the companies that has demanded a hydrogen infrastructure. It told the company's director, Rasmus Bach Nielsen, among other things here at ing.dk in the fall of 2022.

“It will be the most logical to connect the production of hydrogen in Esbjerg with the hub in Egtved, where exports to Germany are available. And in the Triangle area, the most important thing is because some major consumers may arise, such as the refinery, ”he said.

Now that the agreement is in place, says Rasmus Bach Nielsen:

»The agreement is an important step for the entire green energy sector. We now know the exact distribution of roles between Energinet and Evida, and it will push the process of getting the pipes in the soil, ”he says, praising Lars Aagaard for putting turbo in the entire PTX area in a relatively short time.

At H2energy, however, they are looking for clarity on where and when the pipes will be located.

"Of course, we understand that things are taking time and there is a political process, but our Final Investment Decision depends not only on the timing of when the pipes from Esbjerg to Fredericia are ready for use, but also on the price of the use of the very actual the pipes. That said, the agreement document is an important step. PTX will define a whole new industry in Denmark and it helps to promote the country's green future, ”Rasmus Bach Nielsen told the Engineer.

Title: ANALYSE Næste gang staten udbyder havvind, bliver det markant anderledes end før
Full text:
The engineer finds that there will be demands on sustainability and the environment in the upcoming supply of new offshore wind turbines. But Denmark does not go as far as other countries.

The offshore wind offerings that the government and a number of parties are currently negotiating will look significantly different than before.

If you listen to sources close to the negotiations comes the principle of always choosing the cheapest bid to step more in the background. It provides room to make a number of minimum requirements - so -called 'thresholds' - in relation to the sustainability of the parks, the recycling of the materials and the spectacularness of the mills in relation to nature. 

According to the Engineer's information, such minimum requirements are broad support, but they were basically brought to the field by SF, which earlier this spring made a proposal to use part of the tender price to restore the nature and biodiversity of the sea.

SF proposes to earmark one percent of the construction sum to restore and preserve the nature and biodiversity of the sea. 

Two -thirds of the amount, the developer must even dispose of nature measures to be described in the tendering process. 

One -third must go to a fund that e.g. can invest in stone reefs or eelgrass. Although the proposal meets great sympathy from all political corners of the world, there is still disagreement about the details.

The state will be co -owner
Although the state waves goodbye to purely financially founded tender rounds, it will not be a good day for threshold models such as those, you see more and more places abroad such as. Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, where developers will provide solutions that can supply stable electricity supply seen over a day, such as via a combi solution with PTX. 


For the problem, each additional requirement automatically also cuts an extra slice of the price it would otherwise be able to collect to give the winner of the tender access to the area. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply therefore protects its opportunity to make money. 

That is why it recently announced that the government is looking for a model that ensures that the state will both collect a concession fee for each tender and at the same time own 25 percent of each of the parks offered. 

Calls for innovation offerings
That the government just takes small steps disappoints more WE developers such as Vattenfall, which calls for tender rounds, focusing on finding the most innovative proposal rather than that is the cheapest.

However, this idea does not have a time on the ground at Energinet and the Danish Energy Agency, which is nervous that such tendering processes will be an open charging gate for complaints from rejected developers. The risk of litigation and that the case is thus pulling in long stretches is simply too great. Then it is better to go for faster and safer supply, says internal sources in the environment. 

Thus, on the technical front, the government and its agreement parties continue to negotiate on a relatively classic tender model with a total pool of a total of 9 GW, where the 6 GW is supplied by Hesselø (1 GW), Wares Flak II/Category II (2 GW), Nordsø, In (3 gw), while Energiø Bornholm delivers 3 GW. 

In addition, the government will allow overplanting to increase the mill density of the allotted area of ​​another 4 GW. However, these 4 GW are not part of the tender and are thus not secured e.g. Netting. Therefore, they will be able to be used to establish PTX.    

So far, Energiø Bornholm is still in the pool. But when the negotiations on that front got a hard slowing down, after new calculations on Energiø Bornholm's economy recently showed a state aid requirement of DKK 31.5 billion. crowns for the most likely scenario, there is a risk of the island being taken out and driven in a parallel track. 

The sluggishness is a result of several rapporteurs chopping the brakes in because the economy now looks bad. The rapporteurs have become concerned about whether it is really the best way to spend the money, despite the fact that they were already dropping the requirement for the islands to be profitable. 

It all stands and falls with the electricity price 
However, to drop Energiø Bornholm, however, there is hardly any talk. In that case, it would have long since happened, e.g. When the government's finance committee about three months ago assessed two settings to close Energiø Bornholm and the somewhat larger project Energiø North Sea. The Finance Committee chose to keep the projects in the recognition that the energy islands are systemically important in establishing more connections between Denmark and abroad.

With the latest calculations for Energiø Bornholm, the government and its civil servants may also have come to stretch their legs for themselves. If you dive into the material that underlies the ongoing negotiations on Energiø Bornholm, the government expects to be able to earn 26 øre per kwh. And it is just legally low if you ask Hans Henrik Lindboe, a partner in EA Energy Analysis. In his assessment, an electricity price of 40 øre/kWh is not unrealistic. 

What the electricity price really becomes is crucial to where the red numbers become on the bottom line. And it is also this electricity price that will determine whether the project will need state aid or not. If the government chooses to take seriously its considerations of giving the island its own electricity price zone, then the electricity price will be below the level that the developers could earn elsewhere - and then the developers need compensation that either needs to be scratched via higher tariffs or through state aid. 

Summa Summarum there are a lot of unresolved questions that help make the project very uncertain - a premise that the government also repeats over and over again. Therefore, it would not be strange if the government ends up pulling the island out of the tender equation.

Title: Det må briste eller bære: Havvinden ved Energiø Bornholm får ingen statsstøtte

Title: Energiø Bornholm hænger i tynd tråd med ny havvindaftale

The government and its agreement parties have officially entered into an agreement on the largest expansion of offshore wind of Danish history of 9 GW offshore winds, although there is a significant risk that Energiø Bornholm and thus one -third of the agreement's wind turbines will be completely dropped.

Several parties are critical of the new political agreement that the government and a number of parties entered into last night, and which set the framework for the offer of at least six GW of offshore wind plus Energiø Bornholm, which is set at 3 GW.

Find a new business model

Hasty process

She says that she has repeatedly called for basic analyzes of the current market situation, how other countries are expanding offshore winds and what is happening in the Netherlands, which is considered to be one of the front runners in the area.

Formulated in a hurry

»The reporting requirements come in relation to EU law and would thus also be placed without the agreement entered into. And since there are no decided tendering crities, the tenders will continue to be only a competition for price, ”she says. 

Vattenfall's Innovation Director Thomas Hjort is not yet able to say whether the company will bid on projects under the auspices of Energiø Bornholm.

The Danish Energiø will not be the first in the North Sea, and the economy can therefore be pressed, but there will still be space in the market for electricity production.

Belgium and Germany are already well in the process of establishing energy islands in the North Sea, and the Netherlands and the UK are following right after. They have all seen the idea and are planning and purchasing equipment.

Overall, there is a prospect that our neighboring countries in the North Sea within the same timeframe as Denmark or faster - are ready to send 11.3 GW electricity from offshore wind turbines to the European electricity market.

Meanwhile, the start date for the Danish Energiø has moved from 2030 to 2033, and Danish actors are still waiting for the tender material from the Danish Energy Agency.

However, the fact that other countries have come further in their efforts to establish their energy islands does not necessarily have to become a major problem for Denmark, says Lena Kitzing, associate professor and head of the research group Society, Market and Politics at the DTU institute Wind energy and energy systems .

Last year, she and her colleagues published an article in the journal Energes, in which they quantified the socio -economic value of the offshoret and identified their most important drivers using a modeling of how Europe's energy system develops until 2050 - also in the offshore wind area.

With the help of the model, the researchers analyzed that in terms of decarbonizing the energy system of the future, it will be socially economically to establish 214 GW of interconnected energy islands in the North Sea-the equivalent of at least eight-nine islands, each of which is in the order of 20 GW or more.

In the analysis, however, the researchers did not expect islands larger than 24 GW. Most people are likely to be a little less - especially at the beginning of development.

"Our calculations show that more energy islands are needed in the North Sea - maybe about eight pieces when we look towards 2050. So it's not that one country can stretch legs for the other country's plans to build an energy island by hurting to build first. All North Sea countries will probably get energy islands in the future, ”says Lena Kitzing.

So it was never the expectation that the Danish island should be the only one, but the question is whether it is a problem that it does not even come in as number two, but more likely as number last?

“Those who utilize the resource first get the greatest financial advantage. Therefore, each new Energiø will offend the price image for electricity from the offshore wind turbines in general in the North Sea, ”says Carsten Chachah, senior chief consultant at Greenpower Denmark.

But when the Danish Energiø 100 km west of Thorsminde was launched in 2021 with the support of almost all the parties of the Folketing, it was with the goal that it should be 'the world's first'.

In this connection, the then climate, energy and environment minister Dan Jørgensen (S) said that "it is important for Denmark to be a pioneering country." In this way, other countries should be inspired by the Danish solutions.

It can have an impact on the energy island of the North Sea, which in its original form should have been sitting like a spider in the middle of a cobweb of electrical connections to the other countries around the North Sea.

As the Danish Energiø in the North Sea is laid out, it is a far more complex, but possibly more future -proofed structure than, for example, the German platforms, and Carsten Chachah wonders that the Germans are going solo with clean platforms.

“So even though I think we need to get started as soon as possible, it doesn't have to be a problem to come after the others. Sometimes it can be fine to let others take the first steps and then learn from their mistakes, ”he says.

But there is a risk of waiting for too long, and it has to do with the previously mentioned extra bill for Energiø Bornholm, explains Hans Henrik Lindboe:

Lena Kitzing does not expect hydrogen production to play such a great financial role. Together with her colleagues, she has done analyzes that show that it is not worthwhile to start hydrogen production on the islands, except maybe from some small niche productions.

Another factor that comes into play is the extent to which it is possible to use an existing infrastructure, such as one has succeeded, for example, in Belgium, but does not have the opportunity in Denmark.

“So for all countries there are special considerations that make it difficult to compare the selected solutions and schedules. Title: Det første skridt er afgørende': DTU opfordrer til at tænke ud af boksen i fremtidige energiøer

Especially the electricity system on an energy island is very different from what we know. Therefore, DTU report recommends to view the Energy Islands as new inventions. The innovative solutions ensure the schedule and minimize the price.

Tailor simple, cheap wind turbines for energy islands rather than going for the existing expensive and complicated products. 

Together with some other solutions, it can speed up the pace and cut 20-30 billion kroner of a 10 GW Energy Island equivalent to 10 percent of the total expenses.

This is what the invitation from a group of DTU researchers, with, among others, Professor Jacob Østergaard from DTU Vind and energy systems at the forefront has just released the report Denmark as the Energy Island Pioneer based on a number of interviews with relevant industry organizations and companies. The report illustrates the technical challenges of establishing such a large plant and how research and innovation can help solve them. 

»The price and time horizon for establishing an energy island has so far been estimated on the basis of an expectation of using the components and system solutions already known from the normal electricity grid. But that strategy is not optimal for such an extreme project. Here is a need for innovation. And it is necessary to develop new simple solutions to keep the price down and the pace up, ”says Jacob Østergaard. 

He adds that we need to use Energiø Bornholm as a learning and development site. 

»In the report we have deliberately written a 10 GW Energiø rather than Energiø North Sea. The reason is that it is probably not realistic to harvest all the savings already in the energy island of the North Sea. Therefore, the amounts mentioned do not apply to it, but to a future island of that size, ”he says. 

Isolated behind a wall
One of the areas where innovation in the working group's assessment can really move something is in the design of the interaction between the mills and the large HVDC connections that use DC for the transfer of electrical energy as opposed to the transmission network's alternating power lines.

As the mills connect into a network that is insulated behind the HVDC converters, they are decoupled from consumers. It makes it possible to design the web on the energy island based on other design criteria than what we are used to in the existing electricity grid with consumers, says Jacob Østergaard.

E.g. Should wind turbines usually used in the offshore parks meet a strip of grid connection requirements to ensure that the mills contribute to maintaining stability in the electricity grid, minimize the risk of errors and disturbances and maintain the voltage quality of consumers. But many of these requirements are unnecessary to place in the isolated network that is established on the island as long as the HVDC connections live up to them. "So why make a more expensive mill," says Jacob Østergaard.

The report also advises on how the islands can best integrate PTX so that they not only get the best possible market solutions and investment setups, but can also best contribute to the stabilization of the island's isolated electricity grid.

Specifically, it is about combining the electrolysis system's converters to incorporate a greater flexibility into the energy island's electricity grid so that the errors that occur out here do not break through in a country because the PTX system can absorb the imbalances.

It's a paradigm shift 
By placing the PTX plant out on the energy island far out on the sea, you will be able to use it to operate and stabilize the electricity grid that is insulated out here. It can't be done if you put the PTX system inland. Here it can only control how much surplus energy is posted into the ordinary electricity grid. At the same time, it is cheaper to transport the hydrogen than electricity to land, he says. 

»We are planning that you can also use PTX systems to stabilize the supply network on such an extreme energy system. And that's also what we need in the future electricity system based on renewable energy, ”says Jacob Østergaard.

While the current electricity system is based on large, stabilized power plants with built -in inertia, the energy island's electricity system is 100 percent based on converters and thus exclusively electronically controlled. This means that errors and imbalances here are propagating much faster.

“The electricity system on an energy island is very different from what we know of. We're talking about a paradigm shift. It requires new methods of management, and of course we need to be sure that they will work safe and stable, ”says Jacob Østergaard. 

He points out that Is a need to find out how the respective converts should react by mistake and how to coordinate each other. Here the research must step in and deliver new solutions, he says.

The components have to play together
The working group looks at the wind turbines and the HVDC converters under one hat because there are limits to how much you can optimize the effects of the future energy islands and reduce costs and time spent by looking at its individual components separately. 

The trick is to be able to think the parts together into a whole that can drive the large transformation in the form of an EU with a total of 400 GW offshore wind energy by 2050.

»With the report we give the ball up to think innovation into the energy islands, not least in relation to system solutions. Many of the winnings of the Energy Islands are in the possibility of optimizing them as a system, where the individual parts are thought together in a new way, ”says Jacob Østergaard.

As the Energy Islands are blasting the framework for existing offshore parks, there is a need to rethink many of the previous technologies to make them work in the new context.

“It corresponds in many ways to the time when the first car was built 140 years ago. They were almost motor -driven horse -drawn carriages, just without a horse. To some extent, such projects will always be limited by the world we come from, unless we consciously think innovation, ”he says.

And in his opinion, it is especially the first step that is crucial to whether one succeeds in developing a future -proofed setup. If you go in the wrong direction, you risk getting out of a dead end compared to the further expansion of the entire North Sea and the Baltic Sea. 

“That's why it's not just about optimizing the energy islands themselves. They must be seen as elements of the overall energy system with a future offshore electric and hydrogen infrastructure. It must secure the solutions in relation to the further expansion of energy islands and offshore infrastructure and hubs in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea, ”says Jacob Østergaard.

Title: Analyse: Energiø Bornholm drukner i ubekendte
Full text:
The political agreement on the framework for Danish history's largest expansion of offshore wind can shrink if neither the state nor the sets dare to take on the risks.

Over the past month, the government parties have been busy giving Energiø Bornholm artificial respiration. The urge to try to keep alive the high -profile political project was particularly stated after the engineer in May was able to publish new figures for the island's project economy, which the Danish Energy Agency had calculated on the basis of its ministry.

The figures showed a project -economic deficit of DKK 12 billion for the most likely scenario, where the design of the energy island is continuously adapted to upcoming climate targets. This scenario will trigger a support requirement of just under DKK 1.6 billion annually for 20 years - a total of DKK 31.5 billion.

What changes the estimates of the energy island from a profitable project to a project with blood -red numbers on the bottom line is that according to the board there are insufficient revenue. The electricity price is too low and investors have too high interest -ranking requirements.

In the days after the engineer had brought the figures to the square, the chairman of the Baltic Energy Island Foundation, Claus M. Andersen, told several media that the island, despite the alarming accounts, of course still becomes something-it is only a matter of finding out of how.

However, during the negotiations on the new offshore wind agreement, the government failed to get the rapporteurs that it is okay to spend so many of the Danes' tax dollars on holding their hands under such an uncertain project. In particular, the Alternative and the Liberal Alliance refused, pointing out that it was originally intended that the project should be able to run around by itself.

Bounds of support
What the rapporteurs just agreed to was to give green light to give DKK 17.6 billion in state aid to establish the Danish part of the island's infrastructure in the form of a cable to Zealand/Germany and a station on Bornholm. Everything else has to set up with themselves whether they dare to bid in the upcoming tendering processes.

Therefore, the final offshore wind agreement did not sound at least 9 GW of extra offshore wind compared to the current 2.3 GW, which would otherwise have been the government's proposals for the negotiations. Instead, the wording was at least 6 GW plus Energiø Bornholm.

And the latter is probably going to suffer the suffocation death, because too few dare to tie in with the risks that lie in that the agreement does not support the developers who want to establish and operate the wind turbines that convert winds into electricity. They have to cope with market conditions.

Chaos in the backdrop
But in fact, the government has also been very much in doubt as to whether it should keep life in Energiø Bornholm. An access to documents shows that as late as February and March this year, the government went with concrete considerations of stopping the project due to an uncertain economy.

On February 8, an employee of the Danish Energy Agency sent e.g. An email out to other employees in the same board and associated ministry that the project would now be separated from the tender framework to provide the opportunity to decide the support model and support ceiling and discuss at all "whether the government wants to continue or support the project".

On February 12, an employee of the Ministry asked the Board for help to answer a question from the Ministry of Finance about "whether there are alternatives that can utilize the offshore wind at Bornholm and make it a better business than in an energy beer solution."

The Ministry even doubts that this can be done, as the Danish Energy Agency's socio -economic analysis "just shows the value of making an energy beer solution to utilize the offshore wind instead of radial offshore wind in the same location".

The employee also mentioned a previous calculation that the Danish Energy Agency had prepared the year before, which showed that it is hardly possible to improve the project's economy if the Danish state changes its mind and fails to establish a cable for Germany, so that the offshore wind comes the Danes alone for good.

"The project economy in that calculation looks fairly comparable with 3 GW overall in 2030, while the social economy is a little worse," noticed the staff of the ministry.

On February 14, an employee of the Danish Energy Agency replied that Energiø Bornholm is, as you know, just planned as an energy island with a foreign connection. If the entire project is "conceived new and established as either a radial offshore wind farm or a non -connected sea park with PTX connected, it will require further analysis, while the concept for the radial parks must be fixed."

»Basically, the difference between Energiø Bornholm compared to Radial Parker is that the power night on Bornholm itself is very small, while preparing a number of other large offshore wind turbine projects in Zealand. So the foreign connection is quite important if a power evening is to be secured for a project of that magnitude, ”the mail states:

"It is noted that if a radial park is planned instead, some of the cost of preparation will be lost, the intergovernmental agreement concluded with Germany will have to break, and it may be necessary to update the environmental surveys," the employee writes from the Danish Energy Agency to the Ministry.

Burst or bear
The dialogue illustrates the government's dilemma: Should it close the project due to poor finances and bid farewell to 3 GW, which it cannot establish elsewhere, as well as the 1.2 billion kroner it has so far cost to run the project in position, or should it Try to realize the project to the best of the best and then take on the many risks?

It smells of a losing case that the government then tries to twist out by letting it up to the sets to decide whether the project should burst or carry.

And as for the energy company Vattenfall, Denmark's largest operator of offshore wind, Innovation Director Thomas Hjort is not yet able to say whether the company will offer projects under the auspices of Energiø Bornholm.

»Energiø Bornholm is a complicated project, especially because the electrical connections are both about the offshore wind, but also as general connections between Denmark and Germany. We look forward to becoming wiser in the upcoming market dialogue. "

Title: Britisk offshorebranche skriger på teknikere og ingeniører og skal bruge det tredobbelte om få år
Full text:
New report calls for a strategy to tackle the lack of, among other things, turbine technicians, engineers and others with technical skills.

It is not only in Denmark where the lack of labor risks tightening legs for the green transition. The UK is currently reporting a 'dramatic increase' in the need for the number of employees if the British government's target of 50 GW offshore energy - including 5 GW fluid - is to be reached by 2030.

It shows a new report from the Offshore Wind Industry Council (OWIC), which gives a snapshot of the British workforce in offshore wind.

At the same time, OWIC is looking at the expected future need for labor by 2030. Here, the projection is that in seven years there are expected to be 104,401 jobs within offshore wind, provided that all announced projects will be successful. According to the report, there were 32,257 people in the industry at the beginning of the year.

»The offshore wind sector needs many more people in short, medium and long term to move forward. We all - across industry and government - have to work even closer together to develop a strong, new strategy that attracts all the skills we need to move forward as soon as possible, ”says Richard Sandford, co -chairman of OWIC to the media E&T - Engineering and Technology.

It is persons in key areas such as planning and approval as well as high -voltage technicians, turbine technicians and people with a number of digital skills that are particularly in demand. 

The report also points out that more should be done to attract young people to search for a Stem-related career (Vote covers engineers and IT and scientific candidates).

Offshore wind is a global challenge
However, it is not only in the UK that labor for the offshore sector is high. In an analysis from the Engineers' Association, IDA, of Danish Energy and Infrastructure Projects by 2030, it is estimated that approximately 205,000 full-time equivalents will be needed for the construction of offshore wind farms.

In addition, there are a number of other projects such as energy islands, roll -out of district heating, several charging stations and the establishment of new highways and bridges. Thomas Søby, chief economist at IDA, has stated in a previous interview with the Engineer that labor cannot be provided for all of them. He therefore calls for a political point of view to be a great priority - and here it should be green investments such as offshore wind turbines that must be at the forefront of the queue.

“We have to have a debate about what's most important. I think you should initially drop the highways and prioritize resources where they do the best benefit socially and in relation to the climate targets, ”he says.

A forecast prepared by Global Wind Organization (GWO) and Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC) earlier this year shows that there will be a need for 568,800 trained wind engineers to construct, install, operate and maintain the global onshore and offshore wind turbine fleet in 2026 .

In particular, the need for offshore will grow, estimating a growth of 92 percent in the total number of technicians.

Title: Manglen på vindteknikere kan stikke kæp i hjulet på politiske ambitioner
Full text:
There are plenty of projects on the drawing board, but hardly as many hands to set up the mills. Global Wind Service must already refuse tasks today.

In Fredericia, it is considered with equal parts enthusiasm and concern when new major offshore projects see the light of day. For in the headquarters of Global Wind Service, one of Europe's largest wind turbine set -up providers as well as service and maintenance, the biggest challenge is currently getting enough qualified labor. This applies to both wind engineering, project managers and engineers.

“We have huge challenges in recruiting the right skills, which also makes it difficult to meet the ambitious goals that are from politicians around Europe. There is enough work out there to chase. The challenge is that we do not have enough qualified and experienced labor, ”says Lars Petersen.

He is the Chief Commercial Officer in Global Wind Service, which has 1,800 employees, of whom approximately 1,500 are technicians in the field, and currently primarily installing offshore mills in the Netherlands, France, the UK and Asia, especially Taiwan.

According to a forecast prepared by Global Wind Organization (GWO) and Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), there will be a need to recruit 142,100 new technicians over the next five years.

The report concludes that 568,800 trained wind engineers will be needed to construct, install, operate and maintain the global onshore and offshore wind turbine fleet in 2026.

In particular, the need in offshore will grow. Here, a growth of 92 percent is estimated in the total number of technicians. In comparison, the expectation 'only' sounds at 27 percent for onshore technicians. However, in 2026, most wind technicians, according to the forecast, will work with operation and maintenance of onshore wind turbines.

“You have to keep in mind that when you have a lot of ambitious goals, it also requires someone to do it. The challenge just becomes proportionally greater as more and more is being expanded, ”says Lars Petersen, who adds that it is not unusual for the industry to go on a beach.

"When we are all pressed and we have projects that are progressing, and you suddenly have to lack people, the easy solution is of course to go in the market and take apart."

He points out that of course it is not a sustainable solution - neither for the industry nor for the projects - that one runs predators on each other.

Looking at other skills
Among other things, Global Wind Service has its own training academy, where people with a craftsmanship background such as mechanics, plumber or electricians can be introduced to the wind industry. But:

“Obviously, it also has its limitation. We can only have a certain number throughout a year, otherwise the level of experience will be too low on the projects. We are constantly trying to balance how much experience we have, compared to how many green people we can take in, ”explains Lars Petersen.

Another way of curbing the lack of skills is to gain access to another type of labor. Among other things, the company has tried this in England, where they have been targeted for people who want to leave the defense and have a civilian career.

“If you have worked with the Defense Material, you will have some prerequisites as well as good mechanical or electrical skills where we can see that they can be transferred to something we can use. So we've done a lot to promote wind to previous Armed Forces, he says.

Although several alternatives are being thought of to obtain hands, it is far from enough to meet the need. It is constantly noticed that the lack of wind technicians is a bottleneck.

“Unfortunately, we say no to tasks every month as we lack experienced people. Of course, it is not satisfactory that we cannot deliver on the queries that are coming. "

Drop motorways - prioritize green investment
In an analysis from the Engineers' Association, IDA, of Danish Energy and Infrastructure Projects by 2030, it is estimated that approximately 205,000 full-time equivalents will be needed for the construction of offshore wind farms.

Thomas Søby, chief economist at IDA, points out that there are many ideas in pipeline such as energy islands, roll -out of district heating, several charging stations and the establishment of new highways and bridges.

"It may be that you can find the money, but there is never really anyone who asks who the FA is going to make it," he says, pointing out that labor cannot be obtained for all of them.

“I simply don't have the imagination to imagine that it can be done. Then they have to pick up people inside the forests that we had no idea existed. "

The chief economist calls for a political point of view to be prioritizing hard - and here it should be green investments such as offshore wind turbines that must be in the front of the queue.

“We have to have a debate about what's most important. I think you should initially drop the highways and prioritize resources where they do the best benefit socially and in relation to the climate targets, ”he says.

May 30, 2023, the government, together with a number of agreement parties, published the framework for expansion of offshore winds of 9 GW - potentially 14 GW or more. For Lars Petersen, however, the big question is still: Who should put up the many new mills?

»Overall, we think it is great that Denmark has increased the level of ambition and will build energy islands in the Danish waters and that the state is actively investing in the new offshore projects. It gives us a unique opportunity to promote the entire Danish cluster of companies that contribute to the green transition. We just have to make sure that we are also hands enough to lift the task, ”he says.

Title: Ingeniørstuderende vender de 'sorte' teknologier ryggen
Full text:
De unge vælger bredt: Ingeniørstuderendes interesser afspejler samfundets

Du finder ikke mange ingeniørstuderende, som har viet livet til at aflure forbrændingsmotorens hemmeligheder, eller som underholder med dampmaskinens lovende egenskaber over en fredagsbajer i S-Huset på DTU.

De studerendes interesser følger nemlig i høj grad det, som generelt optager samfundet inden for teknologiens verden.

Det fortæller Mads Pagh Nielsen, studieleder på Institut for Energiteknik på Aalborg Universitet.

»Det er meget tydeligt, at de studerende bliver præget af samfundsdebatten. De er enormt orienteret mod den grønne omstilling og bæredygtighed og har samtidig vendt de ‘sorte’ teknologier ryggen,« siger Mads Pagh Nielsen.

Han bakkes op af Lars D. Christoffersen, dekan på DTU.

»Jeg oplever i høj grad de studerende som mennesker, der ser problemer ude i samfundet og gerne vil bidrage til en løsning, i deres tilfælde med fokus på teknologiske løsninger, eksempelvis grøn omstilling eller sundhedsteknologi,« siger han.

Farvel forbrænding, goddag brint
Når man spørger personer inden for uddannelsesområdet – dekaner, institutledere, studerende – hvad der optager de studerende på landets ingeniøruddannelser, er det nærmest som at spørge, hvad der optager Ingeniørens læsere.

Det er power-to-x, energiøer, sundhedsteknologi, automatisering, den grønne omstilling og bæredygtighed.

Derimod, fortæller Mads Pagh Nielsen, er de studerende mindre interesserede i eksempelvis vindmøller og solceller.

»Det er begrænset, hvor meget længere man kan nå med eksempelvis design af vindmøllevinger. Selvfølgelig kan de optimeres, men de store skridt i det felt er taget,« siger han og nævner, at heller ikke eksempelvis forbrændingsmotorer, varmepumper eller kraftværksteknologier bliver mødt med særlig interesse fra de studerende.

»Og det er faktisk lidt uheldigt, for der er stadig brug for innovation inden for de teknologier, også selvom vi står midt i den grønne omstilling,« siger Mads Pagh Nielsen.

»Vi prøver også at skabe interesse for andre områder inden for energi, eksempelvis kraftværksteknologier, for man skal som ingeniør kunne noget inden for forskellige områder, særlig når der er behov for sektorkobling i energiinfrastrukturen,« siger Mads Pagh Nielsen.

Had/kærlighed
Vi flytter os lidt fra tunnelsynet på vedvarende energi og den grønne omstilling, for selvom det er meget aktuelle emner i disse tider, er det ingenlunde det eneste, der bliver uddannet ingeniører til.

Nete Sparre Hangel er næstforperson i Polyteknisk Forening – de ingeniørstuderendes studieorganisation – med fokus på de uddannelsesmæssige områder – og så læser hun til diplomingeniør i produktion på DTU.

Hun ser, at uddannelsesvalget blandt hendes medstuderende i en grad har været båret af et kompromis mellem interesse og udsigten til et meget, meget langt arbejdsliv.
