Det er power-to-x, energiøer, sundhedsteknologi, automatisering, den grønne omstilling og bæredygtighed.

Derimod, fortæller Mads Pagh Nielsen, er de studerende mindre interesserede i eksempelvis vindmøller og solceller.

»Det er begrænset, hvor meget længere man kan nå med eksempelvis design af vindmøllevinger. Selvfølgelig kan de optimeres, men de store skridt i det felt er taget,« siger han og nævner, at heller ikke eksempelvis forbrændingsmotorer, varmepumper eller kraftværksteknologier bliver mødt med særlig interesse fra de studerende.

»Og det er faktisk lidt uheldigt, for der er stadig brug for innovation inden for de teknologier, også selvom vi står midt i den grønne omstilling,« siger Mads Pagh Nielsen.

Grønnere bygninger skal bygges på fleksibel elstyring
Sponseret briefing
Grønnere bygninger skal bygges på fleksibel elstyring
Elforsyning
»Vi prøver også at skabe interesse for andre områder inden for energi, eksempelvis kraftværksteknologier, for man skal som ingeniør kunne noget inden for forskellige områder, særlig når der er behov for sektorkobling i energiinfrastrukturen,« siger Mads Pagh Nielsen.

Had/kærlighed
Vi flytter os lidt fra tunnelsynet på vedvarende energi og den grønne omstilling, for selvom det er meget aktuelle emner i disse tider, er det ingenlunde det eneste, der bliver uddannet ingeniører til.

Nete Sparre Hangel er næstforperson i Polyteknisk Forening – de ingeniørstuderendes studieorganisation – med fokus på de uddannelsesmæssige områder – og så læser hun til diplomingeniør i produktion på DTU.

Hun ser, at uddannelsesvalget blandt hendes medstuderende i en grad har været båret af et kompromis mellem interesse og udsigten til et meget, meget langt arbejdsliv.

Artiklen fortsætter efter annoncen
»Samfundet er blevet indrettet på den måde, at du skal vælge en uddannelse, og helst én uddannelse, og på baggrund af den skal du så finde en plads på arbejdsmarkedet de næste 60 år,« siger Nete Sparre Hangel.

Hun vil ikke udtale sig om, hvad der generelt interesserer de omkring 13.000 studerende på DTU, men inden for hendes område, produktion, har fokus de sidste par år i stigende grad rettet sig mod automatisering og – på baggrund af interesse fra både studerende og erhvervslivet – industri 4.0.

Inden for det felt handler det altså om at placere sig på en hylde, som er interessant enten forskningsmæssigt eller for arbejdsmarkedet, men som også interesserer dig som studerende.

»Du skal finde noget, du synes er interessant, og som du gider bruge din tid på; noget, du gider hade dig selv lidt over, men som du samtidig elsker at lave. Det er det, som er vigtigt, når du skal finde din retning,« siger Nete Sparre Hangel.

Bred bachelor vinder frem
Nete Sparre Hangel valgte en linje, der allerede fra starten har markeret en klar retning i ingeniørkunsten. Men Lars D. Christoffersen fortæller, at de nye studerende i højere grad ønsker et bredt perspektiv, når de søger ind.

Det kan han i hvert fald se på de foreløbige ansøgninger, han har modtaget inden ansøgningsfristen i juli. Her er den brede, internationale linje, general engineering, som er »mere populær end nogensinde,« siger han.

»For det første har den et godt ry og et stort internationalt perspektiv, men jeg kan også høre på de studerende, at mange er lidt mere søgende end før i tiden og vil helst ikke låse sig fast fra uddannelsens begyndelse,« siger Lars D. Christoffersen.

Digital power-to-x
Men modsat den brede indgang til ingeniørfeltet, så har netop de linjer, der handler om den grønne omstilling og teknologiske løsninger på klimakrisen, stadig høj interesse blandt de unge.

Derfor har DTU lanceret sin første digitale bachelor, hvor studerende placeret over hele landet kan gennemføre en bachelor uden at skulle møde op på DTU i Kgs. Lyngby eller Ballerup.

Og de første digitale bachelorer fra DTU kommer ud med en høj grad af specialisering. De bliver nemlig uddannet i power-to-x.

»Der er enormt mange power-to-x-aktiviter ude i landet,« siger Lars D. Christoffersen og nævner blandt andet anlægget i Esbjerg og de kommende energiøer.

»Samtidig har projekterne fået meget national og regional omtale i medierne, og det er et felt, hvor der bliver brug for ingeniører, hvis vi skal nå den grønne omstilling. Derfor valgte vi at starte der,« siger han og understreger, at power-to-x formentlig bliver den første af flere mulige specialiseringer på den digitale bachelor.

DTU forventer omkring 30 optagne på uddannelsens første semester.

Title: Energinet hyrer Rambøll som bygherrerådgiver til Energiøen i Nordsøen
Full text:
Ramboll becomes a developer advisor on the entire electricity transmission plant on the energy island of the North Sea. Now new and efficient solutions must be found for transporting electricity, which can be included in an upcoming supply.

A number of pre -qualified building consortia have for a long time looked a little more thorough in the mailbox to see if the tender material for Denmark's upcoming Energiø in the North Sea should be dumped. 

Originally, the material was intended to be ready in 2022 so that a winning consortium could be assigned the task in March 2023. Last June, the date of the tender material was then moved to September 2023. 

But now, according to a press release from the Ministry of Climate, it has been moved for another year.

However, it does not hold Energinet to take another step in the process, and hire Ramboll to be a builder consultant at the electricity transmission system for the Energiø.

This is what John Ammentorp, country manager for Ramboll's energy business in Denmark, tells ing.dk.

»The main task will be to assist the Energinet with developing the entire electrical infrastructure. This applies to both the transmission from the wind farms, plants on the island itself and the transmission to land. We have already done a concept study, and now it has to be brought further so that the technical data can be included in an upcoming tender, ”he says, adding that Ramboll will subsequently follow up on the tender and the future suppliers of solutions.

Hvdc in unknown waters
Several basic technical questions must also be answered by 2033, when the first phase of the energy island of 3 GW must be ready to supply electricity. For example, this applies to the use of platforms for converter stations, explains Jan Hagenau, senior project manager at Energinet,:

“It has always been the idea that in addition to the energy island itself, platforms may be needed - even in the first phase of the energy island. But as wind farms are built with a total capacity of up to 10 GW in larger and larger distances to the energy island, there may be a further need to establish converter platforms near the wind farms, which can transfer the energy to the energy island with HVDC, ' he says. 

Once the energy has landed on the island, the electricity system must be linked to other countries. For the time being, an agreement has been made with Belgium. 

In order to do so, a so-called 'multiterminal HVDC' plant is needed. It is - slightly simplified - a large coupling system for direct current connections. It is technologically complicated and brand new compared to known wind farms, where energy is sent ashore via a single cable. 

"But because it is new, research and development is also needed to make the concept usable," says John Ammentorp.

Hydrogen or not hydrogen
Another unresolved question is where the production of hydrogen can most optimally take place. Therefore, it is also not determined how much of the energy is to be sent ashore as electricity and, how much to use to produce hydrogen on the island.


The material that Energinet has issued in connection with the publication of the agreement with Ramboll shows that several different solutions are thought of. But Jan Hagenau emphasizes that it is not something that Energinet is directly involved in.

»It will be an upcoming PPP (public private partnership) that builds the island and owns it while we will be responsible for the electricity transmission plant. But as it happens in the framework for Energinet's work, we must plan to land 2 GW to Denmark. Whether this will change if a possible Commercial actor chooses to establish plants such as British production or energy storage on or near the island, we have no knowledge of, ”he says.

The contract between Ramboll and Energinet has a value of DKK 225 million. kroner and run over the next 10 years.

Title: Udbuddet for Energiø Nordsøen udskudt på ubestemt tid
Full text:
The Ministry acknowledges that the current concept of energy island triggers an excessive bill. Therefore, it sends the concept back on the drawing board.

(Updated)

»The hat off for the government's clarity. Energiø North Sea is too expensive and dropped. " 

It is the consulting firm Kraka's Twitter commentary for today's announcement from the Ministry of Climate that it is now dropping to send the $ 210 billion. expensive Energiø in the North Sea in tender because it triggers a loss of more than 50 billion kroner. It is too expensive and risky.

“That bill for taxpayers has now been averted. The government and the minister deserve high praise for that, ”Kraka writes on Twitter.

Instead of sending the energy island in tender to find the companies that are to build the energy island, the ministry and the Danish Energy Agency start looking for a better and cheaper concept. What it is more specifically about is not specified. 

And one does not get much wiser by diving into a 1350 -page large access to the island's business case, which the Engineer has recently gained access to. It is completely darkened. 

Does Danes cost money
To get an idea of ​​what's going on, you have to roll the time backwards to last summer, when the ministry dropped its plans to make a large recessed energy island in favor of a solution with a smaller island and more floating platforms around the island. 

The shift led to the ministry also having to pull the emergency brake and postpone the tender that had been put into the calendar at that time.

Climate, Energy, and the Supply Minister does not hide where the shoe is pressing:

“The original political agreement was resting on a green ambition and an ambition to get rid of Putin's gas. But there was just a sentence in the agreement that it must not cost the Danes money. And the figures now show that we cannot fulfill that prerequisite, ”says Lars Aagaard (M) according to a press release.

Will not promise that there is a cheaper solution
Otherwise, the plan was for the supply to be ready before the summer holidays. But it's not going to happen now. The government and the conciliation parties agree to spend the next six months turning every stone to find ways to redesign the project so that it will still be connected. 

Whether the project is even profitable, which has just been laid down as a requirement in all previous agreements on the energy islands, the minister is not sure. Nevertheless, he assures that the government continues to hold on to the ambition of an energy island in the North Sea. However, the supply is currently being postponed indefinitely.

Title: Energiø Nordsøens ekstreme kompleksitet gav den øgenavnet 'monsteret' på Christiansborg
Full text:
A requirement for state co -ownership, a very long foreign connection and towering material prices made Energiø North Sea too expensive, says experts and sources close to the government. Well, the tendering process was postponed indefinitely, says Kraka Director.

Yesterday the supply of Energiø North Sea was postponed indefinitely. And today, it's time for reflection on what exactly it was that made the government take that step. 

Brian Vad Mathiesen, professor of energy planning at Aalborg University, estimates that it is probably not only about high expenses, but also that there has been a struggle for the tender conditions.

“In this process, it has also happened that quite a few other countries have also gained experience with different concepts for such energy islands. There has also been a debate in Denmark about what opportunities could be to make things more simple and modular. In that light, it is very wise of the government to stop the project in its current form and thus get time to think about finding better solutions and getting the price down, ”says Brian Vad Mathiesen.

“If the government does not, it risks it both becoming more expensive and takes longer to establish such an island. The postponement also gives a chance to find a simple and modular solution and thus can build things faster than what you have expected. In any case, it is wise to incorporate all knowledge in the field to get the expenses down to a reasonable level. "

The only disappointing he thinks is that the government did not make the calculations long ago. 

Impossible project for politicians
The fact that the government first chooses to put the project on hold for 11 hours before the tender is, according to KRAKA director Peter Mogensen, together with the fact that very large projects are regularly proposed, which no one can really see the scope and the consequences of. And they drive on until someone shouts.

"This can be done especially in projects under the auspices of the green transition, where politicians will have to join, if not that they will be against - because it can be used against them. They can be laid out by their opponents as doubters or as not being really green, ”he says, continuing:

"It is an impossible project to be a politician in. A new momentum is emerging every four months. It is a mix between social economy, operating economy, engineering, chemistry, everything else, plus a notion of an energy island that no one knows what is to be used for, and some completely uncertain component about Power-to-X that nobody knows What turns into. That was what should be screwed into a tender - and there are no members of parliament in this country that is able to overlook that problem, ”says Peter Mogensen.

Therefore, he will give Climate Minister Lars Aagaard a large number in the character book for having had the courage to stop a project that may not have been decidedly "crazy", but at least "very questionable".

“It means that you can do it another time too. A precedent has been created to stand up against crazy things. And it is a huge country recovery in this talk, besides stopping the specific project. That's one of the wisest things I've experienced the politicians making since the last election, if not the wisest. "  

Hurray for the climate minister
Peter Mogensen says that Kraka has spent the past few years working through the economy. It has given the house's economists wrinkle in the forehead, where their main concern has been, who should take the risk. If things are going well, then private investors will reap the winnings, but if it goes bad, taxpayers have to pay many generations.

“I'm pretty sure a lot of rapporteurs are now emitting a sigh of relief. For they have read all about what Kraka has come up with where it has dawned on them that this bill ends in the children's room. And now there is finally someone who dares to say. And there you just have to say that the new climate minister must have a large number in the character book, ”says Peter Mogensen.

The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply yesterday stated that it will now explore the possibility of better and cheaper concepts. 

Jakob Østergaard, who is DTU professor in electric technology, is too far from the drawing board to comment on what exactly lies on it. But he mentions that he and his colleagues have recently released a report that shows that with few, concrete innovations can be possible to reduce the cost of a 10 GW Energiø by 20 billion kroner.

“And then it is wise to find some less complex solutions for the energy island that can make it cheaper. Here we can get some of the learning from Energiø Bornholm on the field, ”Jakob Østergaard writes in a text message. 

Far to Belgium
To seriously become clearer about what is really going on behind the ministry's closed doors, one has to listen to the water pipes a little to know something. Here it is reported that it is already several months since the economists calculated that Energiø North Sea would impose a cost of 50 billion on the state.

This happened when the government negotiated with the settlement circle to find DKK 17.6 billion to realize Energiø Bornholm - something that only just succeeded. 

Recognizing that it is hardly realistic to get the same conciliation to sign up to withdrawing another $ 50 billion from the treasury, the government has decided to turn every stone to find ways to make it cheaper. The number that the ministry and the board bring back there must be a political belief in. Otherwise, the project will not turn into anything.

One of the crunches at the supply should be that it is very complicated and marks that the state will own 51 percent of the island - it reduces investors' council across the island. If you divide a little about what it costs to establish the Belgian energy island based on the current material prices, then the conclusion was clear: Energiø North Sea is too expensive.

And if the state has to pay the foreign connections in line with what it has decided to do in relation to Energiø Bornholm, then it is not only 17 billion kroner to be found, but at least double, as the connection must extend all the way to Belgium . So one of the big, unresolved questions is whether to peel the foreign connection out of the project so that the island will stand for itself, and consumers are going to pay it over the tariffs.

It complicates things so much that the project does not hold in its current form. Perhaps that is why, according to sources, the island close to the political environment has been nicknamed 'Monsteret' among the officials trying to get it right.

It must be back on the drawing board.

Title: Første grønne brint produceret til havs ud for den franske kyst
Full text:
French company produces the first kilograms of hydrogen on floating platform. The next target will be a 10 MW electrolysis unit on a platform in the North Sea.

The European Commission has set it as a target in the Repowereu plan, which was launched in May 2022 that by 2030, DKK 10 million will be produced. tons of green hydrogen in the EU.

On top of that comes the ambitious plans to expand the North Sea with offshore wind turbines. Here, hydrogen is made via electrolysis a crucial part of the projects.

This also applies to the Danish Energiø, which last week was paused, among other things, on the grounds that there was a need to look at the technical concepts again.

For it has been an open question on a regular basis whether the hydrogen should be produced close to the wind turbines out of sea or whether electricity should be led ashore and the hydrogen is produced here.

But perhaps the answer has come a little closer after the French company Lhyfe at the end of June could present the first kilograms of hydrogen produced on a floating platform about 20 kilometers off the French west coast.

"We are incredibly proud to be the first in the world to produce hydrogen at sea," said Matthieu Guesné, founder and CEO of LHYFE, in connection with the news.

Up to 400 kg of hydrogen per day
The plant, which has been named Sealhyfe, consists of an electrolysis unit of 1 MW on a floating platform. 

It is connected directly to a floating wind turbine of 2 MW that was installed back at the end of October 2017 during the EU-supported Floatgen project.

The SealhyFe platform has an area of ​​about 200 square meters and is able to produce up to 400 kg of hydrogen a day.

Before the electrolysis system was pulled at sea, it was tested thoroughly in the port of Saint-Nazaire. It must work offshore under extreme conditions and is therefore designed to minimize the need for maintenance once it is installed at sea.

The entire construction is connected to land via a so-called umbilical cable, which, in addition to transferring data and electricity supply, can transport hydrogen ashore.

Commercial test platform in the North Sea
The next step in the development will be a new project called HOPE, where a consortium with nine partners selected by the European Commission under the European Clean Hydrogen Partnership has been awarded 20 million euros in grants.

The goal is to build a plant of 10 MW in the North Sea with the goal of commercialization of the technology. Such a plant will be able to produce up to four tonnes of green hydrogen a day, which will be exported ashore with pipeline and then compressed and delivered to customers.

Title: Sejt træk mod klimaneutral skibsfart: 3 bud på løsninger på kort og lang sigt
Full text:
The world's 175 flag states have succeeded in adopting a common goal of climate neutrality for the shipping industry "in or around, that is, close to" 2050, as the slightly unclear wording sounds in the text text. 

The agreement was signed in the UN Maritime Organization, IMO, in London last week and was received with clapping. 

But as Kåre Press-Kristensen, senior adviser to the Council for Green Change, told the Engineer last Friday, the jumping point from here will be how the industry will get there. 

To elucidate the road to the 2050 goals, the Engineer has spoken to Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen, an independent advisor and one of the country's leading experts in shipping. 

His assessment is that it certainly will not be an easy way.

1. Electrification on short routes
The most obvious green solution would of course be to electrify the fleet. 

However, according to Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen's own calculations, it is limited how much of the shipping industry's fleet is actually candidate to undergo electrification. 

»Freight vessels sailing the long routes on the oceans need huge amounts of energy. For example, a loaded container ship must use batteries that weigh 20 percent of the cargo in order to sail for 1-2 days. Here, electrification is not an option, ”says Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen.

But electrification is suitable for passenger ferries on smaller routes, which can be seen with more passenger ferries in Denmark, such as the electric ferry Ellen, which sails between Ærø and Als as well as the latest electric ferry cave sailing between Esbjerg and Fanø. 

"Ships that have ruting lengths of 1-2 hours are suitable for being electrified, but if they sail longer than that, they will have to look for another solution," says Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen.

2. Streamlined ship design
However, electric route ferries between islands in the South Funen Archipelago are unlikely to make the huge industry climate neutral, as their energy consumption is very low overall. But there are gains that can be picked up by designing the ships better. 

Because according to Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen, the ships in the '00s were built with an optimism that is backing today. They were built "chubby or full," as he calls it. 

“If you see a tanker from the front, you will notice that it seems terribly chubby and it creates a great wave resistance. Ships were designed in that way to have more cargo on board, but the ships are now fining it on the energy side and the ship's technical performance, ”he says.

Thus, on the short run towards 2050, this can be corrected by designing "slimmer" ships with a well -designed hull shape that has a smaller capacity in the future, but conversely is far more energy efficient

3. The long -term, necessary solution
In the long term, however, the shipping industry will have to transition to e-fuel such as e-methanol and e-ammonia. Both fuels must be made of water and hydrogen through PTX. 

And on the one hand, it looks promising. According to calculations from the Maersk Center for Zero Carbon Shipping, a cargo ship that sails on e-ammonia, only three percent of the CO2 that a ship sailing on bunker oil does. 

But on the other hand, the shipping industry is far from the only industry that looks against e-fuel to become climate neutral. Therefore, there is a prospect of a violent bottleneck as we approach 2050, which marks the deadline set in the Paris Agreement. 

For huge amounts of energy need to be used to just produce the e-fuels the shipping industry needs. According to the Maersk Center for Zero Carbon Shipping, the shipping industry alone needs 1,110 GW energy if only 50 percent of the fleet is to use e-fuel to operate the ships. 

In 2020, the world produced just under 3,000 GW of green energy. Energiø Bornholm will have a capacity of 3 GW. Maersk Center for Zero Carbon Shipping estimates that by 2050 the energy needs will reach a staggering 25,000 GW. 

“It will be very difficult to produce the energy that the shipping industry's green transition needs. We must not be overwhelming, ”says Hans Otto Holmegaard Kristensen, appealing to more research into new energy sources, for example in nuclear power.

Title: Bekymrede svenske myndigheder: Søkabel syd for Skåne kan forværre havmiljøet
Full text:
Among other Sweden's meteorological and Hydrological Institute warns that the cable between Energiø Bornholm and Zealand can cause serious damage to the Baltic Sea.

The sea cable, which will be drawn between the upcoming Energiø Bornholm and Zealand, can aggravate the marine environment of the already severely needed Baltic Sea. 

This is the opinion of several Swedish authorities in consultation responses, which they have sent to the Danish Environmental Protection Agency as part of the ESPoo Convention, writes Maritime and Bornholm Tidende. 

The cable to supply Zealand with green power must be carried 209 kilometers underwater from Bornholm to Zealand.

Thus, it can also directly affect the marine environment along the Swedish coasts, giving the Danish authorities a duty to ask the Swedish authorities about their views on the case through ESPOO hearings. 

The ESPOO Convention of 1991 ensures that states inform each other of plans and projects that can have significant cross-border environmental impact.

Environmental impacts still not illuminated
The part of the Baltic Sea, where the cable is to be buried, supplies the rest of the Baltic Sea's central, deeper parts with saline and oxygen -rich water that the marine environment depends on. 

As the salinity of the Baltic Sea is already at the boundary of what wildlife can withstand, it is critical to keep track of whether a project causes less salt to flow into the waters. 

One of the consultation responses comes according to shipping from the Swedish water authorities, the Vattenmandigheterna, who is concerned about the cable's 'cross -border environmental impact' on the water quality, which has already been put under pressure and environmental toxins.

Another comes from Sweden's meteorological and hydrological institution, which is particularly concerned about the places where stone settings are to be established that protect the cable.

The ESPOO hearings take place before the Danish Environmental Protection Agency assesses the environmental impacts.

For shipping, Christina Kittner, project manager and biologist at Landscape & Skov, says in the Danish Environmental Protection Agency:

»The project's impact on the environment has not yet been elucidated. This will be done in connection with the preparation of the environmental impact report for the project. "

The Danish Environmental Protection Agency's assessment is expected to be ready at the end of 2024.

Title: Bornholm kan levere grønne brændstoffer nok til at dække sit behov til færger, industri og transport
Full text:
A study indicates that almost 90,000 tonnes of green fuel have customers on and around the island, where the energy will come from the energy island in the Baltic Sea.

About 88,000 tonnes of green fuels can be produced for port and shipping on the island, as well as up to 60 GWh energy from PTX for heavy transport on land. It shows the results of a new study of potential power-to-X production at Bornholm.

"With this study we show that it is possible here on the island," says Maja Felica Bendtsen, head of Bulk at Rønne Havn A/S and points out that the goal is to pass on knowledge to the Bornholmers and potential developers.

More specifically, the report points out that about 50,000 tonnes of green methanol can be produced, which will cover ferry traffic to and from Bornholm. 

3,000 tonnes of green fuels can also be produced for transport at Rønne Harbor, where it will, among other things, cover the transport of wind turbine parts. In addition, one percent of the shipping market around Bornholm equals 35,000 tonnes of green fuel. About 60,000 ships sail past each year, of which one percent can potentially be covered by PTX on the island.

Inside the island, about 9 GWh energy a year must be used for Bornholm Industry, which corresponds to half of the consumption. There is also a lot of heavy transport on the island, and PTX must help to meet the need for the part of the transport that cannot be electrified. That is, at least 50 GWh energy is needed to cover agricultural machinery and trucks that drive far. This corresponds to about a third of heavy transport on the island.

These values ​​are found, among other things, on the basis of EU rules on green fuels in shipping and the government's climate partnership for industrial companies, which dictate that half of the industry's consumption must be covered by green energy.

No concrete plan yet
According to the study, the price of potential PTX production on Bornholm will be at the high end, but not unrealistically high. Behind the studies, the digital tool Optiplant has been used to calculate the price and potential for PTX productions, and the simulations show that the price of green fuels will be in line with production elsewhere in Europe.

Although the results are merely ideas and not specific action plans, the study also points to a very concrete handling of the waste heat from electrolysis systems. The excess energy that is not bound in hydrogen can be used for district heating on the rocky island. About 35 percent of the energy from electrolysis of water turns into waste heat that can be utilized if the Bornholm district heating network is connected, it is pointed out in the study.

"However, some more studies need to be done, and then there must be support from the population and politicians on the island before this power-to-X production turns into something," says Maja Felica Bendtsen.

So it is not a concrete planned yet, the presented study simply maps the potential. 

It is emphasized that the potential power-to-X production on the island must be developed in the wake of the upcoming energy infrastructure in the Baltic Sea, which will play with the new energy island. The excess renewable energy from the energy island must be used for the project.

Title: Belgien løber med æren for verdens første energiø mens Danmark hænger i bremsen

Title: Nyudviklet materiale fordobler effekten fra varmestråling: 'Vi sætter det foran solcellen'
Full text:
Researchers from Aalborg University have, in collaboration with TU Hamburg, developed a metam material of iridium that can effectively convert heat radiation into electrical energy without too much loss.

The North Jutland University calls it itself a huge technological breakthrough, which can be of great importance to the green transition.

In a collaboration between Aalborg University, TU Hamburg and Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon, Gesthacht, researchers have developed a technique that can double the efficiency of, for example, solar cells. 

By using a technique called Thermophotovoltaic (TPV), where heat radiation through photons is directly translated into electrical energy, researchers have examined how effectively they can concentrate revenue in a new metam material. This material is installed on a component that can be put in front of, for example, a solar cell. A description of the new material is published in a research article in the journal Advanced Materials.

On the one hand, it absorbs all incoming radiation, and then heated up to 1,000 ° C. On the other hand, radiation is emitted with a specific wavelength that is adapted to the solar cell. So it is the heat and not the sun's rays that are converted into electricity. One of the challenges of the TPV technique today is to create materials that can operate at high temperatures without oxidizing.

»A normal silicon sun cell is limited in efficiency because light with wavelengths that are in the infrared area is shorter than 1,150 nanometers cannot be absorbed by silicon. Most of it smokes directly through, and shorter wavelengths that are absorbed generate only a few electrons in the silicon, although the photon energy was actually enough for more. You do not get the energy utilized properly, ”says Professor Kjeld Pedersen from the Department of Materials and Production at Aalborg University.

According to Kjeld Pedersen and his colleague Manohar Chirumamilla, who is one of the driving forces of the project, it is because light in the green/blue area of ​​the light spectrum only generates one electron per photon, although the energy of the photon is actually higher than the one the electron gets . It simply reaches the so-called Shockley-Queisser limit, so that the efficiency of the solar cell is limited to just over 30 percent.

“The idea with us is that if we now put something in front of the solar cell, which absorbs all radiation, then it becomes over 1,000 degrees hot, and something that is hot, then radiates again by 1,000 degrees. The other side we put in thermal contact with an emitter that we have designed so that it can only emit wavelengths that fit the specific solar cell used. Then the theoretical efficiency is suddenly 80 percent, ”explains the Aalborg professor.

From black gold to iridium
Namely, it is the manufacture of the emitter that is a challenge. That's why Manohar Chirumamilla, Kjeld Pedersen and their colleagues designed a nano -size metam material, less than the wavelength of light. However, these nanostructures with a large surface relative to volume become fragile when heated up to high temperatures. Therefore, a more stable material should be found.

The idea for the new material originated from another project in collaboration with Sergey Bozhevolnyi from the University of Southern Denmark, where Kjeld and his colleagues for fun developed a material called black gold. Here they took a gold base and structured it, by digging into it with ion beams and creating structures in nanoscale. The goal was to create a material that absorbed all the light without it escaping again.

“We looked at each other afterwards and thought what the cave can we use it for? We have made something that absorbs and we know that if we can do something where we control the absorption, then we can also do something where we manage emission because it is two sides of the same case. Then the talk fell on TPV and the opportunity to design a material with both absorption and emission, ”explains Kjeld Pedersen.

However, the research team had to find a cheaper material than gold, and here they flattened over the element iridium, which at normal temperature conditions becomes a hard transition metal with high density. What makes the material interesting is that it retains its efficiency at high temperatures and is very inert to oxygen.

Although Iridium is not the cheapest material to find, it is cheaper than gold. And because it spreads out as a thin layer of a few 100 nanometers, the amount of the material to use is not quite high, says Kjeld Pedersen. This iridium layer is then inserted between two hafnium oxide layers that can handle high temperatures.

“We tested them over a few weeks at high temperatures up to 1000 degrees Celsius, where they still worked well. Then it hears that the effectiveness of the radiance from a body increases effectively with the temperature in the fourth. So if now we could bring ours from 800 degrees, which someone has made before, to 1000 degrees, then we have doubled efficiency. So the last degrees really play a role to get the efficiency up because it grows so sharply with the temperature. "

Kjeld Pedersen compares the material with an optical filter where only a specific wavelength is allowed to be absorbed into the material. In other words, the surface of the material acts as a filter that ensures that only certain waves are converted into electrical energy.

“If we say it should be on a solar cell, it will sit on the side facing a solar cell. It is then heated because it is in thermal contact with an absorber, a pure black material on one side, and then it radiates towards the solar cell on the other. You can only radiate something that exactly fits the solar cell having the highest possible efficiency for wavelengths, ”explains Kjeld Pedersen.

Easy to scale up
Because the material is tailored to the solar cell, efficiency increases because more waves are absorbed and converted into energy. Kjeld Pedersen, however, does not think their material works so well with silicon sun cells, but will work better on solo cell solarial cells.

He also sees great potential in scaling up the production of the material. If he and his colleagues can demonstrate that they can make the material on a 100 millimeter disc, then they know that there are equipment that can scale them up to 200 and 300 millimeters.

The production process itself is also not expensive, says Kjeld Pedersen, who estimates that the material could easily hit the commercial market within five years if some startup companies pick up the technology.

Although Iridium is not the cheapest material, it is easy to obtain and can reach a long way. Kjeld Pedersen estimates that the cost of Iridium is far offset by the gain that comes on the increased energy extraction from the material in the long term.

The significant increase in the effectiveness of, for example, solar energy opens up to include the technology of future energy systems. This could be, for example, with large energy plants in connection with Power-to-X on energy islands. Here, large concentrator systems can be built as it is known from CSP (concentrated solar power).

In addition, the technology can also be used as a warehouse where wind and solar energy is used to heat materials where the radiation from the material at a later stage through TPV can generate power.

“I think this technology can have a big impact on storage, or are used in the industry. Think about how many gigawatts a year go into waste heat from industrial processes that could instead be absorbed and translated into power. It may well be that in this context it does not give 40-50 percent power, but maybe 5 percent, which is energy you have created through surplus heat, ”concludes Kjeld Pedersen.

Title: Danske CIP vil bygge GW-energiø ved finske Åland - klos op ad brintrør
Full text:
Together with two electrolysis companies, the Danish Investment Fund is now starting to explore the possibilities of establishing a new energy island in the GW class at Finnish Åland.

Bornholm has long been in play to become the first energy island in the Baltic Sea - but now there is a risk that this state project will be overtaken in a collaboration between CIP's subsidiary Copenhagen Energy Islands, Finnish Flexens and French Lhyfe. 

The treble clover has joined forces to establish an energy island on the Finnish autonomous archipelago Åland, which is in the entrance to the Botnic Gulf a good distance outside Denmark's economic zone. 

The newly released press release only describes the plans in overall twists. And this is because, according to Director of Cip Thomas Koopmann, the parties still have to get stuck on the details such as size, timeframe, wind turbine type and physical location.

“We are in an early development phase where many things need to be clarified. But we are talking about a project in the GW class in terms of both the wind and electrolysis section, ”says Thomas Koopmann.

'Sefer than uncertain'
The idea for the project has not arisen from one day to the next, but through the ongoing dialogues that the three partners have had with stakeholders and regulators - conversations that take out that Åland has the prospect of becoming a metropolis in the Nordic Land's upcoming common hydrogen infrastructure. It will first and foremost consist of the Baltic Sea Hydrogen Collector piping, which will connect Finland, Åland and Sweden with Germany. The piping gets a detour to Gotland and may also get detours to Bornholm and the Baltic countries.

»The idea is to use most of the energy island's manufactured electricity for electrolysis and production of hydrogen. The hydrogen must then be sent through the pipeline to destinations all over Europe. Because we look at Offshore Wind and PTX in an integrated solution - as the most advantageous way of realizing the project, ”says Thomas Koopmann.

Experience with hydrogen projects
Where Copenhagen Energy Island has its expertise in establishing offshore winds, the other two partners must contribute their concrete experience with electrolysis. Here, for several years, Flexens has been successful in developing hydrogen projects adapted to specific regional conditions, while in 2021 Lhyfe opened the world's first industrial green hydrogen production plants connected to a wind farm. The following year, LHYFE opened the world's first offshore pilot platform for the production of green hydrogen.

"The time has come for us to join our partners in order to kick start the next phase of the development of the project," says Thomas Koopmann, who lists some of the questions to answer.

What could potentially prove to be show stops is, for example, the closer examination of the seabed waiting ahead. For it can show that the seabed is "absolutely terribly soft", which can make the construction a very costly and cumbersome affair.

“Although the seabed immediately looks nice, it may prove to be very soft when we begin the physical examination of it. There are also examples of at home in Denmark, such as. The course around Hesselø offshore wind farm. Finally, the business case must be connected, even when we have agreed on the technical details of the project. And these are the ones we start looking at now, ”he says.

It's just a year ago that Ørsted and CIP decided to join forces in a new 50/50-partnership to develop a number of offshore wind projects under the open door scheme in Denmark-including Bornholm Bassin Syd (1.5 GW) and Bornholm Basin East (1.5 GW) in the Baltic Sea near the upcoming state Energiø Bornholm. These projects were put into the world under the auspices of the so-called open door scheme, which has since been shut down. This has made it less likely that CIP and Ørsted will realize the Bornholm projects.

Title: Grøn omstilling bremser op: ‘Kriselignende tilstand i vindsektoren lige nu’
