Title: Norge vil droppe elkabler til Danmark: ‘Tiden er løbet fra store, nye udlandskabler’
Full text:
Since 1977 there have been electric cables between Denmark and Norway. Today, they consist of four cables with a total capacity that makes it possible to exchange 1,620 MW between Jutland and Norway.

But in Norway there is a political debate around the oldest cables, which in 2026 will reach their technical life. The question is whether the cables should be replaced by new ones or they should be completely scrapped.

One of those who does not want to renew the two cables is the party leader of the harvesting party, Trygve Battlevold Vedum. To the NTB news agency, he says.

“The Hero Party believes there is no need to renew the permits. It is our clear primary attitude. We think the time is over for big, new foreign cables, ”says Vedum.

The Center Party's attitude is not new, and the dispute over the export of electricity to Denmark has been going on for several years. The arguments are that exports help to drive electricity prices up in Norway.

This is especially true in the southern price areas. Namely, there is a lack of transfer capacity to Northern Norway, which gives major differences in electricity prices internally in the country. This became clear during the Corona crisis and subsequently in connection with the energy crisis on the basis of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In April 2022, however, the Storting voted no to limit electricity to Denmark, among others. The decision was adopted with the votes of the government parties The Labor Party and the Center Party.

But still, the Hero Party will now limit the number of foreign cables, as they fear that high electricity prices in the rest of Europe will get rid of Norway.

The Norwegian government has set up a "power price committee", with representatives from the industry and the research, which will look at, among other things, how the Norwegian electricity prices are affected by exchange with the rest of Europe.

The head of the Left Party, which is generally considered EU-friendly, Ola Elvestuen, emphasizes that the Power Price Committee has determined that electric cables abroad give Norway better security of supply than if they were not there. Right now, Norway has 17 foreign connections, which in addition to Denmark goes to Sweden, the UK, the Netherlands and Germany.

»The best way to ensure stable low electricity prices in Norway is not to drop cables. It is to ensure that Norway has enough persistent electricity, ”he says.

It is Energinet's Norwegian sister organization Statnett that has the concession to build and operate the cables.

Cable to Scotland exposed
The Norwegian criticism of foreign connections is not new and has been going on for several years.

This applies, for example, to an application to connect Norway to Scotland through a cable with a capacity of 1,400 MW. The approval of the connection, named NorthConnect, was postponed by the then government by 2020 and by 2021 it was dropped.

But in the spring of 2023, the case was resumed to great annoyance for several Norwegian politicians and organizations.

Among other things, energy policy rapporteur at the Progress Party, Terje Halleland to E24, said the government should stop processing of the application.

»Norway should not sponsor Europe with cheap electricity. Now the government has to kill this cable once and for all, ”he said at the time.

There was also strong resistance from the industry and the trade union movement. Head of Norwegian LO, Peggy Hessen Semensvik, believed that the cable should be "buried forever" and from the industry it sounded that NorthConnect should be rejected thoroughly and finally.

System Responsible will preserve cables
While the Norwegian politicians and organizations have looked mad at the cables between Norway and the rest of Europe, the Nordic system -responsible companies have a different perspective.

In the latest joint report called “Nordic Grid Development Perspective 2023”, they write, among other things, about the Skagerrak connection that it may be advantageous to preserve - or even increase - the capacity between Norway and Denmark.

This is because the price differences between Norway and Denmark can give high socio -economic benefits for both countries. Therefore, Statnett and Energinet have also agreed to look forward to a possible replacement of Skagerrak 1+2.

Meanwhile, Statnett and Energy have also initiated a joint project on a so -called "hybrid electricity connection". The idea is to link an upcoming Danish Energiø with Danish and Norwegian offshore winds and thus create another electricity connection between the Danish and Norwegian electricity market.

Title: 2023 i bakspejlet: En tam superleder, flagermus og vand, vand og vand
Full text:
2023 blev et år med sus i. Mest for dem ved østvendte kyster, men også for it-folk, der med generativ AI nu har fået superkræfter. Vi fik PFAS i æg og en tvivlsom superleder – og oven over alting svæver Andreas Mogensen.

Januar: Økologi – nu med PFAS
Lige indtil oprydningen efter nytårsmiddagen havde PFAS for de fleste danskere blot været en forkortelse for en række skadelige stoffer koncentreret omkring brandøvelsespladser. Overskueligt og på afstand. Men da PFAS helt uventet dukkede op i danske økoæg i en koncentration, hvor børn i alderen 4-7 år blot ved at indtage den gennemsnitlige mængde økologiske æg ville overskride den maksimale tolerable grænse for al mad, kunne alle se alvoren.

Forklaringen lå i foderet. Hvor de ikkeøkologiske høns spiste sig mætte i fuldfoder, som er en blanding af soja og forskellige kornsorter, blev de økologiske høns fodret med fiskemel. Problemet blev løst ved at udskifte de økologiske høns’ menu, og snart lagde de igen sunde æg. Mens økolandmændene således kunne ånde lettet op, trak eksperterne til gengæld vejret noget tungere og sendte havet et bekymret blik.

Med en lang række målinger kunne de konstatere, at havet omkring Danmark har det, de kalder en udbredt diffus forurening med PFAS. Det betyder forurening uden én eller få klare kilder, men nærmere, hvad man kan kalde en generel baggrundsforurening. Hvor den så kommer fra, kunne ingen forklare. Men en ting er sikkert. PFAS dukker op langs alle vestvendte kyster, fordi stofferne opkoncentreres voldsomt i havskummet, inden det blæser ind på stranden og over markerne. PFAS kunne ikke længere ignoreres.

Februar: En ulige luftkamp
Ballongate blev betegnelsen for det, der må være den særeste luftkamp i flyvningens historie. En kinesisk ballon med en diameter på 60 meter nåede at bevæge sig ind over Alaska, videre hen over Canada og til det nordlige Idaho, før præsident Biden havde fået nok og beordrede den skudt ned. Det blev gjort med landets tungeste skyts i form af et missil fra et F-22 Raptor-jagerfly i 20 kilometers højde under hele verdenspressens og den kinesiske præsidents bevågenhed. Den amerikanske udenrigsminister blev hjemme fra et besøg i Kina, mens resterne af ballonen blev fisket op af havet. Selve ballonen viste sig at være bygget af amerikansk hardware, mens den bar på kinesiske sensorer til indsamling af billeder og video. Dog uden at sende data hjem til Kina. Siger USA. Det tydeligste indtryk, der står tilbage er en selfie, jagerpiloten tog med ballonen i baggrunden, inden han lukkede luften ud af den.

I det danske hav skulle der ikke være balloner. Der skulle være masser af havvindmøller. Troede man. Planen var, at energiselskaber nu skulle til at bygge offshore-vindmølleparker for egne penge og uden om statslige udbud efter den såkaldte åben dør-ordning. Selskaberne skulle byde ind på alle de arealer, der ikke var øremærket til offentlige udbud. Men pludselig fortrød Energistyrelsen og lukkede muligheden for øjnene af en række meget byggeivrige selskaber. Der lå ellers projekter klar til en produktion af vindenergi, der ville kunne dække danskernes behov to gange. Problemet var, at styrelsen ikke havde gjort det juridisk klart, at ordningen kun var tænkt til små projekter tæt på land. Så branchen havde derfor budt ind med meget store projekter over 1 GW langt fra kysten. Men de arealer hører til de lukrative. Og dem vil staten gerne beholde for sig selv.

Marts: Hønen eller ægget
»Vi er i gang med at sætte en Ferrarimotor i en gammel Ford Taunus.« Så malende beskrev en ekspert i elproduktion det over for Ingeniøren, da vi gik på jagt efter en løsning på et snigende og uundgåeligt problem i den hastige elektrificering af samfundet, vi er midt i: for tynde og for få elkabler. Med forslugne datacentre, elbiler, varmepumper og ikke mindst PtX står vi over for en fordobling af elforbruget frem mod 2030 og noget, der ligner en femdobling i det efterfølgende årti. Hvis al den el skal ledes sikkert ud til forbrugere og produktion, er der brug for en udvidelse af elnettet til 110 milliarder kroner inden 2040. El har på ganske få år bevæget sig fra at være en stabil selvfølge til at være moderne tids månelandingsprojekt.

Men det er ikke blot dimensionerne, der ændres. Selve strategien og vilkårene for udbygningen ændres radikalt. Førhen har selskaberne skullet eftervise et behov, før de kunne spendere forbrugernes penge på nye kabler. Nu skal vi etablere infrastrukturen strategisk. Det betyder, at vi skal bygge VE-zoner i områder, hvor der er plads, og hvor vi kan trække kabler hen. Men det skal vel at mærke ske, inden produktionen overhovedet er flyttet derud. Vi skal med andre ord have lagt massive mængder nye kabler ud nu og her, inden vi kender placeringen af fremtidens produktionsanlæg. Læg dertil et krav om en helt ny måde at styre spændingen på, nu hvor den ikke længere er sikret af stabile kraftværker, men tværtimod er påvirkelig af vindens styrke eller en sky for solen. Der er nok at tage sig af i det, der nu benævnes nationalkritisk infrastruktur.

April: En motor med flade dæk
Med den optimistiske titel ‘Forberedt på fremtiden’ lancerede regeringen en markant reform af de videre­ gående uddannelser, hvor halvdelen af alle landets cirka 500 kandidatuddannelser kan se frem til at blive halveret fra to til et år. Udvalgte kandidatuddannelser skal dog forlænges og lægge op til ekstra fordybelse som forskere eller specialister. Som oplagte områder nævnes nano- og kvanteteknologi. Målet var at få flere kloge hoveder hurtigt ud i erhvervslivet. Men modtagelsen var ikke så taknemmelig fra den side, som regeringen jo nok havde set frem til.

Siemens Gamesa skrev således sammen med en række andre førende virksomheder et åbent brev til regeringen, hvor de peger på, at tekniske og naturvidenskabelige områder netop er de områder, der »udgør størstedelen af fundamentet i den danske vækstmotor.« Vindmølleproducenten meldte herefter direkte ud, at den ikke ønsker at ansætte danske ingeniører med en etårig kandidatuddannelse.

Oppositionen mødte forslaget med udbredt bekymring for, at forkortede kandidatuddannelser kan skabe et A- og et B-hold, og IDAs formand, Laura Klitgaard, noterede, at »det virker, som om man med åbne øjne har piftet dækkene på vores vækstmotor.« Da stod det klart, at regeringen står meget alene ved reformfronten, når det gælder langvarige uddannelser.

Maj: Større klode søges
I kampen for et bedre klima har vi fået en ny modstander: biodiversitet. Pludselig er det ikke længere blot menighedsråd og borgerforeninger, der spænder ben for nye vindmøller. Nu kan hensynet til en lille fla­ germus stoppe de største havvindmølleprojekter.

Problemet er, at vi i vores iver efter massiv elektrificering har glemt, at det der VE kræver så meget plads, at det fremover bliver meget vanskeligt at finde tilstrækkeligt med områder til beskyttet natur. Miljøstyrelsen placerer ganske vist 15 procent af Danmarks areal i den kategori ved at medregne opdyrkede arealer som beskyttet natur, når bare de kan finde et vandhul ude i marken. Men Biodiversitetsrådet kan kun finde 2,3 procent. Elselskaberne sår blomster i striber mellem solcelleparkernes paneler, men fagfolk kalder det green- eller biowashing. For et naturligt habitat kan det aldrig blive.

Så lige nu er vi vidner til en masseudryddelse, hvor 48 procent af klodens arter er i tilbagegang. Hvis hasselmus, stor vandsalamander og springfrø herhjemme skal have en chance, skal vi udlægge 30 procent af vores areal til beskyttet natur, sådan som EU foreskriver. Så kan det godt blive svært at få plads til de møller og paneler. En helt overordnet udfordring er dukket op: mangel på plads, når der skal være plads til landbrug, energiproduktion, vand og alle klodens arter.

Juni: Debatten, der ikke vil dø
Vi har to debatter i Danmark, der bliver ved med at springe op igen og igen. Den ene handler om ytringsfrihed. Den anden om a-kraft. 16 førende forskere stod ganske vist i 2022 frem i samlet fl ok og frarådede danske politikere at tage a-kraft med i planlægningen. Teknologien kan hverken hjælpe med at nå klimamålet for 2030 eller betale sig rent økonomisk sammenlignet med vind- og solenergi. Heller ikke, hvis den leverer fjernvarme som sidegevinst. Sådan lød beskeden.

Og Klimarådet var klar i sin opbakning: »Vores analyse viser, at atomkraft ikke er nødvendigt for at sikre elforsyningsikkerheden i Danmark. De udfordringer, der opstår i helt særlige vejrtilfælde uden vind og sol, kan vi klare med andre midler og billigere.« Klimarådet peger selv på tre løsninger, der kan sikre backup, og som rådet vurderer vil være hurtigere at opføre og billigere end a-kraft: ellagring, fleksibelt forbrug og regulerbar elkapacitet med gasturbiner eller termiske kraftværker. En forsikring, der ifølge Klimarådet vil koste hver husstand ca. 100 kroner årligt.

Alligevel ville flere partier på Christiansborg fortsætte diskussionen, mens Liberal Alliance forsøger at samle flertal bag en ‘Niels Bohr-kommission’. Så a-kraftdiskussionen kan ventes snart at komme på besøg igen.

Juli: Øer i et oprørt hav
Med indgangen til det, der skulle blive den varmeste sommer på kloden i 120.000 år med afsvedne marker, skovbrande og oversvømmelser, skulle der krop på de store VE-planer i Danmark. Hvis ‘hockeystaven’ skulle vise sin forudsete effekt, måtte årtiets klimapolitiske prestigeprojekt – energiøerne – sættes i værk. Men efterhånden som projektets kompleksitet gik op for energipolitikerne, dalede begejstringen, og på Borgen fi k øen i Nordsøen nu øgenavnet monsteret. Da det tilmed viste sig, at øen til en pris på 210 milliarder kroner ville ende med et underskud på 5o milliarder kroner, blev projektet udskudt på ubestemt tid.

Energiøen ved Bornholm har ikke bedre fremtidsudsigter. Partierne kunne ganske vist blive enige om statsstøtte på knap 18 milliarder kroner til at etablere den danske del af øens infrastruktur i form af et kabel til Sjælland og Tyskland samt en station på Bornholm. Men øen og møllerne måtte klare sig på markedsvilkår. Med usikker finansiering, lave elpriser og høje råstofpriser betyder det også en usikker fremtid for energiøen ved solskinsøen.

August: Beviser, tak
Fagfolk elsker fakta. Derfor ser vi dem holde armene tæt til kroppen, når forskere påstår, at de har løst et eller andet gammelkendt problem. Fagfolk vil se det afgørende bevis. Bare ikke når det kommer til superledere. Sådan så det i hvert fald ud, da en koreansk forskergruppe lagde en video ud med et lille stykke materiale svævende i luften, et tegn (men ikke bevis) på superlederegenskaber. Og her hævdede de at have skabt superlederegenskaber ved stuetemperatur, hvor det ellers kræver en temperatur tæt på det absolutte nulpunkt. Materialet blev døbt LK-99, er relativt nemt at fremstille af bly, kobber, fosfor og ilt, og snart efterprøvede forskergrupper forsøget kloden rundt. Stor var begejstringen, indtil en erfaren kemiker fra University of Illinois lige gjorde opmærksom på, at det var gammelkendte egenskaber ved kobbersulfid, der havde skabt illusionen. Verden vil bedrages. Eller også skyldes det bare, at opdagelsen af en superleder ved stuetemperatur betyder stensikker nobelpris og et multimilliarddollar-forretningseventyr.

Mens de sydkoreanske forskere trak sig surmulende tilbage, kunne vi til gengæld se en storsmilende Andreas Mogensen svæve ubesværet ind til mandskabet på ISS som en start på sit seks måneders ophold på stationen. Vi har læst om, at han skal fotografere lyn, afprøve en dansk natlampe og måle kvaliteten af sin nattesøvn. Men alle er i virkeligheden mest spændte på, om Andreas får prøvet den rumvandring, han har drømt om, siden han var barn. Han fortjener det.

September: Biosfæren er i fare
Fordelen ved et gennemdigitaliseret samfund er, at vi ved at pulje persondata kan hjælpe den enkelte borger hurtigt og effektivt. Rette eksperter har adgang til rette data i rette sammenhæng. Men. Alle mulige off entligt ansatte kan også bare dykke ned i andres persondata efter forgodtbefi ndende. De ligger jo der, lige til at snage i. Og det har offentligt ansatte i de seneste par år tilsyneladende benyttet sig flittigt af. De har snaget i mødres, fædres, partneres og fremmedes oplysninger, og i mange tilfælde har de slået børn op. Nogle medarbejdere har lavet ét opslag, mens andre har slået hundredvis af borgere op over flere år uden at møde modstand fra myndighederne. Datatilsynet har andet at tage sig til og har således inden for de sidste to år kun reageret på én procent af alle sager om snageri. Så der er frit slag for de nysgerrige, hævngerrige eller jalousiramte.

‘Jorden er langtfra en sikkerhedszone for menneskeheden.’ Ikke nogen rar melding fra forskere, der har opgjort tilstanden for klodens ni planetære grænser, der tilsammen angiver planetens sundhedstilstand i havet, atmosfæren og biosfæren. I den nyeste opgørelse fastslår de, at seks af grænserne er i risikabel eller højrisikabel tilstand. Og det er ikke længere klimaforandringer, der bekymrer dem mest. Nu er det udviklingen i biosfæren, der fremkalder rynkede øjenbryn. Det er biodiversiteten. For den kan mennesket ikke genoprette. Hvis vi først får styr på udledningerne af klimagasser, er vi i en situation, hvor energibalancen på Jorden kan vende retur til et holocæn-lignende niveau inden for nogle tusinde år. Men når vi taber en art, er den tabt for evigt. Vi kan ikke gå tilbage til en biosfære, som ikke har et menneskeligt fingeraftryk.

Oktober: Risikabel havudsigt
Først var det en diskussion om, hvorvidt vi stod over for en hundredårs eller en tusindårshændelse, der fyldte i medierne. Men så kom stormfloden med mere end to meters vandstigning langs landets sydøstlige kyster. En situation, der nok ikke ville komme bag på kystboere mod vest. Men mod øst var alle enten uforberedte eller udstyret med underdimensionerede dæmninger og stormporte. Ikke fordi stormfloden der ikke forelå masser af planer om kystsikring. De var bare aldrig blevet sat i værk med deres færdige tegninger af sandfodring, diger og pumpestationer.

Tre spørgsmål har stået i vejen: Hvem skal betale? Hvad med min havudsigt? Og hvordan skal en lille kommune kunne overskue al den lovgivning, der skal overholdes, når kysten skal ændres? Således blev skibsværftet i Assens oversvømmet, mens sommerhusejere bekymrede sig mest om prisfald som følge af forringet havudsigt. Og således måtte beboere i Køge evakueres, fordi kommunen havde problemer med at flette kystplanerne sammen med EU’s oversvømmelsesdirektiv og habitatdirektiv. Byens borgmester forklarede det i maritime termer: »Vi oplever at skulle navigere i et lovgivningsmæssigt farvand uden sejlrende.«

Udsigten til klimaforandringer stiller imidlertid krav om et opgør med vores romantiserede forhold til danske kyster. Ved en temperaturstigning på 1,6 grader celsius vil Danmark komme til at opleve stormfloder hvert tredje år, og hvis udslippene fortsætter som hidtil, kommer der i slutningen af århundredet 39 gange flere stormfloder, end vi oplever i dag. Der røg den havudsigt.

November: Inde, ude, inde igen
Det er sjældent, man møder ønsket om at blive reguleret fra dem, der skal reguleres. Det sker imidlertid helt åbenlyst fra topfolk i AI-branchen, anført af manden bag ChatGPT, CEO i OpenAI Sam Altmann.

Som en tyv i natten havde han gjort sin sprogmodel tilgængelig og gratis for alle. Skriv dit prompt i vinduet, og se magien. Men lige så tilgængelig den er, lige så farlig er den, lød advarslen, hvorefter Altmann blev sparket ud af af sin egen bestyrelse. Herefter fulgte et af de særeste jobskifte set i en branche, der ellers ikke mangler originaler. Kort efter fyringen ansatte Microsoft, der ejer 49 procent af firmaet, manden og tilbød alle hans 700 ansatte nyt job.Inden for samme uge var han dog tilbage i stolen som CEO i OpenAI. Et firma, han startede som et idealistisk, nonprofit open source-firma, der ville skabe AI til gavn for menneskeheden. Nu en black box med kolossale kommercielle interesser omgivet af mystik og rygter om at ligge inde med en generel AI.

Hele affæren viser den betydning, techgiganterne lægger i AI-kapløbet. Alene Microsoft har kunnet se sin aktie stige med 50 procent siden OpenAI kom med til firmafrokosten. Senest er Amazon gået i markedet med sin egen chatbot, Q, der for 20 USD om måneden angivelig kan gøre arbejdsdagen nemmere for alle. Hastigheden i udviklingen satte EU-Kommissionen grå hår i hovedet, fordi målet flyttede sig konstant, inden EU-Parlamentet omsider kunne vedtage årets vigtigste regulering – AI Act.

December: Varm rekord i en kold tid
Mens en usædvanlig kold start og blæsende afslutning på december lagde sig over landet, lagde grønne initiativer sig til ro i Bruxelles. Med udsigt til valg til EU-Parlamentet i 2024, hvor meningsmålinger på tværs af grænser peger i retning af en højredrejning, udvandes klima- og miljøforslag, hvis ikke de bare lider en stille død på gangene i ­Bruxelles. Dog kan medlemslandene blive enige om at lægge planer for udvinding af sjældne råstoffer, der er kritiske for den grønne omstilling. Hvis vi skal have tilstrækkeligt med vindmøller og batterier til den grønne omstilling, er det bydende nødvendigt at slippe fri af Kinas dominans på området. Vi har ganske vist råstofferne under jordoverfladen. Men igen ramler vi ind i et af årets hovedtemaer: Pladsmanglen, der hele tiden minder os om, at klimakrisen og biodiversitetskrisen risikerer at blive hinandens værste fjender, hvis ikke vi finder en ny vej tilbage til globaliseringen.

Selv om måneden startede koldt, bliver 2023 det varmeste år i menneskehedens historie, kunne FN’s generalsekretær António Guterres oplyse i sin åbningstale ved COP28-klimatopmødet i Dubai. Med udsigt til et 2024, der med hjælp fra El Niño kan gå hen og blive endnu varmere, kunne disse ord fra åbningstalen passende stå som udgangsreplik for 2023:

»Dette år har set samfund rundtom i verden ramt af brande, oversvømmelser og brændende temperaturer. Rekorden i global opvarmning bør sende kuldegysninger ned af ryggen på verdens ledere. Og det bør få dem til at handle.«

Title: Regeringen udskyder Danmarkshistoriens største havvind-udbud
Full text:
Delays again hit Denmark's largest offshore wind expansion, which can supply power to DKK 9 million. Households. There are several months of delay.

It was safe and shown. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Supply would use the turn of the year to kick-start Danish history's largest offshore wind supply of a minimum of 9 GW plus overplanting.

But now the Engineer is experiencing that the ministry is postponing the supply at some point in the spring. The reason is that the Danish Energy Agency and the investors included in the market dialog have not yet reached an agreement on the framework for the 6 GW traditional offshore wind and 3 GW from Energiø Bornholm.

It can make it difficult for the government to achieve its goal of at least having completed the 9 GWs by the end of 2030, warns the consulting company Kraka Advisory:

“If that's right, then it's a shit. We need the green power. It questions whether we will reach it by 2030, which was already very pressed. It has historically taken an average of nine years from the idea of ​​establishing offshore winds until the wind turbines are established. There are only seven years until the end of 2030, ”says Frederik Læsøe Nielsen, senior economist at Kraka Advisory.

There is also annoyance with Marie Münster, professor of energy system analysis and member of the Climate Council. Because even though it is only a few months, it comes up to the fact that the parliamentary elections in its time delayed the process of preparing the market dialogue itself for several months.  

In Marie Münster's assessment, this can mean that Denmark will not be able to deliver enough WE for his own consumption and, for example, will have to import electricity, which is not necessarily green. However, it will first and foremost go beyond the European and global goals, she says, pointing out that emissions from elimport do not count directly in the national climate goals.

"Although such a postponement does not immediately influence our national climate targets in 2030, they have it on the European and the global - and also on our opportunity to emerge as a pioneering country in the field of climate, which we have as a target in the Climate Act. But we are not a role model if we do not have enough to cover our own consumption, ”says Marie Münster.

Uncertainty about sustainability requirements and PTX 
As the Engineer asks the Danish Energy Agency to state how much the supply is delayed, it replies by mail that it "continues" expects to start the supply during the spring. However, that answer does not match the fact that the Board expected to publish the final tender material around the turn of the year, when the initiated market dialogue in June 2023. But it confirms the tip from sources close to the government that the tender will be further delayed.

The mail is stated that the Danish Energy Agency is experiencing a great interest from the market via the market dialogue - which must still be in progress. Against this background, the board is now finalizing the tender material.

If you listen to the water pipes, the delay is not due to dramatic quarrels, rather discussions about the framework of the supply. Some of the discussions are on the string of sustainability requirements that tenders will be the first to embrace - others are on more legal questions about how the state should take care of its ownership. It is difficult for the parties to reach agreement on the extent to which the state has to sell the power to e.g. PTX projects. They are not elements of the state tender. 

But the clock is ticking.

Title: Luftfartens grønne brændstoffer er nødlandet i stilhed
Full text:
The plans to get Danish domestic flights over to sustainable fuels have long prospects. A large -scale project stands still and alternatives are waiting.

In October 2019, the Engineer's posted with a bunch of other journalists to meet at Copenhagen Airport. The occasion was a new report on the production of sustainable flight fuel - also called SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel). 

Behind the report stood researchers from the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) together with the consulting engineering company NIRAS and the organization NISA (Nordic Initiative for Sustainable Aviation), and the message was that SAF could be produced at a price of 'only' three times the price of fossil fuels. In practice, that would mean an extra cost of airline tickets of about 30 percent.

The technology was clear, and if the right decisions were made, the authors at that time believed that the first production plant to make 100 percent green flight fuel could be ready as early as 2025.

The room emanated with enthusiasm and powerpoints were shown with advanced flow charts and thorough schedules. The parties behind the report praised, and the undersigned had difficulty penetrating with a critical question of the schedule. For how sure were the participants that such a project was implemented on time?

Erik C. Wormslev, then Development Manager for Climate, Energy and Resources at NIRAS and co -author of the report, was optimistic and emphasized that much of the technology could already be purchased, for example the electrolysis units. 

"I don't think it will be a problem in five years," he said, believing that it would be possible to "build a demonstration system of 50-100 MW with enough money in the back.

Ready by 2025?
In round numbers, aircraft accounted for three percent of global CO2 emissions in 2023, which may not seem gigantic. But the problem with aircraft is that they are far more difficult to make climate -friendly than, for example, petrol cars, which in many places can be replaced relatively easily with electric cars. 

There are many trials in the process of short-fledged batteries, hydrogen engines hydrogen engines and-what was the plan in the SDU report-synthetic fuels that can replace fossils 1: 1.

So more than four years after the airport meeting is the good question whether by the end of 2025 we are ready to pour home -produced SAF into the tanks on the planes at the airport at Amager? 

The short answer is no, and the prospect of being able to do within the coming years must be said to be highly questionable.

In 2019, Ørsted had probably received DKK 34.6 million. DKK in support to construct an electrolysis system of 2 MW with associated hydrogen storage. 

The energy was to come from wind power, but already after a short time COWI was out and warn against using fluctuating electricity from wind turbines to electrolysis. The challenge was, Technical Manager Jeppe Grue explained to get the plant to run flexibly, so it can play with the electricity and heating system and absorb the variation in production from the wind turbines.

By 2020, the large -scale project 'Green Fuels for Denmark' was then launched with Ørsted at the forefront and COWI as technical adviser. The goal was to create Denmark's most ambitious project for large-scale production of sustainable e-fuel based on green electricity from wind turbines. 

By 2030, the total electrolysis capacity should be 1.3 GW with a potential to avoid emission of one million tonnes of CO2 over the first ten years of operation.

In 2022, the project received a grant, this time at DKK 600 million. DKK from the Danish Business Authority, to participate in the European IPCEI program. The program aims to support areas of action that the European Commission has decided to be the leader of the EU's future. This applies, among other things, to hydrogen and e-fuel.

Today, COWI does not want to comment further on the project but passes the request to Ørsted, which refers to a response from the fall of 2023 when the engineer last wrote about the project. 

Here Lars Hansen, who is Ørsted's director of PTX in Denmark, acknowledged that "Green Fuels for Denmark is challenged, both due to rising costs, but also because of the lack of new, green power in Eastern Denmark."

The concession came shortly after the offshore wind turbine park had been postponed and risked completely dropping. Nor is it better with Energiø Bornholm, where the supply of 3 GW offshore wind has once again been paused.

Discouraged project participants
Nevertheless, Ørsted has not canceled Green Fuels for Denmark. The company states that efforts are being made to have it implemented despite the challenges, and PTX director Lars Hansen writes in an email to the Engineer that they are still in close dialogue with potential customers of SAF: 

"The final timeline for the production of SAF depends on the needs of the customers and the development of the necessary technology."

We have also asked the other participants who in their time joined Green Fuels. Many have not responded to our inquiry, but generally the reactions here seem four years after discouraged.

From Copenhagen Airports, it sounds from the Director of Public Affairs Søren Rosenkilde Clausen that it is "confident that the project can make a significant contribution in the foreseeable future." 

DFDS, which should have been the customer of both methanol and hydrogen, still support the ambition and hopes that "a way rather than Green Fuels Denmark can be found," while DSV and the City of Copenhagen have not returned on the Engineer's request.

Pity for aviation
The need for the green fuels became clear when Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, in his New Year's speech on January 1, 2022, announced that by 2025 there should be a green flight route in Denmark and that all domestic routes in 2030 should fly on green fuels. She did not mention specifically SAF, but since commercial electric aircraft is still a few years out in the future, SAF would be the obvious choice.

Therefore, today, the director of the Nordic Initiative of Sustainable Aviation, Martin Porsgaard, who was sitting with the presentation of the SDU project in 2019 is also annoyed that they have no longer come.

“Unfortunately, the expansion with wind turbines, which was to supply the green electricity, is lagging afterwards. There is also uncertainty about the CO2 to be used in the fuel, and hydrogen production has more focus on exports to Germany than on the production of SAF in Denmark, ”he says.

The only real green alternative to aviation fuel is today made from used cooking oil, also called UCO (USED COOKING OIL). But also UCO there is uncertainty as resources are limited and the documentation that it is actually based on used fryer oil is often uncertain.

“I would think that by 2025 there may be a route ready at UCO, presumably imported from Asia. The synthetic fuels based on PTX have longer prospects, ”says Martin Porsgaard.

Mixing and passenger tax
In the EU, in the summer of 2023, it was decided that all aircraft flying commercially in the Union must have 2 percent green fuel mixed in 2025, 6 percent by 2030 and 70 percent by 2050. Only a very small part will come from synthetic sources.

Critics point out that in the first many years only UCO will be available, most of which is imported from Asia. Here it is emphasized that the risk of cheating with the used oils is great.

In December, the Danish government followed up on the EU requirement with an agreement on a tax on airline tickets. Specifically, this means that the tax will be phased in from 2025, so that air travel by 2030 will be more expensive by 2030. It should give a proceeds of about DKK 900 million. DKK 2025 increasing to DKK 1.2 billion. DKK in 2030.

Now one might think that the tax revenue should be used to make air transport more green, but the government chose to spend about DKK 600 million. DKK of the proceeds for an increase in the elderly check.

It frustrates Jeppe Juul, who is the transport policy chief of the environmental organization Council for Green Change. He fears that instead of green flight fuel, like those that should have been manufactured in the Green Fuel project, we will import UCO of a questionable nature.

“And when you want to spend only a third of the proceeds from the passenger tax to the green transition in air transport, then what we think it will be strange. There are simply incentives to invest in real synthetic fuels in Denmark, ”he says. Therefore, he trusts that clean electric aircraft will be ready by 2030.

Martin Porsgaard also saw that the entire proceeds from the passenger tax were spent on the development of SAF.

"I would recommend that we reduce the purchase of UCO-SAF from Asia, and instead accumulate the financial means to accelerate PTX-based SAF produced in Denmark."

Title: Biomasse eller grøn el: To veje til grøn luftfart
Full text:
The road for green fuel for aviation was paved, but with Ørsted at the forefront, Green Fuels for Denmark chose a different path than researchers recommended. It may have put the project back.

In the end, all certified aircraft fuel is the same. Or, to put it another way, it doesn't matter where the fuel comes from. Whether it is fossil or synthetic once it is filled on an aircraft, it must live up to some very specific requirements.

But there is a difference between where the energy comes from and where the mature technology for the manufacture of green flight fuel (SAF) is-and that was the starting point for the SDU report 'A Pre-Feasibility Study on Sustainable Aviation Fuel From Biogas, Hydrogen and CO2' from 2019.

The basic principle of the report was that Jetfuel should be produced based on Biomethane and/or CO2 and hydrogen. Either by a traditional steam reform of the biomethane, thereby forming pure synthesis gas (H2) and carbon monoxide (CO), or via the so-called Reverse-Water-Gas-Shift reaction between CO2 and hydrogen, thereby also forming synthesis gas. 

Subsequently, the synthesis gas could be used in the well-known Fischer tropsch process to make SAF. The technologies were known at that time and for most people commercially available.

Although it was SDU and NIRAS who was responsible for the technical description and the calculations in the project, then you should notice the companies that had financed the report. Here you could find Copenhagen Airports, SAS, ARC, Danish Aviation, Dansk Energi (now Green Power Denmark) and Nature Energy, which produced the biogas to use.

Should be ready by 2023
In 2020, a large number of companies launched the Green Fuels project for Denmark. At the forefront was now Ørsted and several of the participants were gangsters from the SDU report.

With on board were also DSV, DFDS, Maersk, Topsoe and the hydrogen companies Nel and Everfuel. 

On the other hand, biogas producer Nature Energy was out, and there is an important point in it. For there was no longer anyone talking about using methane from biogas and hydrogen, extracted from biomass. Now, fuel, sea, sea and air transport based on electrolysis should be produced using green electricity from wind turbines and CO2 from biogenic sources. 

The first step of the project was to be ready in 2023 and consist of a 10 MW electrolysis unit that could immediately supply hydrogen to buses and trucks. 

The second step should be ready in 2027, and here the hydrogen production should be 250 MW based on electricity from a brand new wind farm at Bornholm, which was part of the Energiø project. Based on the hydrogen, methanol was to be produced with CO2 from Copenhagen point sources, such as the Avedøreværket or waste incineration.

In the third step, the entire potential for offshore wind from Bornholm was to be exploited and electrolysis capacity is scaled up to 1.3 GW. In total, 250,000 tonnes of sustainable fuels were to be produced for use in buses, trucks, ships and aircraft. In 2027, the project could potentially replace 5 per cent. of the fossil fuels used at Copenhagen Airport and as much as 30 per cent. by 2030.

A completely different way
“But it was a completely different path than the one we had suggested. We started from the green biogas, which was already in the gas network, and considered hydrogen from electrolysis as the expensive part. But Green Fuels for Denmark chose to start with electrolysis and bet that cheap electricity would come from the upcoming offshore wind farms, 'says Henrik Wenzel, a professor at SDU, head of' Life Cycle Engineering 'and one of the lead authors of the original Proposal from 2019.

On top of that, Henrik Wenzel is adamant that the road from Methanol to E-Kerosen, ie Jetfuel, is an unnecessary extra process step, which at that time still only worked on laboratory scale and ultimately makes the products more expensive.

“I cannot deny that the production of methanol and subsequent jetfuel in the longer term can be profitable. But if they had gone the methane way as we suggested, then I am sure that the first test system for the production of Jetfuel would have been ready today, ”says Henrik Wenzel.

As mentioned earlier, Topsoe had joined the Green Fuels for the Denmark project, and that might have been a good reason. Topsoe are experts in the process by which synthesis gas is converted into methanol. 

Today, Topsoe denies to the Engineer that the company demanded that the effort be made on electrolysis and methanol so that they would join the project. Ørsted does not want to comment on whether it was a requirement from Topsoe to go the methanol way.

"We chose to focus on electric -based solutions for Green Fuels for Denmark because they are in natural extension of our existing activities," writes Lars Hansen, Ørsted's director of PTX in Denmark, in an email. However, he emphasizes that many different technologies are needed to decarbonize Denmark and the world, including both electricity -based solutions and solutions based on biogas.

Title: Ørsted og Elia: Nye mølleparker bør være ‘hybrider’ som Kriegers Flak
Full text:
The energy company Ørsted, together with Belgian Elia, has made four proposals on how to create a basis for expanding wind power at sea across borders.

Some countries have a large energy needs and some countries have large wind resources. This imbalance will try to come to life with four new proposals, which together will ensure that wind power in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea is expanded more optimally and for the benefit of more countries.

However, the challenge is that the countries have many different actors, different legislation and opportunities for investment in renewable energy.

The collaboration was presented today at the Windeurope conference in Bilbao. Present at the presentation was also the Minister of Climate, Energy and Supply Lars Aagaard, the Belgian Minister of Energy Tinne van der Straeten and the EU's Director General of Energi, Ditte Jørul Jørgensen.

Europe must cooperate on VE
Behind the initiative are the energy companies Ørsted and the Belgian system operator, Elia Group. Together, they have developed a model and a number of recommendations that they believe can break down the barriers that make it difficult today to link offshore wind farms with two or more countries.

It may seem like two companies with different agendas, but CEO of Elia Group, Catherine Vandenborre, does not see it as a problem.

“We share more common perceptions of wind energy and so we believe that it is better to exchange energy across borders than the individual countries follow national interests and build wind farms that are linked to their own network. If it continues, then we do not reach the goals of the EU. Instead, we wanted to gather our powers to find solutions. "

Olivia Breese, director of Ørsted Europe, sees the development of wind turbines in Europe, is currently balancing on a knife egg.

“The speed of rollout of the road and speed is essential - we need new solutions to achieve the goals of Europe. These must be solutions that break down some of the silos that are in the energy system. By finding solutions together, we can bring actors together and create opportunities, both for us as actors and for society in general, ”she said by a press presentation.

Therefore, the conference in Bilbao is also a good opportunity to get both politicians and the industry to speak, says Olivia Breese.

"If we can get a political mandate to move forward with solutions, then we can get started solving both the technical, organizational and financial aspects for further work." She says.

Need 'hybrid solutions'
What they suggest are called 'hybrid projects'. The type of wind farms is only one of the world and it is warrior flak between Denmark and Germany that has been connected to the electricity grid since 2021. 

Here, Denmark and Germany are connected via an electric cable that is connected directly to the wind farm. Thus, it is possible to send the energy to where the price is highest. If the wind does not blow, the cable can be used for normal transfer of electricity between the two countries.

So if the extension of offshore wind turbines and green energy is to go faster than today, then many more of these types of projects are needed, they write the two energy companies in a new report.

However, the challenges of building this type of offshore wind farms are many, it is emphasized. 

For example, they may be different legislation between two countries that put obstacles in the way. But also national interests and access to investments are made more difficult when wind farms need to be linked to two countries.

When two countries are connected, according to the two parties, there will also be some asymmetry in the benefit. For example, there may be consumers, large and small, in one country that has a greater advantage than in the other, however, without having contributed investments.

The two companies will now try to do something about it and therefore they have put four proposals in the lake that will make it easier. See fact box.

Energy must be distributed
As an example of an area where this type of plant can make the extension much more efficient and contemporary accommodate several countries, it is pointed out on the North Sea, where all wind farms have so far been built as single parks with a so-called 'point-to-point' connection to land. Energy has then been distributed between the countries via cables. This is also called a radial network.

But if the countries around the North Sea are to benefit more from the large wind resources there are, then it will be more optimal, with a hybrid network where cables on the sea bottom connect the wind farms and send the energy ashore where it is most needed for it. . 

In this way, cables can be saved on land and at the number of connection points between offshore wind farms and land.


The connection is known from the Danish Parker Horns Rev I and II, which is connected via each of their cable to land.

In the hybrid version, the mills will be connected to, for example, a converter platform or an energy island, after which the energy is distributed to the markets where customers are.

In this way, the authors behind the report also emphasize, it is possible for those countries that do not have as large wind resources as Denmark, for example, to participate more actively in the expansion.

The fact that the North Sea has some of the best wind resources in the world has been documented several times. The area is windy, has relatively low sea depths and is close to large consumption areas in both Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands.

Therefore, expansion with hybrid networks must also be seen in the light of the Esbjerg Declaration, where ministers from Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium set a target of expansion with 150 GW wind power in the North Sea 2050.

Calculations from the pan-European organization for transmission companies ENTSO-E show that if the offshore wind farms are built with hybrid connections to land, then the hybrid parks could only contribute 80 GW capacity by 2050.

At present, there are 6 projects in the mold that goes under the concept of 'hybrid' - this also includes the two Danish energy islands in the North Sea and Bornholm respectively. All the projects have starting dates, which are after 2030.

Title: Synspunkt: Politikerne overbyder hinanden på energiområdet
Outlet:
Ingeniøren
Frederik Læssøe Nielsen, Seniorøkonom, Kraka Advisory
Full text:
It is a lemming effect on steroids when politicians will be first and greatest in the climate fight without funding or a sensible plan.

The green agenda has become commonplace, partly because the challenges of climate change are becoming clearer and more tangible day by day and partly because energy policy has become a security policy after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Therefore, of course, it is both good and expected that among the political parties there is also broad support for the ambitious Danish reduction targets and a desire to make the country independent of fossil fuels from Russia and other inconvenient trading partners.

In fact, it has become almost political suicide to appear as a relaxation on climate and energy issues. And while it may sound good to the Danish voters who are hungry for solutions in the green transition, it is in many respects the exact opposite.

The fear of appearing as a climate patch leads to bad, hasty decisions that make us less green change for money, or the transition becomes unnecessary expensive for taxpayers. From the outside, the hunt for the greenest profile looks like a lemming effect on steroids, where it is more important to demonstrate the power of action than the decisions are made on a proper basis.

It's no longer enough to follow. If you want to appear green, you have to constantly overbid and you cannot afford to be thoughtful for fear of being confused with a relax. And thoughtlessness can prove to be expensive - there are several examples. Perhaps the most obvious example of politicians making poor socio -economic decisions so that they can at least not be blamed for being climate -lapping is Energiø Bornholm.

It was originally decided with a built -in prerequisite that it should only be established if it was profitable. But when it came to an end, and a project -economic deficit of only about 10 billion. DKK, which has since developed into state aid needs of as much as DKK 31.5 billion. DKK, towered, the premise was tacitly ignored, while expanding the project from 2 gigawatts to 3 gigawatts. Now the politicians have agreed to put a ceiling on the support of DKK 17.6 billion. DKK, but no one in the process was willing to raise the hand and point out the obvious, namely that the prerequisites of the agreement had progressed emphatically.

At the same time, the energy island in the North Sea is paused because it turned out to require 50 billion. DKK in state aid. But instead of putting it finally in the grave, the civil service is working on a cheaper solution. However, that solution is hardly profitable either. But the vacant stance on dropping the expensive prestige projects is none to take. Therefore, the debate fails, and the general taxpayer cannot be earned when it is large double -digit billion bills.

Politicians will quadruple the production of renewable energy on land, five-fold production of renewable energy at sea and have 4-6 gigawatt electrolysis capacity that can split water into green hydrogen and oxygen-all by 2030. But it is unclear why Denmark should have they ambitions, because they are not motivated by analyzes or arguments, and they provide far more power and hydrogen than Denmark can use in the foreseeable future.

And while it seems relatively harmless when politicians announce ambitious goals because, in isolation, it costs nothing to have great ambitions, the problem arises afterwards. Because once an ambition is announced, it can also be used by others to motivate political actions: 'If the state does not finance a hydrogen tube to Germany when we never reach our goal of 4-6 Gigawatt Electrolysis Capacity'.

In this way, the unmotivated goals suddenly become arguments in themselves and at the same time something that future politicians will also have to control, no matter how bad it is for the social economy and thus the opportunity to actually get as much change for money as possible. In this way, the outline of the climate is painting contemporary and future politicians into an inconvenient corner, where they are relegated to either pursuing unpublished politics or appearing as relaxer.

Objectives and ambitions are of course good at the direction of the transition, but it is crucial that they are backed by professional analyzes and good arguments, otherwise we end up with political agreements that bind politicians to lead inappropriate expensive climate policy. Not only does Denmark thus get less green transition for the money, we also risk losing the broad support in the population.

Title: Minister advarer: Belgisk valg truer energiø til over 200 milliarder kroner

The imminent Belgian choice makes it difficult to realize Energiø North Sea. This is stated in a note that Climate Minister Lars Aagaard has sent to the Folketing's Finance Committee.

Title: Energiøer på randen af fallit: Afhængig af umulig EU-støtte

Government officials are considering the fate of the two Energiø projects in the North Sea and Bornholm respectively. This happens because the cost of establishing the islands has grown unmistakably large and neither neighboring countries nor the EU can afford to support it.

The Ministry informs via mail that they are investigating the possibilities of EU funding and better framework conditions to spread costs beyond several countries. The Ministry considers both Energy Islands to be "projects for the benefit of Europe's green transition", which "therefore can be a candidate for several EU support pools that the government actively searches for the possibilities."

However, it seems optimistic bordering on the naive to believe that the EU can cover the islands' double -digit billion deficits. For the amounts that the Union usually gives to such energy projects is small money. The part of the EU's budget that is earmarked for it is adapted to a world as it looked before needed supply chains and inflation pushing prices dramatically. It was a world of low cost and interest. But that world no longer exists.

One of the largest amounts the EU has ever given to energy projects has been awarded the Kriegers Flak Officer between Bornholm and Zealand, which is divided into a Danish and a German part. Here, the two countries received a few billion kroner in support of establishing a cable to link the parts together. The cable gives the countries an opportunity to send electricity to each other if they are missing.

According to Jan Bentzen, two billion kroner is an incredibly high amount of support from the EU. But two billion kroner proposes as a tailor in hell compared to being able to cover Energiø North Sea's expected project deficit of more than 50 billion kroner. And they still leave a large billion deficit if they were to be used solely to finance the cable Triton Link, which is scheduled to be withdrawn about 1000 km from Denmark to Belgium and which in itself should cost at least 15 billion kroner.

"The EU can't just give more in support, because if it were to bat, it should be with a factor of 10-20, and that money is not found at all," says Jan Bentzen.

Hope was light green
Although support from the EU does not appear to be able to save the two energy islands today, it could actually have moved something, when the then Danish climate and energy minister Dan Jørgensen (S) in 2020 pricked the Belgian energy minister Tinne van der Straeten on the shoulder to make her enter into an agreement to pay part of the bill. For that time Energiø North Sea was just on the tilt of profitability. There were only $ 3.5 billion to convince the Belgians that it was a good idea.

So, a deficit, the Danish regulator, the Supply Authority, would undoubtedly have accepted, as what authority has public coffers in the back and thus can afford to look great at smaller crunches in the economy in its eternal struggle to achieve Danish security of supply.

But the case is a completely different one in Belgium, whose regulator CREG is an independent public body formed by law. Among other things, CREG must approve the costs that are overwhelmed by the TSO Elia's consumers via tariffs, which is why they have a watchful eye on costs.

Therefore, in the negotiations between Belgium and Denmark, CREG is constantly putting their foot down. And only the Belgian minister succeeded in giving the negotiations artificial respiration by holding CRG with promises that the EU would probably support it.

However, that hope diminished as the Ukraine war and pressed supply chains have beaten material prices. For it has more than doubled the amount that is missing to make CRG satisfied.

So where the Belgian minister previously spoke warmly about a possible Danish-Belgian energy cooperation, she is now busy stating that "the connection will only turn into something if it receives EU support and can pay for the Belgian consumers".

Although the negotiations are now also being challenged by the upcoming Belgian parliamentary elections in June, it does not for the time being the Danish government to drop Belgium as a possible partner. There are not many others to go to, as Denmark has previously tried in vain with Germany, the Netherlands and Norway before Belgium came into play. It didn't really lead to anything. Still, the government is now trying again with Germany with the hope of saving the project.

The last convulsions
Although negotiations are still underway, a lot is suggesting that both projects end up being dropped. This is despite the fact that the European Commission and Wind Europe estimate that the EU will need 2000-2500 GW of renewable energy, of which 400 GW is offshore wind and 100 GW must be supplied by Energiø-like projects.

In that light, the Energy Islands are essential for the EU to reach climate neutrality in a cost -effective way, points out Nicolai Bech Kofoed, the think tank Concito's constituted program manager for the EU. 

Although the economy looks difficult for the Energy Islands, one would probably be able to reach the goal if everyone agreed with each other to cooperate. The problem is that we are up on a scale where it hurts financially on the individual country to get involved. So that's why no one really dares to say yes. 

“Seen from a socio-economic point of view, I think it is strange that you choose to build an energy island at Bornholm, which requires massive state aid when you can build offshore projects without state aid elsewhere in the country. So it really just seems like a waste of taxpayers' money. When you look at it from a macroeconomic point of view, it is difficult to rationalize, ”says Peter Kjær Kruse-Andersen.

Title: Krisen i den grønne sektor: Ingeniører søgte mod nye brancher »hen over natten«

Otherwise, it went just as well in the green sector, but crises, governmental treatments and lack of investments can make companies stay back with hiring.

For many, it came as a surprise when the energy company Ørsted on February 7 this year announced that 800 should be fired in the group. Otherwise, Ørsted has been at the forefront of the green transition in Denmark for the last 10-15 years and has during that period moved from Danish wind farms beyond the country's borders and invested in solar cell and wind turbine projects in countries such as the USA, Korea, Taiwan, Sweden , Britain and Germany. 

Now the message was that write -downs on offshore wind projects in the United States had pushed the economy so much that the costs had to be cut - that is, it was on layoffs.

In April, it was LM Wind Power in Kolding, who announced that 179 Danish employees could look forward to a guy's note. The message from the owner, US General Electric, was clear: LM Wind Power needs to be 'transformed' into a smaller, more lean and more profitable business.

Braking
Although there are no general figures on the development, the above indicates that the green sector is no longer roaring out there. 

Or as Emil Plaugmann, a partner and headhunter in the consultancy Capax Recruitment, puts it, the green transition has not stopped, but it has gone from full speed to a decided slowdown.

“We could already feel in the fall that something was on the way. Here we began to get inquiries from employees in several large companies in the green sector that asked about the opportunities to change jobs. Either because they were actively looking for in their careers or because they could feel that there was a change on the road that might have required a trade change. The experience at Capax was that several large companies discovered that they had been hired for many in the green part of the business and that there was now a need to adapt the size of the departments.

"In particular, I think more large consulting and consulting companies had built up for large departments with a focus on green projects and that there should be trimming now," he says.

Green sector has grown
Such announcements are in sharp contrast to the development of recent years. 

The universities have trained engineers and voice candidates, and companies such as Ørsted, Vestas, Siemens and a large number of the advisers have hired them. It has been fully in line with the political framework, which was especially implemented in the legally binding climate law of 2020, which confirmed that Denmark must reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 70 by 70 percent compared to the level in 1990, and that we must be A climate neutral society by 2050.

By 2021, IDA could tell on the basis of a calculation from the Labor Movement's Business Council of IDA's climate response 2045 that a fulfillment of the government's 70-percent objective would create 415,000 jobs spread over 10 years, equivalent to 41,500 jobs a year.

45,000 extra employees needed

Title: Synspunkt: Giv mig bare ét godt argument for at opføre Energiø Bornholm
Outlet:
Ingeniøren, Frederik Læssøe Nielsen
Seniorøkonom, Kraka Advisory
Full text:
It must be evidently for anyone interested that the economy of the energy island project at Bornholm is extremely challenged: DKK 31.5 billion. DKK is the bill for the state if you ask the officials of the Danish Energy Agency, but 'only' DKK 17.6 billion. DKK if you ask the conciliation parties. 

For the politicians have added a ceiling to how expensive the project must be for the Danes. Most recently, however, Lars Aagaard has opened the door to find more money if the ceiling should be exceeded.

The $ 31.5 billion According to the government's own officials in the Danish Energy Agency, the price of the energy island has for the Danes if one is to hope to attract private investors.  

If the conciliation parties decide to find more money in the event that the Danish Energy Agency is right, it is unfortunately not the first time the politicians have looked big on already made agreements and lifting to the Danes about the price of Energiø Bornholm. When the project was first adopted, it was assuming that it had to be established only if it was profitable.  

It is also with reference to the poor economy that the Danish People's Party has recently resigned from the settlement. And the proponents who, in the infancy, - as profitability analyzes had not yet punctured the project's finances - proclaimed it as a Danish flagship project with great financial perspectives for both treasury and export companies, has today completely left that narrative and now cling to new arguments, While one can fear that there is now no limit to how bad the economy one will accept. The problem is that the new arguments are not particularly good either.   

Wind turbines at Bornholm contribute only limited to Danish security of supply
The most frequently used argument for the energy island now is that it contributes to Danish and European security of supply. And yes, it does to a limited extent, but in the most molbo-like way: The improved security of supply stems from the fact that the project connects Eastern Denmark with Germany with a transmission cable that enables import and export of power in situations with respectively . Lack and excess of power.

But if the main purpose of the energy island project is to ensure greater integration of the Danish and the German electricity market, it should happen in the cheapest possible way. It simply cannot be the socio -economic best way of connecting Zealand with Germany to do so with a cable from Zealand, across the Baltic Sea to Bornholm and on to Germany. 

The contribution from the wind turbines at Bornholm is only quite limited, which the Danish Energy Agency has also made politicians aware of. This is because there is already a lot of offshore wind in the Baltic Sea, which will produce electricity with the same time profile as the mills in the energy island project, and therefore extra wind turbines do not contribute particularly in situations where the power production is low. 

There are plenty of good reasons to increase electricity market integration between North and Southern Europe, but of course it has to be done properly and not just act as an excuse to continue with a financially disastrous project where the part of the project that can be justified could be obtained Cheaper.

Bornholm is not ideal for PTX production
Another argument for Energiø Bornholm is that energy production should be used for the production of hydrogen and other PTX products. That argument is often performed by politicians or other actors who at the same time argue that Bornholm will in the future be used as a gas station for passing ships in the Baltic Sea. The problem, however, is that Bornholm is hardly the obvious place for PTX production-neither with nor without the role of the Baltic Sea's gas station.

A report from DTU, comparing production costs on Bornholm with the costs of Western Europe, USA and China, shows that it will be the most expensive to produce hydrogen and to process it to ammonia if you do it on Bornholm. 

This means that PTX production on Bornholm is hardly competitive in terms of production costs and thus price.

Even if one assumes that Bornholm must be the Baltic Sea's gas station, it does not make sense to produce green fuels on Bornholm. This is because it is cheap to transport liquid fuels by ship, and therefore the green fuels of the future are likely to be produced where it is cheapest to produce hydrogen. And it is probably in sunny countries like Spain with plenty of room for solar cells as they produce the cheapest power.

So we still have the good to hear just a single good argument for establishing the billion -dollar Energiø Bornholm. If you are with an argument, we can test it in the comments section of this lump.

Title: Datacentre under vandet blev spået en stor fremtid: Nu kasserer Microsoft idéen
Full text:
The future of lowering data centers in the sea to save cooling looks questionable, after Microsoft has in silence has given up underwater data centers.

Stable temperatures, no oxygen that oxidizes and no fumbling technicians. When Microsoft, after two years, raised an underwater data center that had been on the bottom of the sea off the coast of Scotland, the results were promising.

But after chewing on the results for a few years, Microsoft now throws the towel in the ring and gives up a future with underwater data centers. It writes the media Data Center Dynamics.

“I do not build underwater data centers anywhere in the world. We learned a lot about work below sea level and about vibrations and influence on the server. Now we use the experience in other areas, ”says Noelle Walsh, head of the company's cloud operations + innovation (CO + I) department, to Data Center Dynamics.

Project Natick was started back in 2013. 855 servers were enclosed inside a cylindrical container that was filled with nitrogen before it was lowered into the sea.

In order to compare the underwater servers, Microsoft set up 135 similar servers in a standard data center on land and let the two data centers perform the same tasks in Microsoft's Azure cloud.

Fewer servers broke under water
Only six of the 855 submarine servers broke down compared to eight out of the 135 on land, and Microsoft points to the stable outdoor temperatures as a factor in success.

Microsoft initially had two explanations for why the data center underwater has done so well.

First, the container has been emptied of oxygen and has instead been filled with nitrogen that does not strain metal components with corrosion. In fact, computer hardware does not work very well in regular office environments where the air oxidizes the electronics, as well as fluctuations in temperature and humidity depending on the season also consume the electronics.

Secondly, Microsoft believes that the lack of technician visits - nobody has been watching the data center for two years - also has a positive impact on the number of errors on the servers. No one has encountered the server racks on the bottom of the sea, nor has cables been switched or disconnected along the way.

Microsoft at the time concluded that "underwater data centers were" reliable, practical and energy -friendly. "

Expensive to dig on the bottom of the ocean
However, when the solution has not been successful, it is probably because the cost of installing and operating a data center underwater is too high.

The data center must be linked to existing land -based infrastructure in the form of electricity grids and fiber infrastructure.

Pulling cables on the bottom of the sea is not cheap and repairs are costly.

Microsoft's vague announcements about vibrations and influence on the server suggest that the servers have had difficulty dealing with vibrations and movements.

Another challenge is security. The Nord Stream Sabotage in the Baltic Sea as well as a number of over-won cables off the Norwegian and Finnish coasts have shown that underwater infrastructure is vulnerable to hybrid war. A group of American and Japanese security researchers showed earlier this year, what it was easy to carry out a so -called acoustic attack on servers lowered in water.

»The biggest benefits of having a data center underwater are the free cooling and insulation from changing environments on land. But these two advantages can also turn into problems because the density of the water carries acoustic signals faster than in the air, and the isolated data center is difficult to monitor or service if components break, says Jahidul Islam, professor of electro and computer technology at University of Florida.

Energy Islands Scrinkled
In connection with the design of an energy island in the North Sea, GlobalConnect suggested that a data center be established in connection with the energy island, which has both access to electricity grids and fiber networks.

However, that project is also laid in the grave. Last year, however, the government decided to pause the supply of energy island in the North Sea, as are the plans for an underwater data center as a neighbor.

Although you are hardly going to retrieve data deep below sea level, the project may change the setup in a data center.

The idea of ​​removing technicians and automating the operation of data centers lives on at Microsoft.

“We look more at robotics from the perspective that some of these new servers will be very heavy. How can we automate it instead of having people to push things around, says Noelle Walsh of Microsoft to Datacenterdynamics.

In addition to Microsoft, two other companies, one American and one Chinese, are working on spreading the idea of ​​data centers underwater. Last year, Chinese Beijing Highlander lowered a 1.3 ton heavy data center at 35 meters depth, while US Subsea Cloud is working on a smaller version of an underwater data center that can be lowered several kilometers down the sea bottom.

However, both companies are still in the test phase.

Subsea Cloud is establishing test sites off the UK and Norway, while so far only a Chinese data center has been lowered.

Title: Leder: Den grønne trepartsaftale er ikke så historisk endda: Hvor blev det grønne udstillingsvindue af?
Full text:
Then we got an agreement on CO2 tax on agriculture as part of a so-called 'green tripartite'. The Minister of Taxation called it "world history" and the chairman of Agriculture & Food believed that other countries in the world can learn something.

But is Denmark really a pioneering country, and do we really go ahead and show that it can be possible to have both economic growth and falling CO2 emissions or other green progress?

When the Engineer's articles about, for example, CO2-saving solutions and public grants for green technology find their way to social media, this comment always appears in some form: 'Denmark is so small a country that we do not mean a shit in The big picture, so why should we spend money (taxes) on reducing CO2 emissions? '

The question is relevant, and the answer is, among other things, about the ethical and moral responsibility we have as citizens of a nation that undoubtedly has one of the largest climate footprints on the planet measured per year. per capita-both in terms of domestic consumption and all the CO2 emissions that we very deftly do not include when we buy electric cars and fly to Thailand. The government's own report GA24 shows that half of the Danes' climate imprint in 2022 of 11 tonnes per year. inhabitant took place abroad.

It is true that in the global image we do not mean much and our local efforts even less. But in the Climate Act of 2019 it actually states that Denmark has a moral responsibility and to be a pioneering country in the international climate effort, so that we can inspire and influence the rest of the world.

The promises were repeated in the fall of 2023, when the government released the report Climate Program 2023: "As a rich and well -functioning country, Denmark must take the lead as a green pioneering country". It included, among other things, an industry that will develop and export solutions that the whole world can benefit from.

During these months, however, the criticism hits the government due to creative maths, which with a snap removes millions of tonnes of CO2, so the 70 percent reduction target is now within reach. And organizations such as Dansk Industri and Dansk Erhverv have stated in a joint press release on energy efficiency: "The government's desk exercises are not worthy of a green pioneer."

It does not stop there: a previous first place on the 'Environmental Performance Index', which the US University Yale publishes annually, has been exchanged for a tenth place by countries such as the UK, Sweden and Norway. And when Director of Quality of Life in the EU Commission's Environment Directorate Veronica Manfredi in May was in Copenhagen, she expressed disappointment with the discharges of wastewater to our already overloaded marine environment.

The criticism puts the government and the announcement of Denmark as a technological showcase for green technology in a difficult position. For exports and the positive, global impact are limited to few areas. It is also evident from GA24, where it can be read that almost 60 percent of the export of energy technology consists of wind turbines, and when it comes to the CO2-saving effects of environmental technologies, the water sector accounts for 67 percent of exports.

At the same time, the Danish energy industry faces massive challenges in many of the areas that should have been demonstration projects for further export. New wind turbines on land have dried out, PTX plants are exposed, and the energy island in the North Sea is probably placed in the grave.

However, there are bright spots: For more than a decade, the Danish Energy Agency has a collaboration with a large number of countries, including the USA, China, India and South Africa, with the aim of sharing Danish experience, know -how, technical solutions and regulatory frameworks for countries maintain economic growth and a high electricity supply security. In a whole new analysis of the Vietnamese electricity system, the government emphasizes that Denmark here can contribute with experience and knowledge to help Vietnam meet the country's target of climate neutrality by 2050.

But in general, the experience of teaching other countries lies to be green gradually far back-when we disconnected CO2 emissions from economic growth in the 90s and 00s-and that does not fix the green tripartite agreement: the think tank Concito believes, for example, That the CO2 tax is "disappointingly low" and will not sufficiently promote investments in new technology. Conservative politician Anders Storgaard even believes that "agriculture laughs all the way to the slurry tank".

Maybe the deal is not so world historical even - at least not seen with green glasses. Far more and more stronger projects are needed Made in Denmark rather than airy plans and desk exercises, if we are to be the green showcase for the whole world again that we have promised each other.
